533104|2026-03.headline: Globus Spirits FY26 P&A revenue rose 27% to INR164 crores, while Q4 manufacturing EBITDA was INR8.3/litre and the company dropped its equity raise.
533104|2026-03.overview: Globus Spirits closed FY26 with installed capacity of 334 million litres after the UP distillery commissioning, at 80% utilisation (adjusted for UP start-up). Manufacturing EBITDA was INR6.2/litre for FY26 and INR8.3/litre in Q4, while Q4 volumes dipped on an ENA shift and a one-time inventory build-up that management expects to clear in Q1. Consumer P&A grew 27% for the year (58% excluding Delhi), but Q4 P&A EBITDA loss widened to INR5 crores, partly due to INR3-3.5 crores of label registration costs. Management said internal accruals and debt refinancing (annual debt outflow cut from INR67 crores to INR14 crores for FY27) mean there is no immediate need for the equity raise.

financial_highlights.change: Q4 later stated as INR6.3 in Q&A

segments.name: Manufacturing (bulk alcohol: ENA, ethanol, exports)
segments.commentary: FY26 bulk sales about 199.5 million litres, roughly 70:30 ethanol to ENA, with guidance of more than 20 crore litres in FY27 plus UP volumes (about 2 crore litres). Q4 exports started at 3.7 million litres; Q4 volume dipped on ENA shift and inventory build-up.

segments.name: Prestige & Above (P&A)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR164 crores (+27%), volume 1.19 million cases; 5 core markets with 4 profitable; Delhi share fell to 23% of volume after a Q3 disruption, and Delhi recovered to 90% of Q4 FY25 volume.

segments.name: Regular & Others (R&O)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR900 crores and 15.7 million cases; Q4 EBITDA margin about 18%, which management expects to ease to 16-18% range as UP grows. Rajasthan plus UP volume grew 7% in FY26, with other markets degrowing.

guidance_outlook: Manufacturing EBITDA guided at INR5-7 per litre for FY27, same as FY26 range, regardless of ENA or ethanol mix.
Bulk sales target above 20 crore litres for FY27 excluding UP; UP expected to add about 2 crore litres.
FY27 interest cost expected around INR14-15 crores per quarter after UP capitalisation ended; refinancing saves about INR50 crores in FY27 with debt outflow of INR14 crores.
Equity fundraise put on hold; FY27 expansion to be funded from internal accruals, with the enabling resolution still valid.
R&O Rajasthan plus UP volume growth expected above 7% in FY27; Q1 to see West Bengal volume (marginal) and inventory liquidation.
FY29 targets reaffirmed: P&A revenue around INR500 crores with about 50% growth, and presence in at least 8 more states.
Maintenance capex INR40-50 crores per year, plus INR20-30 crores for malt whiskey ageing and bottling, INR60-80 crores total for a few years.
capex_capacity: Installed capacity 334 million litres per annum after the UP distillery commissioning in the prior quarter; 6 distilleries across North and East India.
FY26 capacity utilisation 80% (adjusted for UP start-up), within the 80-85% annual guidance.
Eastern plants shifting from rice to maize derate capacity by 75 KL per day per plant when run fully on maize.
Facilities in Haryana, Bihar and UP geared for large-scale ENA exports.
Capex: maintenance INR40-50 crores, plus INR20-30 crores for whiskey ageing and bottling, INR60-80 crores sustained for a few years.
demand_pricing: Delhi volumes in Q3 FY26 fell to 60% of Q3 FY25; Q4 recovered to 90%. Management says the Delhi P&A business grew 58% ex-Delhi in FY26.
P&A realisation impacted by mix; management said price/mix contributed about 3% of growth.
Rajasthan price increase of INR30 per case replicated for FY27; no price increase yet in UP or Haryana.
ENA carries a lower realisation than ethanol, which lowered Q4 revenue; management says this is market structure, not a pricing issue.
Scotch import tariff cut expected to offset part of raw material and packaging cost inflation from the Middle East situation.
Management expects ethanol blending demand to grow strongly and flex-fuel mandates to add demand.
Global ENA supply constraints from high energy costs are creating export opportunities.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company giving a P&A growth target for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is committed to the FY29 target of about 50% growth in P&A but will not give piecemeal annual guidance; the FY29 P&A figure is INR500 crores, not INR1,000 crores.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 P&A EBITDA loss widen to INR5 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR3-3.5 crores of label registration costs were paid for new brand launches timed for Jan-Feb, plus investment in East expansion and Jharkhand; core markets are described as 4 of 5 profitable.

qa_highlights.question: Why did R&O growth slow and how much did Delhi affect it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give Delhi case numbers; UP and Rajasthan together grew 7% in volume, while Delhi, West Bengal and Haryana drove flat overall volume. Delhi R&O is paused until policy stabilises.

qa_highlights.question: What is the interest cost trajectory after Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 interest rose about INR3 crores because UP term loan interest stopped being capitalised; guided INR14-15 crores per quarter going forward.

qa_highlights.question: What are the net debt and working capital levels?
qa_highlights.answer: Net debt is INR627 crores at Q4 exit; R&O working capital is 5-6 days and expected to rise slightly from Q1.

qa_highlights.question: How does the company plan to expand into new states?
qa_highlights.answer: Expansion may use third-party manufacturing (e.g., Assam) or captive units depending on efficiency; 8 new states is the minimum baked into the FY29 plan.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company disclose realisation per case or UP volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not release realisation per case by category or separate UP volumes currently; it will consider disclosure internally.

risks_watch: Q1 FY27 volume recovery depends on clearing the Q4 ENA inventory build-up and state permission cycles.
Input cost inflation (PET, packaging, freight, fuel) tied to the Middle East situation; management says the impact is modest but has not quantified it.
Delhi R&O policy remains unstable and paused; West Bengal relaunch depends on licence transfer timing.
R&O margin expected to fall from 18% toward 16-18% as UP (lower-margin) grows.
P&A losses are volatile quarter to quarter; the FY29 targets rely on emerging markets moving to core.
Bihar prohibition reversal is a potential upside but timing is uncertain.
Management did not give separate UP numbers or realisation per case, limiting visibility.
533104|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on the long-term plan and the UP and Bihar opportunity, but cautious on near-term quarterly P&A losses and Delhi, which management declined to quantify. Management was evasive on Delhi R&O numbers and realisation per case, and it corrected several analyst assumptions (P&A target, Q4 margin).
key_quotes: We are in no immediate pressure to dilute equity at this stage.
Our revised business plan demonstrates a cash flow trajectory that is stronger than was initially projected around Q2 or Q3 of last year, allowing us to self-fund our current growth initiatives.
INR5 to INR7 is our guidance for the EBITDA per liter. That's the range in which it will remain for the year.
Delhi volumes in Q3 FY26 dropped drastically to 60% of the Q3 FY25 volumes.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Manufacturing EBITDA is guided at INR5-7/litre for FY27, flat to FY26's INR6.2, and Q4 was INR8.3/litre; R&O margin is expected to ease from about 18% to 16-18% as lower-margin UP grows, offset by a Scotch import tariff cut and P&A losses that are volatile.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Installed capacity is 334 million litres after UP commissioning, utilisation was 80% for FY26 (adjusted for UP start-up), and FY27 expansion is to be funded from internal accruals with the enabling resolution still valid, so new capacity is planned but no dated new plant was given beyond UP, new-state expansion (possibly via third-party manufacturing such as Assam) and the FY29 plan of at least 8

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Bulk volume guided to well over 20 crore litres (ex-UP) in FY27, FY26 P&A volume grew 31% to 1.19 million cases, and Rajasthan plus UP volume is expected to grow above 7%; Q1 volume depends on clearing the ENA inventory build-up.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation of 80% sits at the bottom edge of the 80-85% guided range, and management is funding FY27 expansion from internal accruals; capex guided at INR60-80 crores sustained for a few years, but no specific new project was announced.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Bulk volume is guided to well over 20 crore litres plus about 2 crore litres from UP, ethanol blending demand is expected to grow strongly, and global ENA supply constraints are opening export opportunities (Q4 exports started at 3.7 million litres).

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q4 volumes dipped on ENA shift and inventory build-up that management expects to clear in Q1, Delhi R&O is paused, and input cost inflation from the Middle East situation is unquantified; Q4 P&A EBITDA loss widened to INR5 crores.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.when: Q4 FY26 to Q1 FY27 (new brands launched for Jan-Feb)
rows.why: About INR3-3.5 crores of label registration costs were paid for new brand launches timed for Jan-Feb, and the company is investing in the East expansion and Jharkhand, though no specific product names were given.

rows.label: Rajasthan INR30/case price increase replicated for FY27; no increase yet in UP o
rows.why: The Rajasthan INR30 per case increase is already in place for FY27, while price/mix contributed about 3% of P&A growth in FY26.

rows.label: Annual debt outflow cut to INR14 crores and interest saving of about INR50 crore
rows.why: Refinancing has cut the annual debt outflow from INR67 crores to INR14 crores, saving about INR50 crores, with net debt at INR627 crores and interest coverage up to 3.14x from 1.76x.

rows.label: Bihar prohibition reversal and expansion into 8+ new states by FY29
rows.why: Eight new states is the minimum in the FY29 plan, with third-party manufacturing or captive units to be used depending on efficiency, but Bihar reversal timing is uncertain.

tone.note: Management was confident on the FY29 P&A target, UP and Bihar opportunity and debt reduction, but cautious on quarterly P&A losses and Delhi; analysts pushed on P&A growth targets, Q4 margin and Delhi R&O numbers, and management declined to give Delhi figures or realisation per case.

533104|2026-06.headline: Globus Spirits Q1 FY27 revenue rose 13% to INR7,888 million, EBITDA up 33% to INR795 million, PAT up 49% to INR276 million (corrected figures).
533104|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 showed strong growth across manufacturing and consumer, with EBITDA margin of about 10% and PAT margin of about 4%. Manufacturing (ENA/ethanol) volumes reached 56.11 million litres at a record 89% utilisation, with EBITDA of about INR6.5 per litre within the INR5-7 guidance band. Prestige and above (P&A) revenue grew 35% YoY to INR550 million but still posted negative EBITDA of INR13 million, while Regular and Others (R&O) grew 10% with UP volumes scaling rapidly. Management flagged glass and PET cost-push of 10-17% and seasonal agri inflation in Q2, but said it is hedged within the margin band. Net debt was INR650 crore versus INR660 crore in March 2026. Several figures were corrected during the call: revenue should read INR7,888 million, PAT INR276 million and growth 49%, and EBITDA per litre INR6.5.

financial_highlights.value: INR7,888 million (corrected from INR7,887 million stated on call)
INR276 million (corrected from INR278 million stated on call)
INR6.5 (corrected from INR6.6 stated on call)

segments.name: Manufacturing (ENA/ethanol)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 11% YoY to INR4,720 million on 56.11 million litres sold, with 89% capacity utilisation on about 334 million litres installed capacity. EBITDA was about INR6.5 per litre, within the INR5-7 guidance band.

segments.name: Prestige and above (P&A)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 35% YoY and 38% QoQ to INR550 million, with volumes up 45% YoY to 0.42 million cases. EBITDA was negative INR13 million as spending went into distribution and brand building; brands cited were Terai, Snoski and Brothers & Co.

segments.name: Regular and Others (R&O)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 10% YoY to INR2,564 million, volumes up 13% YoY to 4.48 million cases and EBITDA up 13% YoY to INR440 million. UP R&O volumes grew 2.4x YoY and crossed 0.2 million cases per month.

guidance_outlook: Manufacturing EBITDA guided at INR5-7 per litre; management expects to stay in this range for all quarters of FY27.
R&O EBITDA margin guidance of 15-17%, with mix from lower-margin UP expected to pull margins toward 15-16% from the 17-18% of recent years.
Maintenance capex of about INR50-60 crore a year; no new ENA/ethanol capacity planned, with at most about 1% gain from technology. No capacity expansion planned through FY29.
P&A expected to reach profitability sooner rather than later, having moved from about negative 60% margin a couple of years ago to near breakeven.
Management expects the UK FTA to benefit the industry on Scotch costs, but said the timing and size of the benefit are uncertain and not yet visible in numbers.
West Bengal R&O re-entry expected within about 60 days of regulatory approvals, which management hopes come this quarter.
capex_capacity: Installed manufacturing capacity is about 334 million litres; Q1 utilisation was 89% against a guidance of about 85%.
UP plant utilisation was above 90% in Q1 per the CFO. About 25% of UP output is consumed captively and the rest sold in bulk, with optimisation still under way.
Capex has been limited to maintenance after UP commissioning; cash generation is being fed into P&A growth and debt paydown.
Management expects a 15-17% R&O margin band to hold while UP grows fast.
demand_pricing: Management expects ethanol demand for E20 blending to grow about 7-7.5% a year, in line with petrol growth; E85/E50 depends on car compatibility, which is limited for now.
Industry ethanol is in oversupply, but Globus ran at 89% by shifting ENA and ethanol mix and selling ENA in India and overseas, with overseas prices firming.
Glass and PET cost-push is 10-17% depending on brand and pack and is expected to persist; management says the company holds only slim packaging inventory.
Agri inflation is seasonal: Q2 and part of Q3 are inflationary, then prices ease as harvests arrive. Maize is partly hedged and FCI supplies a fixed-price portion; broken rice is unhedged.
UP is a large market of about 95 lakh cases a month. West Bengal IMIL is about 26-27 lakh cases a month, per management, slightly smaller than Rajasthan or Haryana.
Management says the company has 11 states total presence, with 4 core states plus Delhi and UP (5 core states overall), and a 6th state nearing core status.

qa_highlights.question: How will ethanol demand drivers develop given the E20 controversy, and could ethanol for cooking matter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said E20 is government policy, the controversy has not hurt offtake, and demand is growing about 7.5% YoY with sticky month-on-month volumes. Cooking-fuel ethanol adoption will be slow in India without distribution and canisters.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company expecting Bihar prohibition to be lifted?
qa_highlights.answer: Management believes prohibition in Bihar will eventually be reversed, but gave no firm timeline, estimating a change over about 1-2 years under the new Chief Minister.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of glass cost inflation on R&O and P&A?
qa_highlights.answer: Glass and PET cost-push is 10-17% by brand and pack and is expected to persist for some time, with energy costs also rising.

qa_highlights.question: Will UK FTA lower Scotch costs and expand gross profit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects a tailwind as inventory transitions, but benefits depend on suppliers revising base prices. Rupee depreciation of about 20% against the pound limits the net impact, and the company is not a market maker on Scotch prices.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of R&O in West Bengal and how is the market structured?
qa_highlights.answer: Regulatory approvals are the last step and are expected this quarter; the company would return to the market about 60 days later. Management does not see the market turning unfavourable.

qa_highlights.question: How much growth can be achieved without capex, and at what utilisation is new capex needed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management has no plans for new ENA/ethanol capex beyond maintenance of INR50-60 crore a year; utilisation guidance is about 85%. Capacity is seen flat through FY29.

qa_highlights.question: What are the net debt and manufacturing margin trends?
qa_highlights.answer: Net debt was INR650 crore against INR660 crore in March 2026. Manufacturing margin is within INR5-7 per litre and management is not concerned about changes in that range.

qa_highlights.question: Why does the IMFL brand mix shift across states, with some brands rising and others falling?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said brand growth varies by state because category mix differs (vodka, semi-premium and deluxe whisky markets). It said no brand is structurally declining and this will continue as the company enters new geographies.

qa_highlights.question: What is the UP ramp-up path and what is the margin outlook for R&O?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to quantify quarterly UP additions but said UP is the next big bankable R&O opportunity, with a FY29 guideline already set.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company balance volume growth, input inflation and shareholder returns?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said manufacturing margin is protected by FCI fixed-price supply, maize hedging, and monthly pass-through in the flexi-price E&A business. P&A is self-funded from cash flow, with no further capacity expansion planned.

risks_watch: Glass and PET cost-push of 10-17% may squeeze R&O margins if pass-through lags.
Q2 agri inflation for broken rice (unhedged) and maize, plus the eastern India rainfall deficit.

Ethanol overcapacity in the industry and policy ambiguity around E20 and higher blends.

533104|2026-09.headline: Globus Spirits Q2 FY27 EBITDA rose 2% YoY to INR63.8 crores; manufacturing EBITDA fell to INR4.6/litre, with INR5-7/litre guidance maintained.
533104|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue was INR758 crores (up 15% YoY) and EBITDA INR63.8 crores (up 2% YoY), while H1 EBITDA rose 17% to INR143.3 crores. Manufacturing EBITDA per litre dropped to INR4.6 on seasonal grain and fuel inflation and plant maintenance, with H1 at INR5.59 and trailing 12 months at about INR6.6. Management kept the INR5-7 per litre annual manufacturing guidance, citing the 2026-27 ethanol year and lower broken-rice and maize prices. The INR200 crore QIP was completed, with about INR155 crores used to repay debt and debt-to-EBITDA falling from 2.63x to about 2x.

financial_highlights.value: INR4.6/litre (EBITDA INR25.4 crores on 55.26 million litres)
financial_highlights.change: H1 INR5.59/litre; trailing 12 months about INR6.6/litre
vs INR270 crores in H1 FY26; driven by higher trade receivables
Hit by additional UP depreciation and a one-time deferred tax benefit in Q2 FY26

segments.name: Manufacturing (ENA/ethanol)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR455 crores on 55.26 million litres with EBITDA INR25.4 crores (INR4.6/litre), hit by grain and fuel costs and plant maintenance. Management guides INR5-7/litre annually and expects higher utilisation in the 2026-27 ethanol year.

segments.name: Prestige & Above (P&A)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR59.9 crores (+54% YoY, +9% QoQ) on 0.46 million cases (+64% YoY); EBITDA loss narrowed to INR0.2 crores. H1 revenue about INR114.9 crores on about 0.88 million cases; 5 of 12 footprint states are profitable.

segments.name: Regular & Others (R&O)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR242.8 crores (+14% YoY) on 4.24 million cases (+16% YoY); EBITDA INR38.6 crores (+4% YoY), a margin moderation vs Q1 on lower sequential volume. H1 revenue about INR499.2 crores and EBITDA INR82.6 crores; growth is mainly from UP.

guidance_outlook: Manufacturing EBITDA guidance of INR5-7 per litre maintained on an annual basis; H1 was below range, and management hopes for higher H2 realisations as maize and rice prices cool after Diwali.
R&O EBITDA margin guidance of 16-18% reiterated; a separate comment cited a range of 15-18%.
Interest savings of about INR6 crores in H2 FY27 (INR11-12 crores annualised) from debt repayment and refinancing.
P&A next phase: 5 additional duty-free channels and entry into 2 new states in FY27; CSG entry targeted in Q3 subject to approvals.
Management expects higher capacity utilisation in the 2026-27 ethanol year (from November) as sugar-based ethanol supply falls; it does not expect to raise the per-litre margin guidance.
Management plans to re-enter West Bengal in FY28 and is re-evaluating Delhi plans given weak industry volumes; West Bengal sales are currently zero.
capex_capacity: Manufacturing capacity of about 20-25 crore litres annually; utilisation has been 80-85%, expected to rise meaningfully in the coming year.
UP distilleries are not yet at full utilisation; UP utilisation has risen in the last 3-4 months as UP shifts from molasses-based to grain-based country liquor.
Rajasthan has headroom of about 400,000-500,000 cases a month, subject to a state ceiling; no plans to expand Rajasthan capacity, with capital focused on consumer business.
Behror unit is largely for internal consumption and was excluded from the discussion.
QIP of INR200 crores completed; about INR150-155 crores used for debt repayment and the balance held as liquid funds, which may fund bottling and whisky-related expansion.
demand_pricing: Management expects about 900 crore litres of grain-based ethanol demand from OMCs, with chemical use of 100-150 crore litres and beverage use of 300-400 crore litres.
Maize-based ethanol was about 60% of H1 ethanol sales; management says it could fall to about 30% as the product mix shifts with profitability.
September-end grain prices were about INR27-28/kg for rice and INR23-24/kg for maize, versus INR24-25 and INR21-22 at end-Q1; these are end-period, not average, prices.
Management expects broken rice supply to rise as FCI moves to 10% broken content from 25%, which should keep rice prices subdued.
Power and fuel cost was INR6.3/kg in Q2, up 10-11% QoQ, totalling about INR60.43 crores for the quarter.
Rajasthan R&O grows low-to-mid single-digit volume plus 4-6% annual price increases; Globus holds about 50% of the private 60% of the market.
Management said packaging material inflation linked to oil prices was an unusual headwind this year.
ENA export volume was about 5 million litres in H1; exports are not tracked as a separate business.

qa_highlights.question: Can the INR5-7/litre manufacturing guidance hold after the INR3/litre cut in maize-based ethanol prices?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said maize prices should stay lower, citing FCI rice allocation clarity and more broken rice; the ENA and ethanol flexibility keeps the guidance intact. It acknowledged Q2 at 4.6-4.7/litre.

qa_highlights.question: Why did R&O EBITDA fall in Q2, and how much did UP contribute?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to commodity cycle timing, with Q2 the peak of raw material and fuel inflation. Rajasthan grows mid-single digits in volume; almost all incremental R&O growth came from UP.

qa_highlights.question: Will UP margins converge with Rajasthan, and is the R&O margin range changing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated a 16-18% R&O EBITDA margin range; Rajasthan sits at the higher end and UP at the lower end, with UP improving as scale builds.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plan for the INR200 crore QIP proceeds?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR150 crores repaid debt and the balance is liquid, to fund IMFL growth, bottling and whisky expansion.

qa_highlights.question: How will the end of sugar-based ethanol affect volumes and ENA prices?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects much higher volumes in the Nov-Oct ethanol year and sees a large capacity base in India, so it will not raise per-litre margin guidance. Long-term offtake covers all units except Bihar.

qa_highlights.question: Will P&A reach breakeven, and what is the growth-versus-profit trade-off?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it would prioritise growth over profit while the balance sheet and cash flows allow, with profitability to follow as spending is pulled back.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for Delhi, West Bengal and Haryana?
qa_highlights.answer: Delhi allocation rose but industry sales are weak, so plans are being re-evaluated. West Bengal is zero now with re-entry planned in FY28; Haryana contributes but is growing slowly.

risks_watch: Manufacturing margin pressure in H1 (INR4.6/litre in Q2) from grain, fuel and packaging inflation; H2 recovery depends on maize and rice prices cooling after Diwali.
Maize-based ethanol profitability after the INR3/litre price cut; the product mix may shift toward FCI rice and broken rice.
Possible industry-wide shift into ENA that could pressure ENA prices, though management believes state-level logistics limit this.
P&A remains loss-making (EBITDA loss INR0.2 crores); growth is being prioritised over profit.
Operating cash flow fell to INR139 crores from INR270 crores as receivables rose; monitor working capital.
Delhi market compression and West Bengal absence; watch whether UP growth can offset them.
Rajasthan capacity ceiling, with about 400,000-500,000 cases a month of headroom.
Sustainability of the 16-18% R&O margin as UP mix rises, and the 15-18% range management cited elsewhere.
533104|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on the medium-term manufacturing guidance and the balance sheet, though the Q2 margin dip was explained away as seasonal. Management was evasive on specifics such as state-wise UP sizing, ENA realisations and outlet-level shelf data, and deferred several questions to follow-up calls.
key_quotes: The manufacturing business is sort of steady at that range, 5% to 7% with a 20 crores to 25 crores litre kind of capacity, kind of sale annually.
So it's a conscious decision to chase growth given the strength of the balance sheet and the strength of our cash flows.
I would not look at the revenue of the company as a sort of homogeneous number.

533106|2026-03.headline: Oil India FY26: consolidated income Rs 38,981 cr (+3% YoY), PAT Rs 7,551 cr (+7%), with Rs 11.5/share dividend repeated.
533106|2026-03.overview: Oil India's annual investors' meet (25 May 2026, transcript filed 29 May) covered FY26 results, a record 74-well drilling year and a 1.6x GRM uplift at subsidiary NRL. Consolidated EBITDA was Rs 13,498 cr (+5%) and PAT Rs 7,551 cr (+7%) despite crude realisation falling to $69/bbl from $78. Production was 6.64 MMtoe, with about 0.1 MMt lost to a 10-15 day economic blockade. Management reiterated the 9 MMTPA NRL expansion by March 2027, a roughly 100-well-a-year drilling plan, and offshore exploration reliant on the Samudra Manthan Mission for deep-water wells.

financial_highlights.change: ~60% drilling, ~25% capital projects, ~13% investments in subsidiaries/JVs
Down from $78; lowest in last 5 years

segments.name: Upstream (Oil India)
segments.commentary: Production 6.64 MMtoe (3.45 MMt oil, 3.15 BCM gas); daily crude peaked at ~81,354 bpd, with management citing 82,200+ bpd as of late May. Record 74 wells drilled (22 exploration, 52 development) and 307 workovers. 2P reserve replacement ratio 1.20 (vs 0.94) on 231 MMt reserves, 31-year reserve life.

segments.name: Midstream (pipelines)
segments.commentary: Numaligarh-Siliguri product pipeline expanded from 1.72 to 5.5 MMTPA, completed at Rs 750 crore vs Rs 860 crore approved outlay; PM inaugurated 13 March 2026. Duliajan-Numaligarh gas pipeline expanded from 1.2 to 2.5 MMSCMD, mechanically complete, awaiting a ~7-day NRL shutdown to commission.

segments.name: Downstream (NRL, 100% subsidiary of Oil India Ltd, 3 MMTPA)
segments.commentary: Record 103% crude throughput, 99.1% availability, 87.25% distillate yield and 727 TMT MS output; GRM 1.6x prior year. Navratna status conferred Dec 2025. Expansion to 9 MMTPA targeted for March 2027, with polypropylene unit on track; expansion capex ~Rs 46,000 crore including ~Rs 7,200 crore for PPU.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Mozambique force majeure lifted Nov 2025; two LNG trains of 13 MMTPA targeted for end-2028 or early 2029, with ~$1.8 billion committed and ~$300 million cost escalation pending CCEA approval. Russian assets (Taas, Vankor) have returned ~$1 billion in dividends. Libya 95/96 major commercial discovery.

segments.name: New energy and others
segments.commentary: Oil India Green Energy Ltd (wholly-owned) has ~2 GW renewable capacity in JVs pipeline and 2 CBG plants under construction, with 2 more awarded or in tender, against a target of 25 by 2030. 49 KTPA bamboo 2G ethanol plant inaugurated Sept 2025; NRL green hydrogen plant of 2.4 KTPA (Rs 138 crore) due by end-2026.

guidance_outlook: Production: 4 MMtoe achievable with ~100 wells drilled per year; long-term target 12 MMtoe by 2030 (from 10).
Gas: 3.35 BCM guided for FY27; ~5 BCM targeted by FY28 once Duliajan feeder line and DNPL expansion are commissioned.
NRL: CDU/VDU ~mid-July 2026 (~400 TMT output after that, mostly diesel), DHDT about a month later, PFCC/RPTU by Dec-Jan, full 9 MMTPA by March 2027 (stabilised by March 2028).
Capex: rollover of ~Rs 10,000 crore a year for ~100 onshore wells per year, plus shallow-water offshore drilling.

Offshore: deep-water well targeted for spud around June 2027; four-plus-four deep-water wells at ~Rs 1,200 crore each (Rs 4,800-5,000 crore), contingent on Samudra Manthan Mission sponsorship. Shallow-water wells ~Rs 800 crore each.
NRL excise duty: ~Rs 3,000 crore accrued in FY26, with 50% NE excise benefit and no sunset clause at 9 MMTPA; management expects calibration if FOB HSD prices fall.
capex_capacity: Drilling: 74 wells in FY26 (record); released drillable location inventory ~218 vs ~45 earlier; average Assam shelf depth ~4,300 m.

demand_pricing: Realisation: crude at $69/bbl in FY26, lowest in 5 years; government moves on royalty and post-wellhead cost realisation cited as cash-flow support.

Gas to NE CGD: ~50,000 SCMD allocated to NE Gas Distribution and Purbabharati Gas Distribution as NRL reseller.
Product demand: management cites 7-8% growth in refined product consumption; NRL export via Indo-Bangladesh pipeline optional, not the basis for 9 MMTPA.
Competition/partners: TotalEnergies signed technology service agreement (Nov 2025) for offshore seismic and exploration support, with a say in investment decisions.

qa_highlights.question: What is the offshore exploration capex and how will the capability gap be addressed?

qa_highlights.question: NRL excise duty benefit in FY26 and impact of recent duty cut?
qa_highlights.answer: ~Rs 3,000 crore accrued in FY26; no sunset clause on 50% NE excise benefit at 9 MMTPA. Management expects excise to be recalibrated against HSD FOB prices if they fall.

qa_highlights.question: NRL 9 MMTPA viability, and terms of the TotalEnergies arrangement?
qa_highlights.answer: Viability rests on domestic demand (7-8% growth) and NE/mainland logistics, with Panchgram, Singimari and Jogighopa depots and Siliguri tankage. TotalEnergies is a service agreement, with Total able to weigh in on investment decisions.

qa_highlights.question: NRL timelines, first product output, and capex spent/remaining?

qa_highlights.question: FY27 production, gas and capex outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: 4 MMT with 100 wells; gas 3.35 BCM in FY27 and ~5 BCM 18 months out. Rollover capex ~Rs 10,000 crore per year.

qa_highlights.question: Current production exit rate and gas ramp path?

qa_highlights.question: Mozambique incremental equity outflow?

533106|2026-06.headline: Oil India Q1 FY27 standalone PAT rose to INR2,870 crore from INR813 crore, on record EBITDA of INR4,605 crore and crude realisation of USD98.73/bbl.
533106|2026-06.overview: Standalone operating revenue hit a record INR7,958 crore and EBITDA a record INR4,605 crore, with margin above 54%. Crude output was 0.95 MMT, up 11%+ YoY, and daily output peaked at 10,921 MT on 27 June, later 11,017 MT on 3 August. Subsidiary NRL ran at 105% capacity utilisation with a GRM of USD35.95/bbl (about USD33 ex-inventory gain), and consolidated PAT was INR4,026 crore. Management guided to roughly 1 MMT crude per quarter and about 3.9–4 MMT for FY27, and gas evacuation hinges on DNPL/IGGL connectivity.

segments.name: Upstream (standalone crude and gas)
segments.commentary: Q1 FY27 production was 1.707 MMBoE, with crude at 0.95 MMT (+11%+ YoY) and gas up 0.4% QoQ. Gas off-take has been constrained at about 2.93 BCM by evacuation limits, and management targets 3.8 BCM next year and about 5 BCM by FY29.

segments.name: NRL (refining, material subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Capacity utilisation was 105%, distillate yield 87%, and GRM USD35.95/bbl vs USD5.02 a year earlier. Management said about USD2 of the GRM was inventory gain, and OMC discounts under SAED were netted off.

guidance_outlook: Crude production: about 1 MMT per quarter from now on, roughly 3.9 MMT for FY27 with a possible touch of 4 MMT; FY29 target of about 4.2 MMT from main producing areas, with upside from near-field exploration.
Capex: FY27 budget is INR8,600 crore (to be revised at the next review); Q1 spend was about INR3,050 crore, including INR1,230 crore on exploratory drilling.
Wells: FY27 target of 100 wells (42 exploratory, 57 development), up from 74 in FY26; a further 10% rise is intended for FY28.

NRL: CDU/VDU, DHDT and SRU to be commissioned by Oct–Nov 2026, remaining units by 31 March 2027, reaching about 75% of 9 MMT rated capacity by Q4 FY28; Paradip–Numaligarh pipeline mechanical completion targeted October and commissioning by December 2026.
Gas: 200 m connection within the NRL campus (2–3 months) to link DNPL with IGGL; DFL feeder line about 20% complete; big jump in evacuation expected from Q1 FY28 and about 5 BCM by FY29.
GST on royalty: about INR2,500 crore (excluding interest) is already provided; payment to be made, with no prospective interest. The Assam land tax is a contingent liability with no P&L impact.
capex_capacity: Q1 FY27 capex about INR3,050 crore: survey INR450 crore, exploratory drilling INR1,230 crore, development drilling INR700 crore, capital equipment and projects INR350 crore, subsidiaries/JVs/overseas INR350 crore. FY26 actual capex was INR13,026 crore.
Wells drilled in Q1: 17 (7 exploratory, 10 development). Drilling history: FY25 22 exploratory and 35 development; FY26 22 exploratory and 52 development.

Andaman: Vijayapuram-1 spend about INR1,000–1,050 crore; hydro-frac testing in August; fourth Andaman well by a jack-up rig targeted for December 2026; 600 sq km of new 3D seismic to be processed by October.

Deep water (Mahanadi and KG): 4,200 line km and 5,300 sq km of 3D acquired; first deep-water rig expected June–July 2027, second by March 2028. Government reimbursement of up to INR675 crore per well is proposed under the Samudra Manthan scheme.

NRL expansion: about INR30,000 crore spent to date, with INR34,000–35,000 crore expected for the refinery project and another INR7,200–7,300 crore for the PPU project. NRL debt is about INR19,000 crore.
demand_pricing: Crude realisation was USD98.73/bbl and gas USD7.19/MMBtu; new-well gas is priced outside APM, and incremental volumes will all be new-well gas.

NRL's GRM is about USD33 excluding the roughly USD2 inventory gain. Diesel and petrol discounts to OMCs under SAED ran at INR13/l to INR3/l for petrol and INR10/l to nil for diesel during the quarter, and have reappeared as a monthly recalibration.

Gas off-take from BCPL is stable at about 1.25–1.35 MMSCMD (about 4.25 MMSCMD returned to the grid by Oil India). NEEPCO is cutting gas use in favour of hydro, and excise benefit fell as government calibrated excise to hold retail prices.
NRL operating cost is about USD4.5–5/bbl, targeted to fall to about USD3.5/bbl as expansion units stabilise.

qa_highlights.question: What is the current crude run-rate, and can production sustain the 10,921 MT/day level?
qa_highlights.answer: Director Operations said the company expects about 1 MMT per quarter from here, citing workover, well intervention and optimisation; output reached 11,017 MT/day on 3 August.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline for gas ramp-up from 2.93 BCM to about 5 BCM?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY27 and H1 FY28 would be flat to slow; the big jump is expected from Q1 FY28 once the 200 m NRL link and DFL/IGGL are complete, with about 1.5 MMSCMD of extra headroom from DNPL capacity expansion and 3.5–4 MMSCMD of evacuation planned.

qa_highlights.question: What is the normalised NRL GRM, and what is the exploration capex outlook given the government support?
qa_highlights.answer: NRL GRM was about USD35 including about USD2 inventory gain (about USD33 ex-gain). Exploration: 100 wells targeted in FY27 and a 10%+ rise intended thereafter, with deep-water programme funded in part by government schemes.

qa_highlights.question: What is the NRL expansion status and the Paradip–Numaligarh pipeline timing?
qa_highlights.answer: CDU/VDU mechanically complete, with three units to be commissioned by Oct–Nov 2026 and the rest by 31 March 2027; pipeline ROU is secured except about 8 km, with commissioning by December 2026.

qa_highlights.question: What is the debt position across the group?
qa_highlights.answer: Standalone: USD1.4 bn loan for Mozambique. Singapore subsidiary: USD500 mn bond due May 2027. NRL: about INR19,000 crore. Total group debt about INR37,233 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why did contract costs rise, and what is the GST-on-royalty payment outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Contract cost rose by about INR146 crore QoQ to INR615 crore, mainly offshore G&G costs. About INR2,500 crore GST on royalty (excl. interest) is already provided, to be paid with no prospective interest; the Assam land tax is a contingent liability.

risks_watch: Gas evacuation remains the binding constraint: BCPL and NEEPCO off-take is seasonal and the DFL/IGGL and 200 m NRL link are still pending.
NRL's GRM is inflated by SAED-linked discounts and an inventory gain of about USD2/bbl; the normalised GRM is about USD33 and the discount level is calibrated monthly.
Andaman Vijayapuram-1 and -3 testing is still pending; a write-down or capitalised-cost review is possible after the September decision.
Assam land tax case is being withdrawn via the state legislature; the contingent liability is removed only once withdrawal is effective.
Q2 gas volumes could dip with monsoon and tea-garden seasonality from October; exploration cost (G&G) inflated opex in Q1.

We have always maintained that ramping up the production by itself is not a challenge. Absense of the network is a challenge which we are trying to address and once the network is laid, it is ready for evacuation, ramping up production will definitely happen.

533148|2026-03.headline: JSW Energy Q4 FY26 revenue rose 39% YoY to ₹4,851 crore and EBITDA 72% to ₹2,602 crore; FY26 EBITDA hit a record ₹11,041 crore.
533148|2026-03.overview: Installed capacity rose 2.6 GW in FY26 to 13.45 GW, with generation up 58% YoY, and Q4 net generation rose 48% YoY to 11.7 BU. Q4 PAT was ₹574 crore (up 38%) while PAT to shareholders was ₹308 crore, with depreciation up ~1.7x and interest up ~2.4x YoY as new assets capitalised. Management guided FY27 to be a year of accelerating earnings, with ~3 GW of RE additions and ~₹20,000 crore capex, and kept net debt/EBITDA at ~5.2x (ex-CWIP debt). Merchant realisations were ~20% above exchange prices in FY26, though exchange prices averaged ~₹3.86/unit.

segments.name: Renewables
segments.commentary: Q4 renewable generation rose 68% YoY on wind, solar, hydro and O2 Power additions; 118 MW organic RE added in Q4. Installed base is 13.45 GW after 2.6 GW added in FY26 (1.3 GW acquired, rest organic).

segments.name: Thermal
segments.commentary: Q4 thermal generation rose 43% YoY to 8.8 BU; portfolio PLF 78% in Q4 and 73% in FY26 versus national averages of 68.7% and 65.8%. KSK Mahanadi Q4 PLF 93%, FY26 KSK EBITDA above ₹3,300 crore; Utkal Q4 PLF 75%, Vijayanagar Q4 PLF 79%.

segments.name: Energy storage
segments.commentary: 5 GWh battery assembly facility in Pune commissioned in Q4 FY26 with commercial sales started; locked-in storage is 29.6 GWh (3.2 GWh BESS, 26.4 GWh pumped hydro).

guidance_outlook: FY27: ~3 GW of capacity additions (about 35-40% wind, rest solar/hybrid), split roughly evenly between H1 and H2; FY27 capex about ₹20,000 crore, of which ~₹4,000-5,000 crore for thermal and pumped storage.
FY28 RE additions guided at ~3-3.5 GW; thermal (KSK 1.8 GW) and partial Salboni capacity add to FY29-FY30.
KSK first 600 MW thermal unit expected by mid-FY28; Tidong 150 MW hydro: 50 MW commissioned 8 May 2026, balance two units before June 2026.
Curtailment expected to end by July 2026 when the Rajasthan evacuation line is commissioned.
Steady-state EBITDA for KSK base case ₹2,700 crore; management expects to beat it. Steady-state EBITDA for ~6 GW wind and solar about ₹75 lakh per MW per year.
New DSM regulations budgeted at 1.5-2% revenue impact on renewables without substation grouping.
Net debt/EBITDA target about 5-5.5x by 2030; FY30 targets of 30 GW generation and 40 GWh storage; locked-in capacity 32.1 GW.
Effective tax rate expected to move toward 23-24% as deferred tax benefits and MAT credit adjustments run through.
capex_capacity: Under construction: ~14 GW, all under long-term PPAs; CWIP ₹17,300 crore at FY26 end, of which ~₹11,200 crore RE.
Salboni thermal now 3,200 MW (two 1,600 MW PPAs); first 1,600 MW under construction with equipment procurement on schedule. GE Power boiler business acquisition expected to close within two quarters.
Pumped storage: Stage 1 forest clearance received; 36-month construction timeline; electro-mechanical ordering placed.
Blade manufacturing plant at Halol expected to commission in H1 FY27; Sany wind turbine contract for 2.4 GW fixed in price and currency with supplies started.
Pipeline of ~4.6 GW with Letters of Intent secured beyond the 14 GW under construction.
demand_pricing: Power demand grew 0.9% in FY26 (weakest in five years) and 2.2% in Q4; FY27 YTD demand up 4.6%. Peak demand 256 GW on 25 April 2026; system preparing for ~270 GW.

Utkal 400 MW 25-year PPA at ₹5.78/unit; 115 MW 2-year PPA with Assam discom from 1 April 2026. Open capacity now about 5% of installed base.
No new PPA signings expected for unsigned national capacity until evacuation eases, which management sees as 2029.

qa_highlights.question: Breakdown of FY27 RE additions and FY28 guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: About 3 GW in FY27, 35-40% wind and rest solar/hybrid; FY28 about 3-3.5 GW, with thermal and pumped storage adding from FY29-30.

qa_highlights.question: Is the KSK minority buyout amount crystallised, and what is the KSK PPA outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Not yet crystallised; number expected by end of Q2. KSK's last unit may be merchant for now, but the company prefers long-term PPAs and is talking to states.

qa_highlights.question: Is the ₹20,000 crore capex fundable from internal cash flows, and what is the CWIP breakup?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said internal cash flows and leverage limits can fund it; ₹1,800 crore warrants available as backup. Thermal and pumped storage get ₹4,000-5,000 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Mytrah EBITDA jump YoY?

qa_highlights.question: What are the DSM impact assumptions?

qa_highlights.question: What was the curtailment impact?
qa_highlights.answer: About ₹16 crore in Q4 and ~₹50 crore in FY26, from temporary-access assets in Rajasthan; the rest is under permanent recovery and paid.

qa_highlights.question: What was KSK merchant EBITDA in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: ₹203 crore from merchant sales in the quarter, disclosed in closing remarks.

rows.why: About ₹4,500 crore is short-term, and refinancing at operating-company level is needed, while the weighted cost of debt fell 67 bps to 8.36%.

rows.label: Pumped storage Stage 1 construction start
rows.why: Stage 1 forest clearance is received, electro-mechanical ordering is placed, and the 36-month timeline plus ₹4,000-5,000 crore thermal and pumped storage capex is funded for FY27.

tone.note: Management was confident on FY27 RE delivery, ~14 GW under construction and the 20% merchant premium, but evasive on the KSK buyout amount, BESS order book and merchant revenue split; analysts pushed on evacuation, DSM and curtailment.

533148|2026-06.headline: JSW Energy added 873 MW in Q1 FY27 (about 1.1 GW since April) and holds ₹12,880 crore cash, while net debt is about ₹55,000 crore and TTM net leverage is 4.95x.
533148|2026-06.overview: Revenue was flat YoY at ₹5,437 crore and EBITDA rose 2% to ₹3,103 crore, while PAT fell to ₹533 crore (₹471 crore attributable) on higher depreciation (+20% to ₹890 crore) and interest (+16% to ₹1,519 crore) from new capacity. Net generation fell 5% YoY to 12.9 BU, with hydro down about 26% on weak hydrology and thermal down 6%, partly offset by solar up 29%. Management reiterated FY27 targets of 3 GW capacity addition and ₹20,000 crore capex, and outlined a pumped storage pipeline, the Maruti Clean Coal acquisition, and a 600 MW Mahanadi unit 4 for FY28.

segments.name: Renewables (solar and wind)
segments.commentary: Solar generation rose 29% and wind 3% YoY, supported by 1,168 MW of added capacity; renewables are about 61% of the 14.6 GW installed base. Solar PLF was about 21-22% in Q1 and management expects a higher second half.

segments.name: Hydro
segments.commentary: Portfolio generation fell about 26% YoY on weak hydrology (Sutlej basin -39%, Ravi -24%, national -7%) despite Tidong and Kutehr additions. Karcham, Baspa and Kutehr were above 100% PLF in July.

segments.name: Thermal
segments.commentary: Thermal generation fell 6% YoY to 8 BU; Mahanadi lost about 184 MU (about 7%) due to a 17-day evacuation outage, which management says falls under force majeure. Thermal fleet is 5.7 GW, with open capacity under 4%.

segments.name: Battery storage (BESS) assembly
segments.commentary: The 5 GWh battery plant won a first large external order of about ₹440 crore; management guides to about $2.75-3/kWh margin, roughly $15 million a year and close to ₹150 crore EBITDA.

guidance_outlook: FY27 target of 3 GW capacity addition and ₹20,000 crore capex reaffirmed; about 1.1 GW already added since April, with about 225 MW more in July.
Net leverage to be below 5x by 2030; FY28 capacity addition guided to be in the same range (about 3 GW), with FY28 connectivity details promised soon.
Mahanadi unit 4 (600 MW) targeted for commissioning in FY28, taking the plant from 1.8 GW to 3.6 GW; capex expected to be 25-30% lower than greenfield.

Preferential promoter allotment balance of about ₹1,875 crore due before June 2027; management expects operating cash flow plus fundraise proceeds to cover about ₹12,000-12,500 crore of the ₹20,000 crore capex.
Bhavali (1,500 MW) and Kandhaura (1,680 MW; 1,500 MW PPA signed with UP) pumped storage projects; management expects significantly high-teen IRRs. Narihalla (Karnataka) PPA expected soon.
capex_capacity: Q1 FY27 commissioning of 873 MW, including 150 MW early commissioning of Tidong Hydro (originally October 2026) that added ₹20-22 crore EBITDA in Q1.

Connectivity: 300 MW under TGNA expected to convert to GNA before 31 August; 400 MW O2 Power (Rajasthan) connectivity now expected September-October. Management says the remaining 1.9 GW of FY27 additions is fully connected, with about 530 MW off-grid captive.

Salboni 2x800 MW: TG order placed with Toshiba JSW Power Systems, land fully acquired, site work underway. GE Durgapur boiler facility acquisition expected by end of Q1; nameplate 1.1 GW, targeted 1.6 GW after debottlenecking.
Halol (Gujarat) wind blade plant commissioned 8 June 2026 with 450 blades per year (about 600 MW of wind); Chitradurga plant expected by FY27.

Pumped storage readiness: Bhavali has environment clearance, land mostly acquired, L&T civil and Voith electromechanical orders placed; Kandhaura awaiting forest clearance and connectivity, with readiness expected in Q4 FY27.
demand_pricing: Q1 FY27 national power demand grew 8.5% YoY (July month-to-date about 12%); peak demand hit 271 GW in May, above FY26's 245 GW peak.
DAM prices averaged ₹5.10/unit in Q1 FY27 vs about ₹4.40 in Q1 FY26 (about 16% higher).
API4 coal index rose to $113 in Q1 FY27 from $90 in Q1 FY26 (about 25%); management says it is resilient through its shift to domestic coal.
Management said it is seeing buyer interest for 600 MW-scale thermal PPAs, citing imported-coal replacement demand.
Maruti Clean Coal & Power (300 MW Chhattisgarh): 195 MW net PPA with Rajasthan discoms (14-year residual life), about 64 MW merchant; acquisition agreement signed.

qa_highlights.question: How is the thermal fleet handling sub-technical-minimum operation during midday solar hours?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Mahanadi backdowns were minimal under merit order, Utkal minimum load stayed at or above 60%, and July PLF was above 85% with availability above 90%. Fixed costs are recovered during backdowns.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of boiler sourcing for Mahanadi unit 4 and Salboni?
qa_highlights.answer: Mahanadi unit 4 is about 30-40% complete with BoP ready; equipment is Chinese-sourced and under dispatch. Salboni TG is with TJPS; the GE Durgapur boiler facility (1.1 GW nameplate) is expected to be acquired by end-Q1 and debottlenecked to 1.6 GW.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin on the BESS external order?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided to about $2.75-3/kWh, roughly $15 million a year, or close to ₹150 crore EBITDA. It sees backward integration into cells as the next value-add step, with no long-term cell supplier yet.

qa_highlights.question: Are the 1.9 GW of remaining FY27 projects connected, and what about FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said all 1.9 GW is connected, including 530 MW off-grid captive. FY28 connectivity details will come later.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the lower thermal PLFs, especially at Utkal and Ratnagiri?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed Utkal's drop to a planned unit shutdown for annual availability in Q1, with availability above 91% in July. Ratnagiri's drop was a planned shutdown plus weaker June demand.

qa_highlights.question: Why is PAT under pressure and when will it improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said interest is higher during early years post-commissioning, and EBITDA-to-PBT conversion should improve as assets stabilise over 4-5 years.

risks_watch: Weak hydrology: Q1 hydro generation down about 26% YoY; monsoon recovery in July is the key check.
Curtailment: 69 MU of wind and solar curtailed in Q1 (about ₹15 crore revenue impact); 300 MW TGNA conversion by 31 August and 400 MW Rajasthan connectivity in September-October.
Project execution: pumped storage timelines, Mahanadi unit 4 (FY28), the GE boiler acquisition, and the Chitradurga blade plant by FY27.
Balance sheet: about ₹1,875 crore of promoter preferential money due before June 2027; gross debt about ₹74,000 crore, and FY28 funding needs still to be disclosed.
Mahanadi evacuation outage (17 days, about 184 MU) to be recognised under force majeure; the outcome is not yet confirmed.
533148|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and detailed, especially on capacity additions, connectivity and pumped storage returns. Management was more guarded on FY28 targets (deferred to a later update) and on PAT trajectory, which it attributed to depreciation and interest timing.

So we are absolutely confident of meeting the timelines in terms of the PPA timelines.
we are absolutely 100% secured from connectivity and which is all commissioned also.

rows.why: 873 MW commissioned in Q1 plus ~225 MW more in July, with 1.9 GW of remaining FY27 additions described as fully connected; 3 GW FY27 target reaffirmed and Mahanadi unit 4 (600 MW, 1.8 GW to 3.6 GW) targeted for FY28.

533148|2026-09.headline: JSW Energy Q2 FY27: revenue up 24% YoY to ₹6,658 crore and PAT attributable up 50% to ₹1,056 crore, with 1.4 GW commissioned since April.
533148|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue rose 24% YoY to ₹6,658 crore and EBITDA rose 23% to ₹3,907 crore, with net generation up 17% to 17.5 BU. Installed capacity crossed 15.1 GW after 513 MW of Q2 additions and the 300 MW Maruti Clean Coal acquisition (closed 6 August). Merchant realisation of ~₹6.9/unit was about 20% above the DAM average of ₹5.7/unit, supported by bilateral contracts. Management reaffirmed 2.5–3 GW annual RE additions and a 30 GW target for 2030, and said the Q3 merchant book is fully booked at similar or better prices.

financial_highlights.change: down ~51 bps from 8.79% a year ago

financial_highlights.metric: Net debt / TTM EBITDA (excluding CWIP debt)

segments.name: Thermal
segments.commentary: Consolidated thermal PLF 75% vs All-India 67.8%; generation 8.9 BU up 13% YoY including 321 MU from Maruti. Mahanadi ran at 90% PLF; Utkal at 82% PLF with plant EBITDA up over 3x YoY to ₹368 crore.

segments.name: Hydro
segments.commentary: Hydro generation 3,421 MU, up 13% YoY, against a national decline of ~15%. Kutehr generated ~408 MU at ~78% PLF; Tidong (commissioned Q1 FY27) generated 199 MU at 61% PLF; Karcham Wangtoo and Baspa at ~90% consolidated PLF.

segments.name: Renewables (wind and solar)
segments.commentary: Wind PLF 46% and solar PLF 19%; generation up 25% for wind and 36% for solar on ~1.5 GW YoY capacity increase. Q2 additions were 301 MW solar and 212 MW hybrid.

guidance_outlook: FY27 organic RE commissioning target of 3 GW (1.4 GW done since April, 1.6 GW remaining and described as fully on track); management says the 2.5–3 GW annual pace will hold each year.
FY27 capex about ₹20,000 crore; cash accrual about ₹6,500 crore plus ~₹7,150 crore equity from fundraising and JSW Steel share monetisation.
Operational capacity expected at about 16.7–16.8 GW by year-end FY27; 1 GWh of standalone BESS to be commissioned in FY27 (Rajasthan and Kerala, under ESAs).
KSK Mahanadi 1,200 MW expansion: 600 MW unit by FY28 and balance 1,200 MW by FY29; capex per MW guided at least 25–30% below industry average.
Salboni 3,200 MW (four 800 MW units): first unit expected by 2030; boilers ordered from the Durgapur facility.
Interest-rate sensitivity: management assumes ~30 bps increase in average cost of debt (to ~8.5%) if a further 75 bps rate hike occurs; new projects underwritten at 9% cost of debt over 25 years.
Q3 FY27 merchant volumes fully booked at similar or better than ₹6.9/unit; Q4 discussions under way.
Maruti Clean Coal acquisition: EV ₹1,410 crore, EBITDA and PAT accretive from day one; ₹45 crore EBITDA in 55 days of ownership.
capex_capacity: Installed capacity above 15.1 GW after 1.7 GW added since April (1.4 GW organic plus 300 MW Maruti); renewables about 61% of portfolio.
Locked-in pipeline toward 30 GW by 2030; 4 capacity categories beyond 2030 cited: C&I, group captive, pumped hydro (~26.4 GWh pipeline) and thermal.
C&I installed portfolio incl. group captive 3.7 GW (~25% of operating capacity), targeted at over 8.5 GW by 2030.
Halol wind blade facility producing since June; Chitradurga facility on track for completion in Q3 FY27.
Toshiba JSW stake raised to 10.7% in July; GE Power India boiler business acquisition received NCLT sanction on 1 October, closing expected soon.
Punatsangchhu-III (920 MW, Bhutan): DPR stage; project cost and timeline to be shared after details due by June 2027.
demand_pricing: Power demand grew ~11.1% YoY in Q2 FY27 (September +11.3%); October month-to-date growth 21.2%; peak demand touched 270 GW; monsoon ~13% below normal.
DAM prices averaged ₹5.7/unit in Q2; JSW merchant realisation ~₹6.9/unit (about 20% above DAM). Merchant volume 1.1 BU, about 7% of energy sold and about 4% of capacity (all thermal).
API4 imported coal averaged ~US$115/t in Q2, up ~28% YoY; company says domestic coal shift and job-work arrangements at imported-coal plants shielded it from the increase.

Curtailment was ~4.8% of generation in H1 vs national ~5.4%; Q2 curtailed ~225 MU with ~₹59 crore revenue impact. About 60% of curtailed capacity on temporary GNA to move to permanent GNA by end-Q3 FY27.
Group RTC demand expected to more than double to ~7 GW by 2032; 4.5 GW of 6.2 GW Group MoUs yet to be tied up, with 2 GW under advanced discussion.

qa_highlights.question: Are the Mahanadi expansion PPAs utility-type, given Chhattisgarh discom rules requiring in-state capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said new discom PPAs are expected, with the 5% free-power commitment to Chhattisgarh as the existing obligation. A part of the capacity may be kept for short-term merchant sale given low fuel cost near the mine; first unit FY28, balance two in FY29.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the sharp QoQ jump in Utkal EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 had outages and lower availability, limiting merchant sales; Q2 PLF was ~82% with long-term PPAs with Karnataka and Assam, and better merchant sales added to fixed-cost recovery.

qa_highlights.question: Tenure of the 25% fixed-rate debt?
qa_highlights.answer: About 15% is forex-linked and fully hedged for rates and FX, with tenor ~5–6 years; the rest is NCDs with ~4–5 years tenor.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 1 GWh BESS linked to PPA capacity or merchant?
qa_highlights.answer: All BESS in FY27 is under ESAs in Rajasthan and Kerala; these are standalone BESS with no solar investment. Separately, solar-plus-battery for evening-peak sales is planned, with evening connectivity applied about 8 months earlier.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 30 GW target fully PPA-backed, and what IRR threshold applies to group captive deals?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 30 GW plan contains only ~800 MW of Salboni Phase I, with the other ~2.4 GW beyond 2030; all under-construction RE is under PPA, including 2 GW of group captive under discussion. Minimum benchmark is mid-to-high-teen IRR.

qa_highlights.question: Is KSK 1,200 MW commissioning by FY29 realistic?
qa_highlights.answer: Equipment is already ordered, and balance-of-plant, coal and ash handling, rail and transmission for 3.6 GW are in place, so a ~3-year timeline is expected versus 4.5–5 years for greenfield.

qa_highlights.question: What is the interest-rate impact if rates rise 75 bps?
qa_highlights.answer: Only ~75% of the floating book is MCLR-linked; management assumes ~40 bps pass-through and ~30 bps effective increase, taking cost of debt to ≤8.5%. No impact on the 9%-underwritten new projects.

qa_highlights.question: Run-rate EBITDA and FY27 net debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not share run-rate EBITDA or forward guidance; it indicated a 16.7–16.8 GW base by year-end. FY27 equity funding visibility is ~₹13,150 crore (₹6,500 crore accruals plus ₹7,150 crore fundraising and share monetisation).

risks_watch: Interest-rate exposure: ~75% of term debt is floating, mostly MCLR-linked; management guides to ≤8.5% cost of debt in a further hike scenario.
Curtailment in Gujarat and Rajasthan corridor; ~225 MU lost in Q2 (₹59 crore). Permanent GNA for ~60% of the affected capacity due by end-Q3 FY27.
Merchant pricing sustainability: Q3 is booked at ~₹6.9/unit or better; Q4 still under negotiation. Evening-peak BESS economics depend on continued peak price spreads.
Execution: 1.6 GW of remaining FY27 RE additions; KSK 1,200 MW expansion by FY29; Salboni Phase I first unit by 2030.
Imported coal price pressure (API4 ~US$115/t, up ~28% YoY); company relies on domestic coal and job-work arrangements to offset.
Management declined to disclose run-rate EBITDA, and an analyst requested economics disclosure for new RE projects; watch for any change in disclosure.

More guarded on forward numbers: declined to give run-rate EBITDA, Bhutan project cost (awaiting June 2027 DPR) or merchant pricing beyond Q3, and deflected the Chhattisgarh PPA question toward "we will take a call at the right time."
key_quotes: The pipeline is substantially de-risked, and we are confident of achieving our 3 GW commissioning target for FY27, supported by planned capex of around ₹20,000 crore.
Yes, definitely, the project work has started, as we have said that the first unit is expected to be commissioned in FY28 and balance two Units in FY29.
Sharad Mahendra: Yes. Definitely, third quarter is fully booked.
Run rate EBITDA, I think normally, we don't share that information.
So we will take a call at the right time, but we are confident that selling this capacity will not be a problem because of the low fuel cost being close to the mine.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is 75% for consolidated thermal (vs All-India 67.8%) and the 2.5-3 GW annual RE pace, KSK Mahanadi 1,200 MW expansion (600 MW by FY28) and Salboni 3,200 MW are already planned, with the 30 GW 2030 target and ~2.4 GW beyond 2030 needing further sanctions; FY27 equity visibility is ~₹13,150 crore.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management reaffirmed the 3 GW FY27 target and 2.5-3 GW annual pace but declined to give run-rate EBITDA or forward numbers; Q3 merchant book is fully booked at ~₹6.9/unit or better, which could support a raise if Q4 pricing holds.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Risks include 1.6 GW of remaining FY27 RE execution, ~225 MU Q2 curtailment (₹59 crore), imported coal at ~US$115/t (+28% YoY), and ~75% floating-rate debt where a further 75 bps hike lifts cost of debt to ~8.5% from 8.28%.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: 1 GWh standalone BESS in Rajasthan and Kerala to be commissioned in FY27 under ESAs, Halol wind blade facility already producing since June, Chitradurga facility due Q3 FY27, and solar-plus-battery for evening-peak sales planned.

rows.label: Group RTC/captive demand and MoU conversion

rows.why: About 60% of curtailed capacity moves from temporary to permanent GNA by end-Q3 FY27, which should cut the ~225 MU Q2 curtailment (₹59 crore) loss.

rows.label: Net debt/EBITDA falling below 5x
rows.why: Net debt/TTM EBITDA is ~4.94x, down from ~5.2x in FY26, and cost of debt fell 51 bps YoY to 8.28%, though the rate-hike sensitivity could reverse part of this.

533150|2026-03.headline: Godrej Properties Q4 FY26 bookings hit record INR10,163 crores (+21% QoQ); FY27 booking guidance set at over INR39,000 crores.
533150|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 posted record quarterly bookings of INR10,163 crores on 4,789 units and 7.3 mn sq ft, matching the prior best quarter and growing 21% QoQ. FY26 bookings reached INR34,171 crores (+16% YoY), 105% of guidance, and collections hit a record INR19,965 crores (+17% YoY). Q4 total income rose 47% to INR3,895 crores and net profit rose 70% to INR650 crores, with FY26 PAT at INR1,850 crores (+32%). Management guided FY27 bookings above INR39,000 crores and collections above INR24,000 crores, both about 20% growth, and reiterated a 20% ROE target by FY28. Management flagged the Middle East conflict and AI-related sentiment as near-term demand risks, while saying April footfalls and conversions held up.

FY27 collections guided to over INR24,000 crores, about 20% growth; management noted FY26 collections missed the INR21,000 crore guidance by about 5%.

Launch pipeline is large: NCR (Golf Links, Arden tower, Miraya phase), Mumbai (Bandra, Worli tower and phase, Kharghar and Panvel phases, Vikhroli in Q2 or Q3), Thane INR7,500 crore acquisition in late Q3 or Q4, and South, Pune, Kolkata, Raipur and Ahmedabad projects.

demand_pricing: Q4 sales were about 50% sustenance; FY26 mix was roughly 60% launches and 40% sustenance.

A pan-India sustenance campaign launched days before the call uses a 1% per month payment scheme with about 20% upfront and bullet payments. Management says it is a sourcing tool, not a PLP, and cap PLP-style discounts at 5% to 7% of quarterly sales.
Demand weakened in the last two weeks of March amid the Middle East conflict; management estimated about INR1,000 crores of sales were lost, and April footfalls and conversions have been reasonable.

qa_highlights.question: How is FY27 guidance achievable given NCR de-growth, AI concerns in Bengaluru and Pune, and geopolitical risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said NCR's FY26 dip was due to slipped launches (Gurgaon approvals, Ashok Vihar) and expects NCR to return above INR10,000 crores. It sees AI worries as overdone and reasonable for guidance, and said the launch calendar is skewed to H1 and built bottom-up with buffers.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cost impact of the Middle East war on demand, NRI inflows and construction costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Demand dipped in March but has since normalised somewhat; the Dubai-related shift to Indian property is expected to play out over time. Input costs are estimated to rise 5% to 6% at most, with a 0.1% to 0.2% quarterly margin impact, and forward contracts cover most inputs.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company keep pursuing BD above its INR20,000 crore guidance, and when will FCF turn positive?
qa_highlights.answer: BD depends on opportunities, and the balance sheet can support more than guided levels. At INR20,000 crores of BD, FCF should be positive; at FY26-like levels, breakeven. FY28 is expected to be strongly FCF positive.

qa_highlights.question: Why did imputed EBIT margin fall to about 24.5% in FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to a large Bengaluru 50-50 JV project (about INR4,000 crores of sales) and a fall in economic interest to 88% from 93%. PAT margin was at the top of the 10% to 15% guided range for a third year.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the dividend being introduced, and what does it signal about cash generation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said surplus cash will rise as BD investment normalises relative to cash generation, so dividends will be made consistent and growing. The FY27 dividend is modest.

qa_highlights.question: Will the FY27 collections and revenue recognition step up?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects the major revenue step-up in FY28 as OCs arrive, with about INR2,900 crores of revenue already linked to OCs. Economic interest has compounded at 55% a year over five years.

533150|2026-09.headline: Godrej Properties Q2 FY27 bookings fell 6% YoY to INR8,008 crore, but sustenance sales rose 83% to INR5,054 crore and collections hit INR5,318 crore.
533150|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 bookings were INR8,008 crore from 3,658 units (6.2 mn sq ft), down 6% YoY and 7% QoQ, while H1 bookings grew 7% to INR16,669 crore. Sustenance sales were the standout at INR5,054 crore. Collections rose 31% YoY to a record Q2 of INR5,318 crore and operating cash flow was INR1,584 crore. Reported P&L fell sharply: EBITDA down 72% to INR171 crore and net profit down 62% to INR154 crore, which management attributed to back-ended deliveries and JV exit accounting (Mahalunge, Orris). Management guided H2 bookings of INR22,500-25,000 crore and a strong Q3 launch pipeline.

segments.commentary: NCR just under INR2,000 crore, Mumbai about INR1,900 crore, Bangalore just under INR1,600 crore, Pune about INR1,000 crore, Hyderabad about INR700 crore, other cities about INR800 crore.

Four projects added in H1 with about 9 mn sq ft and about INR15,500 crore expected booking value, about 78% of FY27 guidance.

H2 cash collections of INR15,000 crore and operating cash flow of INR7,000 crore, with the company expecting to be free cash flow positive for the period.

Sustenance was 60-40 vs launches historically; Q2 mix was 63% launch and 37% sustenance per management's framing of the quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA and net profit fall sharply despite higher sales?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajendra Khetawat said the Mahalunge JV became a 100% owned project after the partner exit, so the bulk of profit had been recognised earlier through DM fees and overheads, which led to near-equal sales and cost of sales. The Orris settlement also picked up losses on consolidation in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: How long will sustenance sales stay high and what is the launch vs sustenance mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Gaurav Pandey said H2 launches will likely outperform sustenance, and the 60-40 launch-sustenance mix is a guide that can flip if launches slip. Sustenance strength reflects a deliberate push after Gurgaon and Mumbai launches slipped.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company exceed its H2 sales guidance and how much can it add to pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Pirojsha Godrej said the top end of the H2 range (INR25,000 crore) would imply a 40% five-year compounded booking growth. He said the company will not hold back if opportunities arise beyond the 15-20% FY28 growth target.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the H2 launch pipeline has approvals?
qa_highlights.answer: About 80% of Q3 requirements were secured before the quarter, with the rest expected after Diwali. For Q4, management targets about 80% approvals by mid-December and the rest by mid-January.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook on BD and competitive intensity for land?
qa_highlights.answer: Pirojsha Godrej said competition is ongoing but opportunities meeting return thresholds are available, and BD will remain opportunistic. Gaurav Pandey said one or two deals could close in the quarter if terms fit.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company near FCF-positive status in H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Gaurav Pandey said there is a high probability of being FCF positive in Q4 under aggressive internal scenarios, while noting this is not an obsessive target. FY28 is described as almost certain for operating cash flow guidance.

533151|2026-03.headline: D. B. Corp Q4 FY26 consolidated ad revenue rose ~6% YoY to INR 4,067 mn; FY26 total revenue flat at INR 24,408 mn.
533151|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated total revenue grew 4% YoY to INR 5,896 mn, with EBITDA up 15.6% to INR 1,176 mn and PAT up 18.8% to INR 622 mn. For FY26, reported figures were flat versus FY25 because of the prior-year election advertising; excluding that, print ad revenue grew 6.3% and EBITDA 7.1%, with margin up 66 bps to 28%. Management said April 2026 ad growth was strong double-digit and guided to a strong single-digit growth for FY27. Newsprint prices are rising, with management expecting a further 6-8% increase in Q1 FY27.

segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 circulation revenue stable at INR 1,162 mn; average copies about 39 lakh, down roughly 1-2% (about 1 lakh) from prior quarters. Management said competitors are losing more copies in several markets.

segments.commentary: Q4 ad revenue INR 358 mn and EBITDA INR 95 mn. Seven new stations added during the year, taking the network to 37 cities; all seven turned EBITDA positive within 3 months.

qa_highlights.question: Print growth and sector-wise breakdown for FY26?

533151|2026-06.headline: D.B. Corp Q1 FY27 EBITDA rose about 19% to INR 1,647 million, with margin up 250 bps to 26.1% on advertising growth of about 10%.

Profit after tax rose about 25% YoY to INR 1,007 million. Advertising revenue grew about 10% to INR 4,320 million, with management attributing the growth to both volume and a small pricing contribution. Circulation was flat at INR 1,204 million, with copies down to about 38 lakh from 39 lakh in Q4 while cover price stayed at an average INR 4.93. Management said newsprint rose about 13% YoY and about 8% QoQ and expects further increases in Q2 before easing from Q3.

Energy (LPG/PNG) was quantified at 100-120 bps, which the company said it has passed on through pricing, while wage and labour-code costs were discussed as further headwinds.

533155|2026-09.headline: Jubilant FoodWorks Q2 FY27 call: management targets 5-7% FY27 like-for-like growth, with Domino's price hikes of 140-200 bps offsetting dairy, chicken and vegetable inflation.
533155|2026-09.overview: The transcript is a Q&A-only call with no prepared financial figures read out; the shareholder letter was referenced but not reproduced. Management said Domino's like-for-like growth is planned at 5-7% for the full year, with Q3 tracking to plan and the festive period cited as a swing factor of 100-200 bps. Price increases of about 140-200 bps have been taken selectively, and management said it will take further price if needed. Popeyes is described as the second growth engine, but restaurant-level unit economics still need work, with gross margin upside of 100-200 bps and store-level profitability dependent on higher average daily sales (target about Rs 1 lakh per day). Turkey (Turkish operations) reported LFL is negative due to accounting for inflation, which management says masks positive transaction growth.

segments.name: Popeyes
segments.commentary: About 100 stores in 25 cities; management says it has established a second growth engine, but restaurant-level profitability is not yet in place. Gross margin benefits from Domino's supply-chain scale; store rentals are higher than Domino's legacy sites.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 5-7% LFL a full-year number, and what is the second-half trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the plan is for a full-year 5-7% range, with Q3 on track and an uptick seen from Q4 through Q2; festive weeks could shift the numbers by 100-200 bps.

qa_highlights.question: Why is MAU growing about 25% while MTU grows only about 9%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said online delivery is under-penetrated and new customers are being acquired through revamped digital marketing; conversion is lower for first-time users, but long-term customer value is not seen declining.

qa_highlights.question: Can Popeyes accelerate, and what is the path to store profitability?

533156|2026-06.headline: Vascon Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue fell to INR152 crores (from INR221 crores) and PAT to INR2 crores (from INR22 crores), on EPC execution delays.
533156|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations fell about 31% YoY to INR152 crores, driven by lower EPC execution from cash-flow-stalled government projects. Consolidated EBITDA was INR10 crores versus INR34 crores in Q1 FY26, which included an INR18 crores one-time investment gain; adjusted for that, EBITDA was about INR15 crores at roughly 6% margin. Management said the EPC segment stayed profitable at about 9% EBITDA margin, while real estate booked INR4 crores revenue and a INR4 crores EBITDA loss. Management guided to a recovery from Q3 and reiterated the FY27 revenue target of INR1,200 crores, while net debt rose to about INR152 crores.

533169|2026-03.headline: Man Infra FY26 consolidated PAT after minority interest of INR201 crores; FY27 launches targeted at INR5,500 crores GDV and sales ambition of over INR5,000 crores across FY27-FY28.
533169|2026-03.overview: FY26 was described as a consolidation year: sales of about INR1,800 crores, collections of about INR990 crores and over 5 lakh sq ft sold, with consolidated revenue from operations of about INR630 crores. Q4 FY26 sales were about INR438 crores and collections about INR279 crores, with consolidated PAT after minority interest of INR43 crores on total income of INR187 crores. Management guided to a 35-40% rise in revenue recognition in FY27, driven by about 1 million sq ft of launches and near-complete projects, and reiterated a Vision 2030 goal of doubling GDV to over INR35,000 crores. Balance sheet was reported as net debt-free with net worth of about INR2,266 crores and liquidity of about INR686 crores against debt of about INR58 crores.

segments.commentary: GDV portfolio above INR17,500 crores with balance sales pipeline of INR13,300 crores; management says about INR4,000 crores of the GDV is already sold and the rest is unsold. New Tardeo project adds about INR2,000 crores GDV and about 3 lakh sq ft saleable carpet; South Mumbai GDV above INR8,000 crores.

segments.name: Real estate (US, MICL Global)
segments.commentary: Estimated aggregate GDV of about US$1.4 billion across ongoing and one completed development in Florida. Minority stake acquired in West Avenue, Miami Beach project with estimated GDV above US$1 billion and over 100 units.

segments.commentary: Current EPC order book about INR392 crores to be executed over 3-4 years. Upcoming developments have about 1 crore sq ft construction area, of which about 50% expected to add to the EPC order book once FY27 launches occur. Port segment de-emphasised; management says it will bid selectively.

segments.name: Interest income on project investments
segments.commentary: Cumulative MICL Group investment across project entities about INR1,461 crores; management presents the interest income earned as a business income contributing to 'other income'.

guidance_outlook: FY27 launch pipeline of about INR5,500 crores GDV (about 1 million sq ft), including Marine Lines, Tardeo, BKC and Pali Hill; launches to be timed around Diwali for Marine Lines and Nov-Dec for Tardeo 2.0.
Combined sales ambition of over INR5,000 crores across FY27 and FY28; management targets not less than INR2,500 crores in FY27 with a roughly 50-50 split.
Revenue recognition expected to grow about 35-40% in FY27 versus FY26, with Ghatkopar, Dahisar and Atmosphere projects nearing completion.
Over 1 million sq ft carpet area to be delivered over the next 6-18 months; Aaradhya One Park targeted for completion by March 2027; Atmosphere Tower G expected within 18 months.
Vision 2030 goal to double development portfolio to over INR35,000 crores GDV, with management aiming to achieve it before 2031.
Management expects FY25 revenue and profit levels to be surpassed over time; no price appreciation assumed in project feasibility.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said MICL is not building INR100-200 crore tickets and its ticket sizes are comfortable for the micro-markets, so sales velocity risk is low.

533169|2026-06.headline: Man Infra Q1 FY27 consolidated PAT rose 29% YoY to ₹72 crore on revenue up 8% to ₹218 crore; management reiterates 25%+ FY27 PAT growth guidance.
533169|2026-06.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 as a strong quarter, citing consolidated revenue from operations of ₹218 crore (+8% YoY) and profit after tax attributable to shareholders of ₹72 crore (+29% YoY). Cash and cash equivalents rose to ₹768 crore at June 2026 from ₹686 crore at FY26-end, with borrowings of ₹78 crore, which management said are mostly partner contributions in joint ventures. Pre-sales in the quarter were about 85,000 sq ft, or roughly ₹290 crore, which management acknowledged is low, attributing the gap to launches that have not yet happened (Marine Lines, Berkeley House). Management kept its FY27 PAT growth guidance of over 25% and its target of ₹5,000 crore cumulative pre-sales over two years, and reiterated a ₹35,000 crore group GDV goal by 2031.

Mostly partner contributions in JV projects per management
Management noted it is below FY26 run-rate
