segments.commentary: Launched June 2026 with ~₹500 crore GDV; 30% sold within two months. Artek Park (BKC) is over 25% sold.

segments.commentary: IOA received for an ultra-luxury project with over ₹1,000 crore GDV; demolition and vacation of existing structure underway.

segments.commentary: Acquired project with over ₹2,000 crore GDV; IOA received and launch now targeted within FY27 rather than Q1 FY28.

segments.commentary: Launch targeted by March 2027 after FSI policy change and additional plot acquisitions; over ₹3,000 crore GDV per management, DM structure. Expected to surpass Aavan in height.

segments.commentary: First two villas completed, one sold and one retained as show house for sale around March next year. Third villa targeted at ~$15 million. Ritz-Carlton branded residences presales ~$25 million, completion targeted December 2030. About $35 million transferred so far.

segments.name: EPC
segments.commentary: Management is near final negotiations on a significantly large external EPC order, expected to be announced within two quarters. In-house construction pipeline is ₹9,000-10,000 crore, and a Vadhvan port project is in bidding.

guidance_outlook: FY27 PAT growth guidance of over 25% over FY26 reiterated; management said it sees this as comfortable at the bottom line.
Cumulative pre-sales target of ₹5,000 crore over the next two years reiterated; management said it might exceed this if markets stay strong.
Group GDV target of over ₹35,000 crore by 2031 reiterated, with management expecting it to be achieved earlier.
Management aims for a bottom line near ₹500 crore in roughly 2-3 years; it said a significant jump would start this year.
Launch pipeline of about 1.1 million sq ft carpet and ~₹6,600 crore GDV planned this year (two launched so far: Marina Vista and O2 High Street).
Management said it expects to add ₹2.5-3,000 crore GDV per ₹200 crore of capital, with ~₹3,000 crore of cash generation over three years.
capex_capacity: Aaradhya OnePark (Ghatkopar) delivery targeted by March 2027 with structure complete and finishing ongoing.
Aaradhya Avaan (Tardeo) half-building delivery targeted March 2028; 100% RCC targeted by August 2027.
Aaradhya Parkwood remaining two towers due by end of next year; Atmosphere Tower G due by December 2027.

qa_highlights.question: Will luxury projects be done via joint ventures or some at 100% stake, and does the ₹78 crore borrowing reflect debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said partnerships are used to dilute equity and de-risk, not to deploy all cash in one project, and the company avoids debt. Most of the ₹78 crore is partner contribution treated as debt-like funding used for project cash flow, not external institutional borrowing. Future projects may be 100% owned.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company expand beyond MMR into cities such as Pune or Delhi?
qa_highlights.answer: Not for the next couple of years. Management cited per-sq-ft margins in Mumbai exceeding prices in other cities and limited projects elsewhere, and said it is confident in Mumbai.

qa_highlights.question: Is the ₹5,000 crore two-year pre-sales target still achievable given ₹290 crore in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said real estate sales are lumpy, with launches driving ₹1,000 crore-plus months. Marine Lines (₹3,000 crore-plus GDV) and Berkeley House (₹1,000 crore-plus) are not yet launched, and it expects a turnaround by December and March. It said the target could be exceeded if markets stay strong.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the US (Miami) business, its margins, cash flows and forex approach?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the first two villas are complete, one sold and one held as show house until around March next year. The third villa is priced around $15 million. Ritz-Carlton presales are about $25 million, completion targeted December 2030, and about $35 million has been transferred so far, with principal expected back by 2031 according to management. It said the dollar moved from ₹75 to ₹95 and margins are equal or higher than India.

qa_highlights.question: Why was FY26 cash flow negative and will it turn positive in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to new acquisitions and working capital for ongoing projects during a slow sales year. It said the upward trajectory has started with Q1 PAT growth and the launch pipeline.

qa_highlights.question: What are the margin profiles of ultra-luxury projects, and how is the DM model's economics?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ultra-luxury margins per sq ft are higher, with tickets of ₹1 lakh per sq ft and above and Mount Mary/Pali Hill sales around ₹20,000-25,000 per sq ft. Bottom-line percentage stays around 20-25% across projects. DM projects return about 2.5-3x invested capital, with under 10% of GDV invested.

qa_highlights.question: Does the company assume price appreciation, and how will raw-material inflation be handled?

Launch timing risk: Marine Lines targeted by March 2027 after FSI and plot changes; Tardeo 2.0 pulled forward into FY27 from Q1 FY28.
Delivery timelines: Aaradhya OnePark by March 2027, Atmosphere Tower G by December 2027, Aaradhya Avaan half-building by March 2028 and 100% RCC by August 2027.
US (Miami) exposure: about $35 million transferred, the third villa unsold, Ritz-Carlton completion targeted December 2030, and forex and tax treatment questions still open with follow-up pending.

EPC order expected to be announced within two quarters; the Vadhvan port bid is in progress and the in-house pipeline is ₹9,000-10,000 crore.

533179|2026-06.headline: Persistent to acquire Nagarro at EV €1.27bn (€81/share cash) and signed a ~$650M, 6.5-year net-new deal adding ~$125M annual value.
533179|2026-06.overview: Management held a Sunday call (28 June 2026) announcing two items: a net-new strategic deal with an existing large US-headquartered customer worth roughly $125M annually and about $650M over 6.5 years, and a voluntary public takeover offer for Nagarro at €81 per share in cash. The Nagarro offer implies an equity value of about €1bn and EV of €1.27bn, funded by a committed €1.4bn Barclays bridge facility, with a 50% plus one share minimum acceptance. Persistent has already secured 21% via a share purchase agreement, and management board members intend to tender about 13-14%. Closing is expected around Q4 CY2026 or early Q1 CY2027, subject to regulatory approvals. No Q1 FY27 financial results were discussed on this call.

financial_highlights.metric: Nagarro EBIT margin CY25 / Q1 CY26

financial_highlights.value: 140% to undisturbed close (25-26 June); 94% to 3-month VWAP

segments.name: Persistent (standalone)
segments.commentary: Five-year revenue CAGR of about 23.9%, with North America about 81%+ of revenue and Europe about 8-8.5%. Team of 27,500 across 21 countries.

segments.name: Nagarro (target)
segments.commentary: 5-year revenue CAGR of 18.4%, with about 35% of revenue from North America and about 18,500 staff (13,500 in India). Strengths cited in SAP, Siemens, OpenAI reseller and industrial/consumer verticals; management says constant-currency growth was over 5% recently.

segments.name: Combined group
segments.commentary: Pro forma about $2.9bn revenue, 46,000+ staff across 40+ countries; mix of North America 62%, Europe 22%, Rest of World 16%. Management targets European revenue of 15%+ and $5bn aspiration by FY31.

guidance_outlook: Leverage (net debt / combined EBITDA) at close expected at 1.9x-2.5x depending on acceptance, reducing to about 1x by FY2030.
Transaction expected to be cash EPS accretive and reported EPS accretive in Year 1 excluding one-time transaction expenses.
Goodwill vs other intangibles split about 70:30; intangibles amortised over 8 years.
Acquisition-related bridge interest at Euribor plus 175-250bps, roughly 4.1%-4.8% (4.1%-4.5% quoted in Q&A).
Revenue and cost synergies to be detailed only after regulatory approvals; management says margins will be maintained or improved.
New large deal is accretive to revenue and margin from Q2 onwards with no major ramp-up needed.

Public offer timeline: BaFin filing within 4 weeks, offer clearance in 10 working days to 2 weeks, 4-week acceptance period plus optional 2-week extension; Persistent AGM late July to seek shareholder approval. Squeeze-out possible over about 2 years; no domination agreement intended for 2 years.
capex_capacity: Transaction is fully debt-funded via a committed €1.4bn Barclays bridge facility, which also covers Nagarro refinancing if required, backed by a Persistent parent corporate guarantee.
Management said it does not intend a QIP or further dilution; private equity participation at asset level is being considered but no decision taken.
Management said it has moved from capex-heavy models to an opex model, funding working capital to support cash generation.
demand_pricing: Net new large deal from an existing US-headquartered technology customer: ~$125M annually and ~$650M+ over 6.5 years; customer name not disclosed under NDA.
Persistent has two $100M+ accounts, with a third approaching; the combined entity has 180 logos above $1M (Nagarro's largest customer under $50M) and over 350 $1M+ accounts.
Customer overlap between the two companies is in the single digits, with fewer than 10 significant overlapping customers.

Management said T&M model will decline over time but is not dead; Nagarro's T&M share was cited as 65-68% by analysts. Cannibalisation of T&M revenue acknowledged, with SASVA platform cited as a response.

qa_highlights.question: Has there been incremental due diligence on Nagarro's books given BaFin queries, and why is the multiple at a premium?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said legal and tax diligence on BaFin queries (carve-out from Allgeier and accounting principles) found no impact on performance; the premium was described as reasonable for a control transaction.

qa_highlights.question: Will Nagarro run independently for two years post-closing, and why no cash-plus-share structure?
qa_highlights.answer: Persistent will work with management and aim for a squeeze-out over about 2 years, with no hurry. Management said a share swap was not feasible under German public-to-private dynamics; no QIP or dilution planned.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ramp and margin profile of the large deal?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is net new with little ramp needed, end-to-end product engineering and support, accretive from Q2, at a fairly healthy margin above company average.

qa_highlights.question: How will the combined entity sustain growth given Nagarro's slow growth and the long tail of accounts?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to cross-selling of ERP/CX and mining of 180 $1M+ logos, with tail-account rationalisation possible to release SG&A. It said Nagarro's recent growth was affected by distraction from its take-private process.

qa_highlights.question: Decision tree on acceptance: what if below 50%, and what follows above 50%?
qa_highlights.answer: Persistent holds 21% via SPA; management board commitment of about 13-14% takes it near 35%, with another 35-40% considered broadly committed. Management sees 50%+ as very likely; majority gives control of the supervisory board.

risks_watch: Regulatory approvals (including RBI and various EU jurisdictions) and BaFin clearance of the offer document; close targeted Q4 CY26 to early Q1 CY27.
Acceptance level versus the 50%+1 minimum; leverage moves between 1.9x and 2.5x depending on acceptance.
Nagarro's revenue flat for about two years, with several vertical declines (horizontal tech, energy/utilities, telecom, travel) flagged by analysts.
Integration of a two-year squeeze-out path with minority shareholders; synergy plan and value-creation plan not yet shared.
Cash conversion and debt servicing of roughly €1.4bn of acquisition debt, plus the T&M model and AI cannibalisation risk.
533179|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and assertive on strategic fit, growth and margin ambitions, but deliberately evasive on specifics pending regulatory approvals (no synergy numbers, value-creation plan, or customer names). Pushback was given to analysts on Nagarro's EBIT margins and the premium paid.
key_quotes: This is not a consolidation play. This is an expansion play for us bringing together, as Anand rightly pointed out, people, capabilities, markets which are all complimentary to us
we believe we have paid a reasonable premium for a control transaction.
we do not believe that the combined entity will be at any significant lower margins than what Persistent has today.
We don't intend doing any QIP, just to be clear for everyone. We don't intend diluting our stake at this point in time.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management says margins will be maintained or improved and the new ~$125M annual deal is accretive to margin from Q2 at above company average, but synergy numbers are withheld until regulatory approvals and combined EBITDA margin is ~15.6% for Persistent vs Nagarro 13.9%.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Net-new ~$125M annual (~$650M over 6.5 years) US deal accretive from Q2 with little ramp, and Persistent run-rate revenue above $1.7bn; Nagarro revenue is flat for about two years, so growth is mainly deal-driven.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management says it has moved from capex-heavy to opex model, no QIP or further dilution planned, and the €1.27bn EV deal is funded by a committed €1.4bn bridge rather than new plants.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.when: post close, Q4 CY26 to early Q1 CY27
rows.why: Management guides cash and reported EPS accretion in Year 1 excluding one-time transaction expenses, but gave no organic revenue guidance and no Q1 FY27 results were discussed.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Leverage of 1.9x-2.5x at close on ~€1.4bn acquisition debt at Euribor+175-250bps (~4.1%-4.8%) raises interest cost and execution risk; Nagarro revenue flat for ~2 years and T&M share 65-68% faces cannibalisation.

rows.label: Net-new $125M/yr US deal accretive from Q2
rows.why: Signed ~$650M over 6.5 years (~$125M annually) with an existing US technology customer, accretive from Q2 with little ramp needed and a margin above company average.

rows.label: Nagarro take-private closing
rows.when: Q4 CY26 to early Q1 CY27
rows.why: Voluntary offer at €81/share (EV €1.27bn), 21% already secured via SPA plus ~13-14% board tender intent, with 50%+1 minimum acceptance; management sees 50%+ as very likely, subject to RBI and EU approvals.

rows.label: Leverage down to ~1x by FY2030
rows.why: Net debt/combined EBITDA of 1.9x-2.5x at close, expected to reduce to about 1x by FY2030 as cash generation repays the €1.4bn bridge debt.

tone.note: Management was confident on the $125M net-new deal, accretion and the 50%+ acceptance path, but evasive on synergies, value-creation plan and customer names pending approvals; analysts pushed on Nagarro's EBIT margins, the premium paid, and T&M cannibalisation.

533179|2026-09.headline: Persistent Q2 FY27 revenue rose 20% YoY to USD 487.6M, but EBIT margin fell to 15% and reported PAT dropped 25.4% on Nagarro deal costs.
533179|2026-09.overview: Revenue grew 7.8% QoQ and 20% YoY in USD to USD 487.6M, the 26th sequential quarter of growth, with rupee revenue of Rs 46,639M (+30.3% YoY). EBIT margin was 15% (down 100 bps QoQ and 130 bps YoY) as wage hikes and a 90 bps amortisation hit from the large software deal offset ESOP and currency tailwinds. Reported PAT of Rs 3,515.1M (7.5% margin) was hit by about 3.1% from Nagarro transaction costs, while operating PAT rose 5% YoY to Rs 4,951.5M. Bookings slowed: TCV was USD 633.5M and ACV USD 481M, with management citing deal slippage and a decision-making slowdown linked to Middle East dynamics. The Nagarro acquisition is progressing, with about 94% of shares tendered and closing guided to Q4 CY26 or Q1 CY27.

segments.name: North America
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 22.5% YoY in USD terms.

segments.name: Europe
segments.commentary: Revenue declined 8.5% YoY, attributed to one acquired key client ramping down and one fixed-price engagement completing its planned ramp-down; management called these client-specific.

segments.name: India
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 19.4% YoY; rest of world grew 67% YoY on a smaller base.

segments.name: Software, High-Tech and Emerging
segments.commentary: Grew 28.5% YoY, driven by the large software deal from last quarter and the new Software Reinvention offering.

segments.name: BFSI
segments.commentary: Grew 16.2% YoY, supported by a vendor consolidation win at a large financial services client.

segments.name: Healthcare and Life Sciences
segments.commentary: Grew 12% YoY; management said growth should resume, citing a slowdown from a couple of customer-specific dynamics.

guidance_outlook: EBIT margin aspiration of 16-17%; management said it is an aspiration, not guidance, with no year-end target committed.
Nagarro deal closing expected by Q4 CY26 or Q1 CY27; remaining RBI, Austria and Spain FDI approvals expected within 4-8 weeks.
Nagarro acquisition one-time expenses of about USD 50M in total over 3-4 quarters; about USD 19-20M incurred in Q2 and USD 25-30M more to come.
Post-closing, intent to squeeze out minority shareholders (about 94% acquired) and an estimated 5-6 months to integrate the two companies.
Acquisition debt cost assumed at 5-6% net; USD 1.25B debt and equity raise planned to replace the Euro 1.4B bridge loan, including USD 450M equity or equity-linked instruments.
Transaction-related one-time costs may be treated as an exception for ESOP vesting conditions (12% revenue growth and 12% EPS growth), subject to shareholder approval.
capex_capacity: Headcount rose by 958 QoQ to 29,598 at end of Q2 FY27.
Utilisation fell 70 bps QoQ to 85.8%, reflecting proactive hiring for large-deal ramp-up; utilisation drag was about 20 bps on EBIT margin.
Trailing 12-month attrition was 11.9%, down from 12.3% in Q1.

The large software deal (about USD 650M over 6.5 years) carries about USD 4M per quarter of added amortisation on third-party licences and cloud spend, a 90 bps EBIT margin hit that management expects to ease as spend is optimised and revenue scales.
Internal AI IP (SASVA, iAURA, Gen AI) development cost includes significant people cost plus tools; management said it can rise QoQ with new feature development.
demand_pricing: Q2 bookings were USD 633.5M TCV and USD 481M ACV, versus Q1 TCV of USD 1,146.2M and ACV of USD 536.8M which included the USD 650M large deal; management said some deals slipped and decision-making slowed in recent weeks, linked to Middle East dynamics.
Top 5 customers grew 38.9% YoY, top 10 grew 29.9%, top 20 grew 25%, top 50 grew 24%, top 100 grew 21.6%.
Customers above USD 20M annual revenue rose from 12 to 13, above USD 10M from 25 to 34, above USD 5M from 56 to 60, and above USD 1M from 191 to 280.
BFSI demand themes: vendor consolidation, data modernisation for AI and legacy (mainframe) modernisation; management did not give formal guidance but said all segments should grow well.

Software Reinvention Services targets AI-native product development and cost reduction of legacy products; in one case, a marquee software client's product run cost fell 45%. Management said outcome-based, revenue-share commercials with a backstop, and that the revenue upside is not in the deal financials.
Nagarro target: about 200 USD 1M+ customers with only 10 overlapping with Persistent's, per management's diligence view.

qa_highlights.question: Is high token cost pushing enterprise clients to IT services vendors, and is BFSI an early AI adopter?
qa_highlights.answer: Sandeep Kalra said mid-market ISVs are the most AI-adopting segment, with BFSI and healthcare slower due to regulation. Clients are using small or open-weight models and token FinOps, with services firms brought in to optimise model choice and cost.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 90 bps large-deal amortisation hit persist?
qa_highlights.answer: Vinit Teredesai confirmed it will stay in the base for the next two to three quarters and gradually reduce as cost is optimised and revenue grows.

qa_highlights.question: Is the USD 650M large deal included in last quarter's TCV, and why are Q2 bookings softer?
qa_highlights.answer: Sandeep Kalra said the deal was included in Q1 TCV of USD 1,146.2M and ACV of USD 536.8M, which included USD 125M ACV from it. Q2 ACV of USD 481M and TCV of USD 633.5M were described as a reasonable clip, with some slippage and no productivity-driven decline.

qa_highlights.question: Will software licence costs stay at current levels?
qa_highlights.answer: Sandeep Kalra said it is a mix of licences embedded in deal products and Persistent's own tool investment; levels should be assessed on overall profitability as the reinvention practice grows.

qa_highlights.question: Is margin recovery expected post wage hike, and what is the year-end target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated a 16-17% aspirational margin range, not guidance, with optimisation and deal growth as the levers.

qa_highlights.question: What are quick wins from Nagarro after closing?

Radio revenue fell on a high events-led base and remained loss-making at operating EBITDA level, and the company surrendered six loss-making radio frequencies. 533267|2026-03.headline: Cantabil FY26 standalone EBITDA rose 29% to INR264.3 crore at a 31% margin, with Q4 EBITDA up 34% to INR78.1 crore.

533269|2026-03.headline: VA Tech Wabag FY26: revenue up ~20%, PAT up 26%, order book INR 17,200 crore (over 4x revenue), net cash ~INR 950 crore.
533269|2026-03.overview: Management reported FY26 revenue growth of about 20% year-over-year and PAT growth of 26%, with EBITDA margin at 13.3% and ROCE near 20%. Order intake was about INR 7,500 crore versus about INR 5,700 crore last year, taking the order book to INR 17,200 crore, up 26% YoY. Net cash (ex-HAM investment) was about INR 950 crore, up 35% from INR 700 crore, and the company has been net cash positive for 13 consecutive quarters. Management reiterated the 15-20% growth and 13-15% EBITDA guardrails, with a new five-year strategy to be published later in the year. Q&A focused on Middle East pipeline (Kuwait and Saudi orders expected), quarterly India-cluster profitability, lumpy EPC revenue, and the municipal platform and HAM plans.

segments.commentary: EPC about 83% and O&M about 17% of revenue. O&M is about 40% of order backlog (~INR 6,500 crore), with contracts of 5-20 years; target is to lift O&M to 20% of the mix over 3-5 years.

segments.name: Municipal vs Industrial revenue mix
segments.commentary: Municipal about 80% and industrial about 20% of revenue. Management is adding industrial and mentioned BPCL, Reliance and Aramco-linked pursuits.

segments.name: India vs ROW
segments.commentary: Revenue split about 50:50 India and rest-of-world. Order backlog split about 58-60% India and 40-42% ROW.

segments.name: India cluster
segments.commentary: Key projects include Chennai 45 MLD TTRO (rehab plus O&M, INR 1,000+ crore), Chennai ADB-funded ring main, Kodungaiyur reuse O&M, Perur desalination (Southeast Asia's largest per management), Bangladesh and Nepal projects. Digha-Kankarbagh STP won GWI best wastewater project. Quarterly Indian profit fell from about INR 127 crore to INR 60 crore per the questioner; management said to judge on blended multi-year margins.

segments.name: Middle East and Africa cluster
segments.commentary: Management calls MEA the growth engine; Yanbu desalination mega order won. Al-Haer 200 MLD STP is 83% physically complete. Kuwait order expected to be signed soon (management guided to this quarter); Saudi order may slip to next quarter. Namibia and Senegal in execution; Zambia civil works started.

guidance_outlook: Revenue growth guardrail of 15-20% CAGR and EBITDA margin of 13-15% reiterated; new five-year strategy and guardrails to be published later this year, expected to be better than current guidance.
Order book to remain above 3x revenue (currently over 4x); ROCE expected to cross 20% within a couple of years; O&M target 20% in 3-5 years.

Management expects revenue to rise in coming periods as new India orders (Kodungaiyur, Chennai ring main, BPCL, Reliance, BWSSB, DJB) convert; CFO said next year could be about 35% higher but is lumpy.
Kuwait order expected in the current quarter; Saudi order may go to the next quarter (management best guess).
Municipal platform (HAM-style) and industrial tenders expected to be finalised over the next quarter; no HAM bids confirmed yet.
capex_capacity: Asia's largest desalination plant (Tamil Nadu, 400 MLD per analyst question) expected to be commissioned around this time next year.
Al-Haer 200 MLD STP (Saudi) at 83% physical progress; commissioning expected after construction completion.
Bio-CNG first project signed; expected to supply around 3,500 homes' cooking gas or about 400 vehicles per day; management said revenue is not very large initially, with plans to replicate.

533293|2026-06.overview: Standalone revenue grew 16% YoY to INR1,461 crore, led by domestic power gen (+18%), industrial (+19%) and distribution & aftermarket (+20%), while international fell 11% to INR106 crore. Standalone EBITDA declined 4% YoY to INR165 crore and margin compressed to 11.2% from 13.5%, which management attributed to lower export volumes, elevated commodity costs and a lag between cost inflation and price realisation. Standalone net profit fell 9% to INR99 crore. Consolidated revenue rose 13% to INR2,000 crore, with consolidated net profit down 17% to INR111 crore. Management said pricing actions have been taken across most businesses and expects profitability to improve as they flow through over coming quarters.

segments.commentary: Revenue INR268 crore, +20% YoY; growth across all channels led by service; 12 consecutive quarters of double-digit growth cited.

segments.commentary: Revenue INR301 crore, +3% YoY; PBIT INR26 crore, -7% YoY. Fluid Dynamics business broadly flat at INR294 crore; domestic up, exports down; channel pumps more than doubled.

Middle East, a key export market, operated below normal levels due to West Asia conflict and choked logistics routes.
Management declined to split Power Gen growth between price and volume.

qa_highlights.answer: CFO cited a bridge of about INR31 crore YoY from increments, ESOP expense, and capability investments; some costs structural, some timing, not characterised as one-off.

533295|2026-03.headline: Punjab & Sind Bank posts record FY26 net profit of Rs.1,322 crore (up 30.12%) and total business of Rs.2,63,652 crore (up 14.94%).
533295|2026-03.overview: FY26 showed record net profit of Rs.1,322 crore, up 30.12%, with Q4 net profit of Rs.422 crore, up 34.82% YoY. Gross advances grew 18.29% and deposits 12.37%, with business growing 14.94% to Rs.2,63,652 crore. Asset quality improved on a full-year basis (Gross NPA 2.40%, Net NPA 0.79%), but Q4 slippages rose to Rs.355 crore from Rs.168 crore in Q3, mainly from MSME accounts. Net interest margin for the year was 2.55%, and management guided it to 2.65-2.70% by FY27 end. Management also flagged RBI's ECL framework, which it expects to absorb through a five-year glide path with capital impact of roughly Rs.600-800 crore (CRO's preliminary estimate).

Business correspondent network at 3,027, to be scaled to more than 4,000 by end of FY27.
Resilience operations centre for cyber security due in 3-4 months. IT and AI/cyber budget being increased about 2x.

qa_highlights.question: Is training and L&D set up as a separate function?

There are some of the weak accounts which we thought best to recognize and move ahead.
So we feel that by the end of the current year, we should be touching 2.65 % to 2.70% in terms of the NIM.

533295|2026-06.headline: Punjab & Sind Bank Q1 FY27: business up 15.27% YoY to Rs 2,66,420 crore, advances up 19.35%, net profit up 23.05% to Rs 331 crore.
533295|2026-06.overview: Management reported 19.35% YoY advances growth and 12.16% deposit growth, with NII up 15.33% YoY. Operating profit was flat at about Rs 545 crore despite lower treasury (Rs 80 crore vs about Rs 200 crore a year earlier) and lower written-off recoveries. Asset quality improved on a YoY basis (GNPA 2.21%, NNPA 0.65%), but the quarter included about Rs 123.5 crore of provisions, of which about Rs 150 crore was ECL build-up, which management said was proactive. Management kept FY27 guidance intact and said advances growth of 18-20% is achievable.

segments.name: MSME

segments.commentary: RAM is 60.02% of advances, against a year-end target of 64-65%. The bank is pursuing this through branch activation, digital journeys and co-lending.

Deposit growth guidance of 13-14% was missed slightly in Q1 and is maintained.
NIM target of 2.60-2.65% for FY27, versus 2.53% in Q1.
ROA target of 0.85-0.90%; ROE target of about 12%, versus 10.85% in Q1.
Cost to income to be below 60% in FY27, with an aspiration of below 50% in two to three years.
Credit cost guidance below 1%, including ECL build-up ahead of the 1 April 2027 ECL regime.
Core fee income target of Rs 900-1,000 crore for FY27.
Net slippage for FY27 to stay below Rs 677 crore (FY26 level), with a hope to bring it below Rs 600 crore.
Three-year plan: business of Rs 4,00,000 crore by FY29, 2,000 branches, about 1,600 ATMs and 6,000-6,500 business correspondents.
FCNR(B) and ECB/overseas borrowing mobilisation estimated at about USD 100 million; FCNR(B) alone estimated at USD 20-25 million. GIFT City branch expected around November.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the bank's QoQ business and advances growth look subdued in Q1 compared with peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 is always subdued and the bank paces growth QoQ. It kept 16-18% guidance, now sees 18-20% (and 19-20% possible), and cited about Rs 15,000 crore of undisbursed sanctions.

qa_highlights.question: Why did net profit fall QoQ, and why did provisions rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the extra provisions (Rs 123.5 crore vs Rs 20 crore in Q4) were proactive ECL build-up, not asset quality deterioration. About Rs 150 crore was ECL provision this quarter, and PCR rose to 92.33%.

qa_highlights.question: Which FY27 ratios are being targeted?
qa_highlights.answer: NIM 2.60-2.65% (Q1: 2.53%), ROA 0.85-0.90%, ROE about 12% (Q1: 10.85%), and cost to income below 60%, with an aspiration below 50% in two to three years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the net worth change, and what drove it?
qa_highlights.answer: Net worth is Rs 12,500 crore vs Rs 11,945 crore in Q4. The CFO said the AFS component was Rs 170 crore and the remaining difference was due to a DTA adjustment.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FCNR(B) and overseas borrowing opportunity?
qa_highlights.answer: FCNR(B) is estimated at USD 20-25 million, with about USD 100 million from all routes including ECB and overseas borrowing. Lack of a foreign branch limits leverage; GIFT City branch is expected around November.

qa_highlights.question: What is the gold loan trajectory and co-lending mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Gold loan book is about Rs 4,000 crore, with co-lending about Rs 10,000 crore and expected net addition of about Rs 3,000 crore in the year. Agri gold loan is about Rs 419 crore.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Q1 provisioning is ECL vs normal NPA provisions, and is the credit cost guidance of below 1% realistic?
qa_highlights.answer: About Rs 150 crore was ECL provision this quarter. Management said core credit cost should be very low as no red flags are seen, and the sub-1% guidance is a prudent buffer for ECL when it kicks in on 1 April 2027.

qa_highlights.question: How will NIM evolve given funding cost pressure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated FY27 NIM guidance of 2.60-2.65% versus 2.53% in Q1, citing higher-yield asset deployment and negotiation on pricing.

qa_highlights.question: Will MSME slippage stress continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the current run rate may continue given global trickle-down to MSMEs, but it is not alarming. FY27 net slippage is targeted below Rs 677 crore (FY26 level), with hope to go below Rs 600 crore.

533333|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 162% to INR314 crore and PAT 118% to INR44 crore, helped by the CrudeChem (CCT) acquisition.
533333|2026-03.overview: Fineotex reported Q4 FY26 revenue from operations of INR314 crore, up 162% YoY, with PAT of INR44 crore versus INR20 crore a year earlier, driven by the newly acquired US oilfield chemicals business CrudeChem Technologies Group (CCT). International revenue rose to 70% of the mix and ROIC was stated at 31%. Management said Q4 is the base for future growth, is doubling CCT's manufacturing capacity, and targets a $200 million CCT revenue run-rate before 2028 and a blended EBITDA of 18-20%. Non-CCT textile volumes were said to be recovering, with textile specialty up about 8% YoY in Q4.

segments.commentary: Textile share of total revenue fell to about 35-36%, though textile revenue grew in value. Textile specialty volumes were up about 8% YoY in Q4 and about 15% in volume per a later clarification.

Stake: founders to sell a further 25% of CCT to Fineotex in January 2028, taking the holding to about 79-80% (currently about 53%).

533333|2026-06.headline: Fineotex Q1 FY27 total income rose 165% YoY to INR 386.72 crore, with EBITDA of INR 59.14 crore at a 15.70% margin, driven by the US CrudeChem consolidation.
533333|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 consolidated total income was INR 386.72 crore against INR 146.62 crore a year earlier, mainly from a full quarter of the US operations (CrudeChem Technologies Group, CCTL). EBITDA rose 134.7% YoY to INR 59.14 crore, with margin at 15.70% versus 13.93% in the prior quarter, and PAT grew 92.67% to INR 48.21 crore. The Texas plant capacity was expanded to about 148,000 MTPA, with utilisation stated at about 63%. Management declined to give a fixed margin guidance, while reiterating USD 100 million (FY27) and USD 200 million (FY28) targets for the oil and gas segment.

segments.name: Oil and gas specialty chemicals (CCTL, US)
segments.commentary: Management said about 65% of revenue and about 55% of volume come from oil and gas, roughly INR 250 crore in the quarter. The Texas plant is now about 148,000 MTPA, and management said it is utilised at about 63%.

segments.name: Textile specialty chemicals (India, standalone business)
segments.commentary: Management said the base business is about INR 132 crore after deducting CCTL from consolidated revenue, against INR 137 crore in Q1 FY26, a 1-2% dip that it attributed to monsoon seasonality and competition. Management said pricing was passed on and that the textile business is flattish.

guidance_outlook: Oil and gas segment targets of USD 100 million in FY27 and USD 200 million in FY28, which management said are driven by order book and customer expectations rather than crude prices. Management said it expects the target to be reached by December 2028.
Management said it expects the Texas plant to be fully utilised within the coming few quarters, with scope to add a second shift.
Management said it has no fixed consolidated EBITDA margin guidance. It reiterated the aspiration of 18% margin but did not commit to it.
Management said margins are sustainable, with pass-through of raw material and freight costs through war surcharges in the US.
capex_capacity: Texas manufacturing capacity was expanded to about 148,000 MTPA (from about 80,000 MTPA), taking group capacity to about 268,000 MTPA, per an analyst's figure that management did not dispute.
Texas utilisation is about 63%, with management saying another 30-40% could be added on the existing plant.
Management said further capex needed to support growth is about USD 1-2 million, which it does not regard as material.
A second shift is available on the Texas plant, and new high-performance machinery was installed in the expansion.
The new Indian plant at FSPL Specialties, commissioned in August 2025, operates under Section 115BAB at a 15% tax rate.
demand_pricing: Management said it passes on raw material and freight cost increases through a US war surcharge, and that margins are sustainable even if prices fall.
Management said the order book for CCTL is not a fixed tender-based order book. It said demand is perennial once wells are producing, with short weather-related interruptions.
Management said it has started selling to Canada and has won a Saudi business order. It also said a customer has an USD 8 billion Aramco order where Fineotex's specialty package is used.
Management said textile demand is supported by Indian export recovery, with UK, EU and US trade deals improving sentiment.
Management said it competes with US specialty chemical majors on price, and that its performance is equivalent.

qa_highlights.question: What is the top-line and bottom-line growth outlook from the Texas capacity addition, and are there any inorganic targets?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Texas is at about 63% utilisation, with room to add 30-40%. It said it is evaluating acquisitions with a focus on synergy and value, and will disclose to exchanges once an advanced stage is reached.

qa_highlights.question: Is the USD 200 million FY28 oil and gas target dependent on crude prices?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the target depends on order book and customer relationships, not crude price. It said activity continues even at USD 60, and that crude is currently around USD 90-100.

qa_highlights.question: Why did standalone revenue and EBITDA decline YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the standalone figures exclude FSPL Specialties, the new Indian plant. Combined with FSPL, the dip is not visible, and the difference is an accounting presentation matter.

qa_highlights.question: What is CCTL's ROCE and does it need more capital?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said oil and gas is not capex-intensive and ROCE is among the best in the industry. Growth needs about USD 1-2 million of capex, and the business runs on one shift today.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 15.7% margin sustainable, and can the business reach the 18% level?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it does not guide to a fixed blended margin and that the blended margin is in the 13-14% range or better for CCTL. It said it aspires to better margins.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the CCTL forex gain or loss not clear?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FX gains or losses are reported separately as a foreign exchange item, not as other income, and that natural hedging exists through USD raw material purchases. It said the impact is small, around INR 1-2 crore.

risks_watch: Reported consolidated numbers depend heavily on CCTL, which is about 65% of revenue, so the base textile business is less visible.
The 63% Texas utilisation needs to rise to deliver the USD 100 million FY27 and USD 200 million FY28 oil and gas targets.
Management declined to give fixed margin guidance and did not explain the 18% aspiration in quantified terms.
Non-controlling interest (about 47% of CCTL) and the accounting for it were not clearly quantified on the call.
Textile base business was flat YoY; a rebound is expected in later quarters, but management has not given numbers.
Geopolitical volatility and freight and raw material price movements, with management saying pricing changes are unpredictable.

USD 1 million or USD 2 million investment here and there is not going to change the world for Fineotex at all at the moment.

533339|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue fell 45.2% YoY to Rs.178.1 crore, with operational EBITDA margin at 28.6%; management reaffirms Rs.4,000 crore cumulative revenue for FY27-28.
533339|2026-03.overview: Consolidated Q4 FY26 revenue was Rs.178.1 crore, flat sequentially but down 45.2% YoY, which management attributed to order-inflow timing with most order book slated for FY27. Operational EBITDA was Rs.51 crore (28.6% margin), down about 900 bps QoQ and 1,390 bps YoY, driven by fixed-cost deleveraging, year-end incentives, warranty provision true-up, export post-supply costs and higher R&D. Consolidated order book stood at Rs.1,336 crore, of which about Rs.1,000 crore is expected to execute in FY27, mainly in Q2 and Q3. Management focused its prepared remarks on anti-drone (hard-kill) systems, simulators, and new products launched at Prayagraj, including the HyperStrike interceptor drone and Vrishabh UGV.

rows.why: Management reaffirmed the Rs.4,000 crore FY27-28 target, but it has no quantified near-term order inflow (Q1 FY27 order inflow still awaited) and FY26 revenue fell 29.4%, so an upgrade is not supported by the evidence.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q4 FY26 revenue fell 45.2% YoY to Rs.178.1 crore, simulator orders are delayed, Q1 FY27 inflow is still awaited, and the Rs.4,000 crore target depends on an order book that has to reach about Rs.3,000 crore.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: HyperStrike interceptor drone production starts in FY27 (5,000 per shift per month initially), the Vrishabh UGV commercial launch is planned for FY27, and weapon systems launch during FY27, although 30mm smart ammunition is only expected to supply next financial year.

rows.label: Working capital normalisation to 140-150 days
rows.why: Working capital days are at 196 (vs 194 at Q3) due to FY27 inventory build; long-term guidance is 140-150 days, and arms/ammunition working capital needs arrive from next year at the earliest.

rows.why: Management said a good order inflow is expected in Q1 FY27, no later than Q2, against a Rs.1,500 crore bidding pipeline and a Rs.1,336 crore order book, although no order value was quantified.

rows.label: Anti-drone and simulator exports
rows.why: Chairman said factored exports are in the Rs.4,000 crore target and anti-drone and simulator exports are expected to be significant, but no export order value was quantified.

tone.note: Management was confident on the long-term Rs.4,000 crore target, 35% EBITDA margin and anti-drone demand, but vague on near-term order timing and the margin dip; analysts pushed on order conversion and whether procurement would shift to foreign vendors, which management disagreed with.

533339|2026-06.headline: Zen Technologies Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue fell to Rs.141.6 Cr (vs Rs.158.2 Cr YoY) and operational EBITDA margin to 27.3%, with management guiding to mid-30s for FY27.
533339|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations was Rs.141.6 Cr, down from Rs.178.1 Cr in Q4 FY26 and Rs.158.2 Cr in Q1 FY26, which management attributed to order execution timing. Operational EBITDA was Rs.38.7 Cr at a 27.3% margin versus 40.9% a year ago and 28.6% in Q4, with management citing negative operating leverage on a largely fixed cost base and a Rs.7.65 Cr provision release in the prior-year quarter. Reported PAT was Rs.34.5 Cr after a Rs.3.4 Cr exceptional fire-related loss at a subsidiary; adjusted PAT is about Rs.37 Cr (26.1% margin). Order book stood at Rs.1,239 Cr, with a Rs.177.5 Cr Ministry of Defence simulator order received after quarter end; the group remains debt free with about Rs.1,217 Cr cash.

segments.name: Simulators (army, navy, air force)
segments.commentary: Management calls simulators and anti-drone systems the two matured franchises; a Rs.177.5 Cr MoD order for tank and crew gunnery simulator upgradation came after quarter end. Management expects Rs.700-800 Cr of simulator orders in the pipeline, with some possibly within months.

segments.name: Anti-drone / counter-drone systems
segments.commentary: Demand is tender-gated: management says no anti-drone or simulator tenders have been floated recently, though a fast-track process is expected to bring them. Management cited about Rs.800 Cr of anti-drone orders after Operation Sindoor and expects anti-drone opportunities of at least Rs.2,000 Cr.

segments.name: Vector Technics (drone propulsion)
segments.commentary: Capacity expanded to about 300,000 units. Management said drone segment orders have slowed; it estimates Rs.300 Cr potential revenue if orders at Rs.10,000 per unit materialise, with about 50% of enquiries from overseas.

segments.name: Robotics / new products
segments.commentary: Vrishabh unmanned ground vehicle has completed internal trials; customer trials pending. Management expects robotics, autonomous vehicles and related products to take at least two to three years to mature.

guidance_outlook: FY27 full-year operational EBITDA margin expected in the mid-30s, as revenue scales and operating leverage works in the company's favour; Q1 margin was below the 35% guidance.
Order book expected to end FY27 at about Rs.2,500 Cr after FY27 execution, per management's earlier investor-meeting communication.
Revenue for FY27 expected to be weighted toward Q2 and Q3, given that much of the order book was secured in H2 FY26 with roughly 12-month execution cycles.
Management referenced a cumulative Rs.4,000 Cr revenue target for FY27 and FY28 combined; the simulator share was put at about Rs.2,000 Cr.
Management said it is actively looking to acquire companies, with funds remaining from QIP plus accumulated cash.
capex_capacity: Vector Technics propulsion capacity expanded to about 300,000 units.
Working capital build-up in supplier advances and inventory to execute order book deliveries through FY27.

Air Force: first flight simulator (C295 referred to on the call as C195 in one answer) developed in-house; full motion simulator capability available; company shortlisted for future Air Force simulators.
demand_pricing: Q1 order intake was Rs.44.6 Cr against Rs.141.6 Cr executed, so the order book declined from March 2026.

Management attributes softness to demand, not supply: no tenders for anti-drone or simulator systems had been issued recently; prior tenders were single-vendor because competitors were disqualified on technical grounds.
Management expects some competition and says Zen will not win every requirement.

Export push: targeting Middle East, Africa, Southeast Asia and CIS; also North America and EU via prime contractors (FOCI and ITAR clearances in progress). Management says US target is about $100 Mn in year three.
Government is moving more orders to 12-month fast-track procurement (FTP) cycles, though large orders still go through regular procurement.

qa_highlights.question: Why did margins contract YoY when revenue was roughly flat, given operating leverage should help?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 FY26 benefited from Rs.7.65 Cr of provision releases (about 5 margin points); adjusted for these, Q1 FY26 margin would be about 35%. Q1 FY27 also absorbed Rs.2.88 Cr higher warranty provisions and Rs.4.25 Cr incremental R&D.

qa_highlights.question: Expected FY27 order book size after the July order (around Rs.1,400 Cr)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated an expected year-end FY27 order book of about Rs.2,500 Cr after FY27 execution, with government procurement needed to convert the pipeline.

qa_highlights.question: Does the Rs.4,000 Cr cumulative FY27-FY28 revenue target allow for larger anti-drone and simulator wins?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman Ashok Atluri said many orders are expected, citing about Rs.800 Cr of anti-drone orders placed after Operation Sindoor, and simulator orders of Rs.700-800 Cr in the pipeline; US target is modest, about $100 Mn in year three.

qa_highlights.question: What is the simulator share of the Rs.4,000 Cr FY27-FY28 target and how soon could orders come?
qa_highlights.answer: Simulators were put at about Rs.2,000 Cr of the Rs.4,000 Cr. The Rs.700-800 Cr simulator order pipeline could materialise sooner than Q2 and Q3, with one order possibly very soon and another in a couple of months.

qa_highlights.question: Is the softness in anti-drone and simulator orders a supply issue or a demand issue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is demand-related: no anti-drone or simulator tenders have been floated recently; earlier tenders were single-vendor because rivals were disqualified. Zen expects competition and will not win every requirement; fast-track tenders are expected within months.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Air Force, Navy and Army market potential and the recurrence of tank gunnery orders?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimated Army and Navy simulator potential at upwards of $2.5 Bn (about Rs.25,000 Cr). Using a 4,000-tank illustration, it said the Rs.177 Cr order was for integrating existing simulators and is a very small part of the addressable need; an order lifecycle is about 10 years with AMC from year 2-3.

qa_highlights.question: Is the shift to 12-month procurement a structural change?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said more orders are coming through 12-month fast-track procurement (FTP), but large orders still go via regular procurement, which can take up to three years.

qa_highlights.question: Vector Technics revenue potential and whether it supplies other drone makers?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity is about 300,000 units; drone segment orders have slowed. At Rs.10,000 per unit, potential revenue is about Rs.300 Cr. Around 50% of enquiries are from overseas, and Vector sells to all Indian and friendly-nation customers.

risks_watch: Demand-gated order flow: no anti-drone or simulator tenders recently; Q1 order intake Rs.44.6 Cr vs Rs.141.6 Cr executed, so the order book shrank from March 2026.
Management's FY27 mid-30s EBITDA margin guidance versus Q1 at 27.3%; watch whether revenue scales in Q2 and Q3 to restore operating leverage.

Export and US market entry: FOCI and ITAR clearances pending, with the US targeted as a subcontractor to primes; management said meaningful US revenue is unlikely before year three.
Planned acquisitions using residual QIP funds and accumulated cash; no targets were named.
Working capital cycle rose to 257 days from year-end on supplier advances and inventory; debtor days stable at 122 days.
Rs.3.4 Cr exceptional fire loss at a subsidiary; inventory was insured per management.

I want to affirm that the margin this quarter is a function of revenue timing and operating leverage, not of any structural change in the profitability of the business.
Gautam this is mostly demand-related issue more than our ability to supply I think.

533339|2026-09.headline: Zen Technologies Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue hit a record Rs.345.1 crore (+98.8% YoY) with 38.2% operational EBITDA margin; order book rose to Rs.1,375.7 crore.
533339|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 was the company's highest-ever quarterly revenue at Rs.345.1 crore, more than double Q1 FY27 (Rs.141.6 crore) and up 98.8% YoY. Operational EBITDA margin was 38.2% and PAT attributable to shareholders rose 50.7% YoY to Rs.89.5 crore. H1 FY27 operational EBITDA margin was 35.1%, which management said is in line with its mid-30s full-year guidance. Working capital cycle stretched to 379 days from 255 days in Q1, and H1 operating cash flow was negative, which management attributed to back-ended receivables and supplier advances. Management stated that the company remains debt-free with about Rs.968 crore of cash and bank balances.

segments.commentary: Management said simulators typically carry higher margins than ADS; FY26's 48% margin reflected a simulator-heavy mix. segments.name: Counter-drone (C-UAS)
segments.commentary: No C-UAS orders have been placed as tenders are yet to float. Management expects FTP-linked orders in Q4 FY27 at the earliest, with possible spillover to Q1 or Q2 FY28. Q2 warranty provisions rose Rs.9.3 crore on higher ADS mix.

segments.commentary: Product is in internal trials with no current order book. Revenue expected from FY28, majority of orders in FY29; management assumes an average price of about $10,000 per unit.

qa_highlights.question: Which orders could come in if FTPs slip 6-9 months?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said mainly counter-drone systems, plus about Rs.400 crore of simulator orders, which are taking time to materialise.

qa_highlights.question: What is the update on Hyper Strike and when is revenue expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Product is in internal trials with no current order; significant contribution is expected by next year (FY28), with majority of orders in FY29.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any deferment or delay risk in executing the current order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it does not foresee any deferment or delays in executing existing orders; the Q1-to-Q2 slippage was a one-time spillover.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Rs.1,375.7 crore order book flagged to convert within six months, and how do the naval acquisitions fit?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said Rs.485 crore is already done and the remainder is to be executed over the next two quarters; management described naval CTNs (ARI and Anawave) as a pipeline with no order yet.

533344|2026-03.headline: PFS FY26 PAT rose to INR319 crores from INR217 crores, while Q4 sanctions jumped to INR1,004 crores and gross Stage III fell 73% to INR190 crores.
533344|2026-03.overview: FY26 showed a sharp pickup in sanctions (INR3,448 crores, over 4x FY25) and disbursements (INR1,235 crores, up 35%), with PAT up about 47% to INR319 crores. Asset quality improved materially: gross Stage III fell to INR190 crores and net Stage III to INR47 crores, with provision coverage on Stage III at 75%. AUM moderated to INR3,292 crores as low-yield legacy loans prepaid (INR1,105 crores of unscheduled prepayments), and Q4 profitability softened with RoNW at 6.24% and portfolio yield at 10.29%. Leadership change (MD and CEO R. Balaji resigned, effective after 30 June) and the absence of a dividend dominated investor questions.

segments.name: Infrastructure finance (renewable, transmission, DISCOM, oil and gas, roads, CBG, data centre)
segments.commentary: All FY26 disbursements went to private corporate borrowers; sanctions were mainly private, with one or two utility sanctions where returns are acceptable. Structured finance (value chain) is being built to lift yield over the medium term.

segments.name: Stage III / legacy resolution
segments.commentary: Major part of the INR190 crores gross Stage III is Danu Wind Parks, referred to NCLT; promoters have offered an OTS that will be considered on merits. About 73% of gross Stage III accounts by value transitioned out during the year.

guidance_outlook: Management expects at least 30% to 50% YoY AUM growth (disbursements minus repayments), with quality prioritised over quantity.
About INR2,000 crores of sanctioned amount is undisbursed; roughly INR1,500 crores expected in the next two quarters, with major portion in Q2 FY27.
FY27 disbursement target of INR4,000 crores is not yet set; budget is awaiting approval and is framed on yield and RoA, not volume.
Cost of funds expected to fall as fresh borrowings replace older, higher-cost debt; PFS base rate was cut by 60 bps in the last quarter.
No dividend declared; the board will review it next quarter. Management acknowledged a suggestion for a dividend at the annual meeting.
capex_capacity: Sanctions-to-disbursement gap is structural: infrastructure projects run 6 months to 3.5 years, so disbursement follows construction progress.
Liquidity of about INR1,800 crores on balance sheet; borrowing deferred until required, with ALCO matching disbursement needs.
Average tenure of new project loans cited at 5 to 7 years.
Prepayments of INR1,105 crores and total repayments of INR1,441 crores in FY26; prepayments were low-yield legacy loans and are not predictable.
demand_pricing: Management says new disbursements are at higher yields than prepaid loans, so portfolio yield is expected to improve.
Q4 FY26 portfolio yield fell to 10.29% from 11.27%, which management attributed to portfolio dynamics and calibrated growth.
Sole and multiple lending structures are being prioritised over consortium lending, though PFS also participates in consortium and co-lending on a case-by-case basis.
Net NPA stated at 1.49%, with gross NPA INR190 crores and net NPA INR47 crores.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the gap between sanctions (about INR3,500 crores) and disbursements (about INR1,200 crores) so large?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said infrastructure projects are disbursed as construction progresses over 1 to 3 years, so sanctions convert to disbursement later. Past lack of a sanctioned pipeline also explains the current low disbursement.

qa_highlights.question: Why did R. Balaji resign, and is the FY27 disbursement vision still on track?
qa_highlights.answer: The company said the resignation was for personal reasons already disclosed; the MD and CEO remains until 30 June and a replacement process has started. The FY27 target of about INR4,000 crores was not committed and is pending budget approval.

qa_highlights.question: Why is borrowing cost high at around 9.5%, and what is the guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the cost of borrowing is below 9.5%, that the treasury is pressing lenders for spread cuts, and that the base rate was cut 60 bps. Cost of funds should fall as new, cheaper borrowings replace older debt.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company declare a dividend, and what is the NTPC promoter impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Dividend has not been declared; the board will review it next quarter. Management said no formal intimation on the NTPC shareholding change has been received and no adverse impact is expected.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the company holding cash rather than disbursing, and is this a fundraising issue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it holds about INR1,800 crores of liquidity, will borrow only when needed to match asset-liability timing, and has about INR2,000 crores of pipeline to disburse over the next six months.

qa_highlights.question: What are the INR190 crores gross Stage III accounts, and what is the status?
qa_highlights.answer: Kalur Srinivas said the major portion is Danu Wind Parks, referred to NCLT, with the promoters having offered an OTS that will be considered on merits; updates will be given to exchanges.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for AUM growth over the next two years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided to at least 30% to 50% YoY AUM growth, stating that AUM means disbursements minus repayments, and said no fresh slippage has occurred in the last eight years of disbursements.

segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR 6,091 million and EBITDA INR 601 million (9.9%). Q4 revenue INR 1,668 million, EBITDA INR 233 million (14% margin); India MDF revenue up 37.3% YoY in Q4 and 12.5% for FY26; blended realisation up 9.7% YoY in Q4. Capacity utilisation 83% in Q4, 75% for FY26.

segments.name: Laminates
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR 2,111 million (+6.1% YoY), EBITDA INR 182 million (8.6%). Q4 revenue INR 534 million, EBITDA INR 41 million (7.7%). Domestic revenue +21% YoY for FY26; blended realisation +7.5%, export realisation +13.7%. Utilisation above 91% in Q4 and above 89% for FY26.

segments.name: Jumbo Laminates
segments.commentary: Both phases now operational with 28 lakh sheets per annum capacity (per analyst). Products sold to Russia, Portugal, Slovakia, Romania, Israel, Kosovo and others; brands VIR KLADS, VIR TOPAZ, VIR VAULT. Customer onboarding is long due to certification requirements. Management expects FY27 utilisation of 60-65%, rising to 85% in FY28.

guidance_outlook: Management declined to give numeric FY27/FY28 revenue or EBITDA guidance; four stated priorities: value-added products to 50% of MDF volumes and 60% of MDF revenue (FY26: 42% volume, 54% value), scaling Jumbo Laminates, raising utilisation to about 90% across the year, and aggressive cost optimisation.
Q1 FY27 capacity utilisation expected to be in the range of Q4 FY26 levels (about 83% MDF, above 91% Laminates).
MDF EBITDA margin currently about 8%; target of 10-12% for MDF, driven by value-added mix.
Laminate business EBITDA target of 10-12% on average, with wide range across Jumbo SKUs.
No new debt planned in FY27; scheduled repayment of around INR 50 crores in FY27.

Management estimated Jumbo Laminate potential revenue at 28 lakh sheets x 85% x INR 4,000 per sheet (about INR 950 crores at full utilisation, as per the analyst's arithmetic); management did not confirm the INR 900 crore figure and said it depends on product mix.
capex_capacity: Jumbo Laminate: both phases operational; one facility underwent a major machinery upgrade in April 2026, production ramping up.
Jumbo thickness range 2.1 mm to 18-19 mm versus 0.6 mm to 1.9 mm for conventional laminates; management cited average realisation around INR 4,000 per sheet.
MDF utilisation 83% in Q4 FY26, 75% for FY26; target 90% across the year in FY27.
Laminate utilisation above 91% in Q4 FY26 and above 89% for FY26.
Product mix (approx.): MDF 75%, Laminates 20%, WPC 5%; Jumbo expected to raise laminate share over time.
Management expects three new MDF plants industry-wide this financial year, implying oversupply pressure.
demand_pricing: MDF price hike of 15% and Laminate price hike of 10% from 1 April 2026; management said the hike only offsets cost, with no incremental margin intended.
Chemical prices up roughly 40% since the Middle East conflict began; net impact about 10% of selling price, or about 11% total cost increase per management.
Industry MDF demand CAGR cited at 15-18%; management assumes 650-800 cubic metres per year of new capacity can be absorbed, but sees oversupply near term.

Export: company is not exposed to the US tariffs; laminates are the bulk of exports (Europe, Russia, Western Europe, Baltics, CALA). MDF exports were lower due to Middle East dependence and a calibrated export approach.
Distribution network: 67 new direct distributors and more than 131 retailers and dealers added in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: What will capacity utilisation look like in Q1 FY27 across plants?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 would be in the range of Q4 FY26 levels; MDF exports are under pressure, so domestic sales are being pushed, and a Jumbo facility machinery upgrade completed in April is ramping up.

qa_highlights.question: What revenue or EBITDA guidance for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: No numeric guidance; management instead listed four priorities: 50% value-added share, scaling Jumbo, 90% utilisation and cost optimisation.

qa_highlights.question: What is the current net debt and FY27-28 debt outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Net debt (after cash) went from INR 262 crore (Mar 2025) to INR 254 crore (Mar 2026), including about INR 9 crore euro FX impact; about INR 50 crore scheduled repayment in FY27 and no new debt planned.

qa_highlights.question: Jumbo Laminate realisation and potential revenue at full utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said realisation around INR 4,000 per sheet on average, with utilisation up to 85%; the analyst's 28 lakh sheets x 85% x INR 4,000 math was confirmed as correct, though management later said the calculation overstates output because higher thicknesses yield fewer sheets.

qa_highlights.question: Is the MDF price hike purely cost recovery or margin-accretive?
qa_highlights.answer: Purely cost recovery: chemical costs up about 40%, net about 10% of selling price, so total cost up about 11%; no additional margin is being earned.

qa_highlights.question: Steady-state MDF realisation and EBITDA margin for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Current MDF EBITDA margin about 8%; target 10-12% through higher value-added mix; value-added share missed target slightly in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Jumbo volume, revenue and margin targets for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation targeted at 60-65% in FY27 and up to 85% in FY28; Laminate-business EBITDA target 10-12% on average, with wide margin range by SKU.

qa_highlights.question: Industry demand-supply and MDF capacity additions?
qa_highlights.answer: Three new plants expected this financial year, implying oversupply; management was not aware of unorganised-sector capacity closures.

risks_watch: Oversupply from three new industry MDF plants in FY27 could pressure pricing and utilisation despite the 15% MDF price hike.
Raw material risk: chemical/resin costs up about 40% since the Middle East conflict; formaldehyde supplier and pricing details were not disclosed.
Export exposure to Middle East shipping disruption; MDF export volumes remain subdued.
Jumbo Laminates ramp is slow: long certification cycles; FY27 utilisation target of 60-65% is well below the 85% long-term assumption.
Euro FX exposure contributed about INR 9 crore to net debt increase; FY27 scheduled repayment about INR 50 crore.

rows.why: Jumbo Laminate (2.1 mm to 18-19 mm thickness, brands VIR KLADS, VIR TOPAZ, VIR VAULT) is being scaled from both phases, and value-added MDF products are targeted at 50% of volume (42% in FY26).

rows.label: MDF and laminate price hikes effective 1 Apr 2026

tone.note: Management was confident on the Q4 recovery, Jumbo ramp-up and the 90% utilisation target, but declined numeric FY27/FY28 guidance and was evasive on formaldehyde suppliers and unorganised-sector closures; analysts pressed on oversupply from three new MDF plants and the Jumbo revenue arithmetic.

533470|2026-06.headline: Rushil Decor Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 27.8% YoY to INR 2,920 mn, but EBITDA margin was 7.9% and PAT only INR 20 mn amid input cost and freight pressure.
533470|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 27.8% YoY, driven by normalised Andhra Pradesh MDF operations and a 65.3% jump in laminate revenue. Gross margin was 39% and EBITDA INR 182 mn (7.9% margin), but profitability was hit by elevated resin/chemical costs, higher freight and West Asia shipping disruption. Management said prices are now sustainable with no further hikes beyond the taken ones, and debt is on a schedule to be cleared around FY29 with no major capex beyond maintenance.

segments.name: MDF
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 1,456 mn (+17.2% YoY), EBITDA INR 123 mn (8.4%). India revenue INR 1,447 mn (+32.9%), India volume 52,162 CBM (+16.1%), realisation INR 27,736/CBM (+14.4%). Capacity utilisation 66% after the April maintenance shutdown; exports subdued at ~255 CBM.

segments.name: Laminate (total)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 736 mn (+65.3%): India INR 251 mn (+60.6%), export INR 485 mn (+67.9%). Volume ~8.8 lakh sheets (+27.9%), blended realisation INR 836/sheet (+29.3%). EBITDA INR 52 mn (7%).

segments.name: Jumbo laminate
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 110 mn (+25% YoY), volume ~1.13 lakh sheets (+20.4%), EBITDA INR 23 mn (20.6%). Management puts utilisation at 29% on a 1 mm-equivalent basis against 28 lakh sheets capacity.

segments.name: PVC / MDF retail
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 96 mn (+13.1% YoY), volume +6.9%, EBITDA INR 8 mn (7.9% margin).

guidance_outlook: Jumbo laminate utilisation aspiration: ~50-55% in FY27 and 70-75% next year; ~60% utilisation would give ~INR 75 cr revenue, 90% ~INR 140 cr (Phase 1 + Phase 2).

Management expects Jumbo margins to be maintained through the year; existing laminate normal margin cited at 9-10%, combined laminate margin expected above 10% once Jumbo ramps, subject to chemical and war uncertainty.
Consolidated EBITDA margin target of 10-12%; management said realistically 1-2 quarters more to reach it.
MDF utilisation for FY27 expected to exceed FY26's ~75%; internal targets of 50% volume and 60% value from value-added products.
Debt including working capital ~INR 260 cr; scheduled repayment ~INR 55 cr per year, expected to be debt-free around Q2 FY29; only INR 5-10 cr operational capex planned in FY27.
Current MDF exports running at ~3,200 CBM in July vs 4,000-5,000 CBM per month last year; no revenue guidance given for FY27.
capex_capacity: Jumbo laminate capacity 28 lakh sheets (1 mm basis); capex ~INR 90 cr; management cites asset turn ~1.4-1.5x at full potential.
Jumbo utilisation 29% currently, aspiration 55-60% in FY27 (per call; reconcile with 50-55% stated later), 70-75% next year.
MDF capacity utilisation 66% in Q1 FY27 vs 83% in Q4 FY26 (April planned shutdown); FY26 full year ~75%.
Laminate plant had a single-boiler constraint after Jumbo capacity was added in one plant, reducing output in Q1.
No major capex beyond maintenance; operational capex INR 5-10 cr in FY27.
Entered two new export markets (Honduras, Greece); added 15 distributors and 46 retailers/dealers in Q1.
demand_pricing: MDF industry growing at ~20% CAGR; management says ~800 CBM/day of new capacity can be absorbed, but new capacity (organised and unorganised) is adding competition in domestic market.
MDF price hike of ~15% taken and sustained with no discounts; no further hikes after that. Laminate ~10% hike (taken in Q4 FY26) covering inflation; no further hikes.
Resin prices up ~35-40% vs pre-war; wood prices flat; resin easing in July described as 'very marginal'.
MDF OEM share 35-40% of domestic volume; OEM and retail prices currently the same; no fixed-price long-term OEM contracts.
Export MDF held back by container shortage and high freight; orders in hand but customers must approve higher freight before shipment.
Thailand and Vietnam are supplying the West Asia/export demand; 8-10 overseas factories have BIS licences, but no significant imports into India yet.
Laminate domestic volume growth 15-20%; export growth from new Far East customers.

qa_highlights.question: What is the MDF OEM vs retail split and how did it move in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: OEM is 35-40% of domestic volume, rest via distribution and retail; the mix in Q1 was the same as Q4 per management.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Jumbo laminate utilisation and capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation is 29% on a 1 mm-equivalent basis; capex was ~INR 90 cr for 28 lakh sheets; full-potential revenue ~INR 140 cr at 90% utilisation.

qa_highlights.question: Why did MDF volume stay flat YoY and why were exports low?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited the planned April shutdown, elevated chemical prices causing buyers to hold back, and West Asia disruption; exports were ~255 CBM due to container shortage and high freight.

qa_highlights.question: Will further price hikes be taken to offset input inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no hikes beyond 15% (MDF) and 10% (laminate); market will not accept more, so no guidance on further hikes.

qa_highlights.question: When will the consolidated EBITDA margin reach 10-12%?
qa_highlights.answer: Aspiration is this quarter, but realistically 1-2 quarters more.

qa_highlights.question: What is the path to full potential revenue (~INR 1,100 cr)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no FY27 revenue guidance; said laminate normal turnover ~INR 200 cr could reach INR 250 cr and Jumbo will take time, with no guidance given for the total.

risks_watch: Input cost pressure: resin up ~35-40% vs pre-war with only 'very marginal' easing in July; management says the market will not accept further price hikes, so margin recovery depends on resin and chemical prices.
Export volumes: MDF exports ~255 CBM in Q1 and ~3,200 CBM in July vs 4,000-5,000 CBM per month last year, held back by container shortage, high freight and West Asia shipping disruption.

Domestic MDF oversupply: new organised and unorganised capacity adding competition; an analyst raised possible inventory loss if raw material stays elevated and oversupply persists, and management replied 'Maybe yes'.
Jumbo laminate ramp-up: utilisation 29% on a 1 mm-equivalent basis vs 50-55% (or 55-60%) aspiration for FY27; new export markets need certifications and multi-year contracts, so timing is uncertain.
Consolidated EBITDA margin target of 10-12%: management said realistically 1-2 quarters more; laminate normal margin fell to about 5% in Q1 vs 9-10% historically.

Watch Q2 FY27 for MDF utilisation recovery from 66%, laminate margin recovery, whether the 15% MDF and 10% laminate price hikes hold without discounts, and the debt reduction pace (~INR 18 cr repaid in Q1).
key_quotes: So yes, we don't see any negative side of pricing going at this point of time. The prices, you can say, is more sustainable at this point of time.
Now we have done a single boiler unit. So that also was one of the reasons why the production was also less.
But realistically, yes, we may take 1 or 2 quarters more to reach up to that level.
So considering the schedule which we have been given by the banks and the financial institutions, approximately Q2 FY29, we will be able to clear our debt.

rows.why: Two new export markets were entered in Q1 with 15 distributors and 46 retailers/dealers added, though new Far East customers and certifications need time to convert.

533470|2026-09.headline: Rushil Decor Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 25.3% YoY to Rs 2,953 mn, a record, with PAT up 96.6% to Rs 101 mn.
533470|2026-09.overview: Management reported record quarterly revenue for both the laminate and MDF segments in Q2 FY27, with consolidated EBITDA up 24.5% YoY to Rs 280 mn at a 9.5% margin. Jumbo Laminates scaled up sharply, with revenue up 97.3% QoQ to Rs 217 mn and a 19.4% EBITDA margin, while MDF capacity utilisation rose to 87% from 66% in Q1 with no exports. Management said blended laminate margins are under pressure from raw material and freight costs, with a laminate price hike taken after 10 October 2026. Capex guidance is limited to Rs 15-20 crore from internal accruals, and management has not yet decided on any fresh expansion.

segments.name: MDF
segments.commentary: Q2 FY27 revenue Rs 1,962 mn (+15.8% YoY, record) with EBITDA Rs 194 mn (+6% YoY, margin about 9.9%); India MDF revenue +41% YoY and no exports in the quarter. H1 revenue Rs 3,418 mn (+16.4%), EBITDA Rs 317 mn at 9.3% margin vs 3.7% in H1 FY26.

segments.name: Laminates (total)
segments.commentary: Q2 FY27 revenue Rs 884 mn (+61.7% YoY, record), with India Rs 404 mn (+82.1%) and exports Rs 480 mn (+47.7%); volume about 10.4 lakh sheets (+32.8%); blended realisation Rs 847/sheet (+21.7%). EBITDA Rs 85 mn (margin 9.6% vs 7.7%). H1 revenue Rs 1,622 mn (+63.3%), EBITDA Rs 137 mn (8.4% margin).

segments.name: Jumbo Laminates
segments.commentary: Q2 FY27 revenue Rs 217 mn (+97.3% QoQ), volumes more than tripled QoQ; EBITDA Rs 42 mn (vs Rs 23 mn in Q1), margin 19.4%. Capacity utilisation 41%.

segments.name: PVC
segments.commentary: Q2 FY27 revenue Rs 103 mn (+14.3% YoY), volume +11.8%, realisation +2.3%; EBITDA Rs 2 mn (2.4% margin). H1 revenue Rs 200 mn (+13.7%), EBITDA Rs 10 mn (5.1% margin).

guidance_outlook: FY27 full-year performance expected to be better than H1; no quantified revenue or EBITDA guidance given, and no FY28 guidance.
Management commits to a 12-14% EBITDA margin for the laminate business as a whole once utilisation rises; current blended laminate margin is about 10% (about 12% including Jumbo).
MDF capacity utilisation expected at 82-85% across FY27; targets of 50% of MDF volume and 60% of MDF revenue from value-added products during FY27 (H1: 44% and 55%).
Jumbo Laminates utilisation targeted at 80-85% by March 2027 (from 41%); management indicated Rs 80-100 crore annual Jumbo revenue is possible at that level.
Capex for FY27 limited to normal operational capex of about Rs 15-20 crore from internal accruals (about Rs 14 crore spent in H1).
Laminate price hike taken after 10 October 2026, which should flow into Q3.
capex_capacity: MDF capacity utilisation 87% in Q2 FY27 vs 66% in Q1; management expects 82-85% utilisation through FY27.
Jumbo Laminates utilisation 41% in Q2 FY27; target 80-85% by March 2027.

Management is reviewing a possible fresh capex for MDF or Jumbo Laminates for FY28-FY29; no decision yet, with an announcement possible around end of Q3 FY27. Brownfield lead time for the main machine is about 8 months.
Management hopes laminate becomes at least equal in size to MDF within a couple of years.
demand_pricing: MDF domestic realisation fell about 7% QoQ, attributed to raw material volatility, price pressure and 5-10% competition; management said domestic competition will keep pressure on pricing for one more quarter.

Export of MDF paused amid western-world tensions and high freight (ocean freight cited at about USD 8,000 vs USD 800-900 earlier); strategy is calibrated, with a return to exports once freight normalises.
BIS certification on imports and high freight are cited as reducing MDF import threat; China not seen as a major threat, with Malaysia, Vietnam, Thailand and Indonesia cited as past threats.

Jumbo Laminates is mostly contract-based, with orders signed for Q3 and Q4 FY27; exports to 63 countries (up from 52-54), focus on Europe, Russia and Southeast Asia; Jumbo shipments largely FOB vs CIF for regular laminates.
Distribution expansion in Q2: 8 new direct distributors and 27 dealers added; OEM share about 40% of capacity utilisation, trade and retail about 60%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did MDF realisation fall QoQ and YoY despite value-added mix and a 15% price hike?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited H1 realisation of about Rs 26,600/tonne-equivalent and said YoY improvement reflects the prior-year fire at the Andhra Pradesh plant; the QoQ fall was due to volatile chemical prices, price pressure and 5-10% competition.

qa_highlights.question: What is the full-year capex plan?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said no specific additional capex beyond normal operational capex, about Rs 15-20 crore in total from internal accruals; about Rs 14 crore already spent in H1.

qa_highlights.question: Can Jumbo Laminates reach Rs 80-100 crore revenue at full utilisation with 20%+ margins?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said at 80-85% utilisation it can be Rs 80 crore or Rs 100 crore-plus depending on product mix. CEO said laminate margins will move to 12-14% as utilisation rises; freight costs are a current drag.

qa_highlights.question: Why has non-Jumbo laminate margin fallen to about 6-7%?
qa_highlights.answer: Higher raw material prices and a price hike only taken after 10 October 2026 (in Q3). Management called the current cost environment a new normal and said laminate as a whole is at 10% margin (12% including Jumbo).

qa_highlights.question: Is there a plan for fresh capex in FY28-FY29?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is still reviewing options, including greenfield or brownfield, and will announce something around the end of the quarter once utilisation data is in.

qa_highlights.question: Is any FY27 revenue or EBITDA guidance available?
qa_highlights.answer: No quantified guidance. Management said FY27 will be better than H1, and declined FY28 guidance.

risks_watch: Raw material and freight cost volatility (chemicals and ocean freight) compressing laminate and MDF margins.
MDF pricing pressure from domestic competition; realisation fell about 7% QoQ in Q2.
Dependence on domestic MDF with no exports; export restart depends on freight normalisation.
Jumbo Laminates utilisation ramp from 41% to 80-85% by March 2027; contract visibility for Q3-Q4 only.
Net debt rising to Rs 2,715 mn; payables days fell from 189 to 157, which could pressure working capital.
Pending capex decision for FY28-FY29 that could raise leverage.
