533519|2026-03.headline: L&T Finance posted record FY26 PAT of ₹3,003 Cr (pre one-time Labour Code hit) and Q4 PAT of ₹807 Cr, up 27% YoY, with credit costs down to 2.64%.
533519|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 was marked by record retail disbursements of ₹24,107 Cr (up 62% YoY) and Q4 PAT of ₹807 Cr (up 27% YoY). Consolidated NIMs+Fees rose to 10.47% and credit costs moderated to 2.64%, down 19 bps QoQ. Management launched Lakshya 2031 with targets of 20%+ book CAGR, credit costs below 2%, RoA 3.0-3.2% and RoE 16-18%, and guided FY27 credit costs of 2-2.2% by Q4 FY27. An ECL model refresh released ₹301 Cr of Stage 3 overlays into Stage 1 with no P&L impact, lifting Stage 1 coverage to 0.80%.

segments.name: Farmer Finance
segments.commentary: Q4 disbursements ₹2,037 Cr (up 16% YoY); FY26 ₹8,674 Cr (up 9%); book ₹16,970 Cr (up 12% YoY).

segments.name: Urban Finance (total)

qa_highlights.question: How exposed is the book to the West Asia conflict (SME, personal loans, rural, tractor, two-wheeler), and is the 20%+ FY27 AUM growth guidance inclusive of these risks?
qa_highlights.answer: No visible West Asia impact yet on SME, Rural Business Finance, tractor or two-wheeler portfolios; caution on Kharif fertiliser supply and urban unsecured lending. 20%+ AUM growth guidance stands but excludes unforeseen later geopolitical shocks.

qa_highlights.question: What are the near-term and Lakshya 2031 cost ratio expectations, and how was the ECL refresh's contingency buffer treated?
qa_highlights.answer: Opex to book guided at 3.75%-4% over Lakshya, reflecting tech and branch investment. Management said the ₹125 Cr macro-prudential provision was subsumed into the ECL model (Stage 1 and 2), not released, and that it will keep building macro-prudential provisions as needed.

qa_highlights.question: Why is fee income tepid relative to disbursement growth, and will it grow in line with AUM?
qa_highlights.answer: Fee income is about 1.7%-1.9% of assets and is range-bound; liquidity income and negative carry sit in interest cost, not MTM. Management guides to the combined NIMs+Fees range of 10%-10.5% rather than standalone fees.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Stage 1 provision at 80 bps apply to incremental FY27 book, and does it change the FY27 credit cost outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, new Stage 1 build-up will be provided at 80 bps as a permanent assumption change. Management said the FY27 credit cost outlook of 2%-2.2% is unchanged because lower roll-forwards should more than offset higher provisioning on book growth.

qa_highlights.question: Is the sub-2% credit cost under Lakshya 2031 driven by product mix or by Cyclops, and when does it arrive?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly Cyclops-driven customer selection, applied first to two-wheeler, tractor and SME. Management is confident of reaching 2% or below sometime in FY28, but could not pinpoint the quarter. Two-wheeler prime share is about 90%, up from 65%, and monthly originations rose from ₹650 Cr to about ₹1,000 Cr.

qa_highlights.question: Are disbursement yields above portfolio yields, and what drives yield improvement?
qa_highlights.answer: Disbursement yields are higher than portfolio yields. Personal loan yields are 2%-2.5 pp above the industry salaried average. Two-wheeler industry yields are 16%-18%. Yield improvement is coming from mix shift: home loan to LAP mix moved from about 80/20 to 55/45, with gold, micro-LAP and PL accelerating.

risks_watch: West Asia conflict: possible fertiliser supply constraint for Kharif, industrial gas tightness hitting SMEs, and higher oil prices pressuring urban unsecured lending (PL and SME).
El Niño risk to the monsoon and rural yields, with knock-on effects on Rural Business Finance and Farmer Finance.
ECL: Stage 1 provisioning now at 80 bps, with PCR on Stage 3 falling to 68% from 73%; further ECL recalibration possible in September 2026 or March 2027, and overlays remain in Stage 3.
Credit cost path: 2.64% in Q4 FY26 must fall to 2%-2.2% by Q4 FY27; Cyclops benefits are early (10-month window, ~₹3,250 Cr book) and not yet seasoned.
SR and wholesale book: ~₹7,000 Cr (₹4,808 Cr SR plus ₹2,220 Cr wholesale) still to resolve over 3-4 years; SR provision cover at 64%. Resolution gains are excluded from RoA/RoE targets.

533519|2026-06.headline: L&T Finance posted record Q1 FY27 PAT of ₹902 Cr (up 29% YoY) with RoA of 2.48% and credit cost easing to 2.54%.
533519|2026-06.overview: Consolidated PAT hit a record ₹902 Cr, up 29% YoY, while the consolidated book reached ₹1,29,634 Cr, up 27% YoY. Retail disbursements were ₹23,852 Cr, up 36% YoY, though management said it deliberately let go of about ₹1,000–1,200 Cr of potential disbursements to protect asset quality. Credit cost moderated 10 bps sequentially to 2.54%, and NIMs + Fees was flat QoQ at 10.47%, with NIM down 24 bps offset by higher fee and other income. Management reiterated Lakshya 2031 targets (RoA 3.0–3.2%, RoE 16–18%, credit cost ≤2% over the period) and set a near-term 2.8% RoA goal for Q4 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why did NIM fall while fee and other income rose, and is the NIMs + Fees trajectory sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Sachinn Joshi said NIM fell 24 bps to 8.54% as debt-equity rose to 3.97x from 3.73x and surplus liquidity of ~₹4,200 Cr was held; yields rose 1 bp. Surplus income was booked in fee and other income, so NIMs + Fees stayed at 10.47%.

qa_highlights.question: What guardrails govern Personal loan growth, and why were SME and Gold disbursements slower?
qa_highlights.answer: Sudipta Roy said PL is predominantly salaried, with Cyclops and credit parameters improving each quarter; the high growth reflects a low base. SME was cut in some cohorts due to West Asia war concerns; Gold origination fell in April on new RBI tiered-loan guardrails, with recovery in May–June.

qa_highlights.question: How will cost of funds move, and what is the funding strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects Q2 up 5–7 bps and FY27 WACB of 7.35–7.40% vs 7.35% in FY26. Liquidity was cut to ~₹9,000 Cr at quarter end; PSL and domestic borrowing remain the main sources, with international funding deferred for now.

qa_highlights.question: How will the ~80 bps RoA gap to Lakshya be closed, and what is the insurance commission risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Sudipta Roy said ~20 bps comes from ARC drag fading over 2–3 years, 30–40 bps from credit and credit-administration cost, and a small part from expansion. Insurance commission changes were called an industry-wide issue; payments revenue expected only after 2–2.5 years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the El Nino and monsoon risk to rural portfolio and asset quality?
qa_highlights.answer: Sudipta Roy said rainfall was ~14% below normal as of 10 July, versus an IMD projection of ~10% deficit, with reservoirs at acceptable levels outside a few South India locations. He sees the worries as overdone, citing microfinance deleveraging from ₹4.4 lakh Cr to ₹3.3 lakh Cr.

qa_highlights.question: Is the wholesale GS3 increase a risk to credit cost, and what is the SR/ARC position?
qa_highlights.answer: Sachinn Joshi said the small GS3 rise is a settlement transition already provided for and will reverse next quarter; the rest of the wholesale book (~₹2,000 Cr) is standard. SR PCR rose to 68% from 58%; credit cost guidance excludes wholesale slippage.

qa_highlights.question: How much AI spend is variable, and what is the opex trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Management could not give the variable AI share on the call and offered to follow up offline. Head-count efficiencies are expected to show in FY29–FY30, with the next two to three quarters not very sharp.

Monsoon and El Nino effects on Farmer and Tractor portfolios, and on rural collections.

Management said the mix shift away from Microfinance (grew ~5% when market de-grew) and towards Micro LAP, PL, Gold, and SME should keep yields up.
Cost of funds: CPs rose from about 5% to 8% of mix; PSL share fell from 26% to about 23%; PTCs about 5% at cheap rates; base cost now 6.95%, first time below 7%.
Fee and other income dipped QoQ because about ₹4,000 Cr of excess Q1 liquidity earned lower income; normal range is 180-185 bps, and liquidity was 20-22 bps lower this quarter.

qa_highlights.question: How will the repo rate hike be passed through, and what repricing exposure exists?

qa_highlights.question: Is the IRDAI commission consultation a risk to the 3% RoA target, and what offsets exist?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the impact is not quantified and the draft is under discussion; SRO FIDC is engaging the regulator for a glide path. Offsets cited include cross-sell via Hercules, PPI and payments fee income, and a one-to-one retail insurance channel accelerating in H2.

qa_highlights.question: What is the exposure to drought-affected states and rural underwriting changes?
qa_highlights.answer: Drought-declared-area book is about ₹1,033 Cr (3.3% of ₹31,500 Cr rural group and business loan book). Guardrails tightened in those districts; no visible risk build-up per management.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Two-Wheeler collection efficiency dip in September?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it was an AI-based self-cure experiment (self-cure about 43%, targeting 50%-55%) that overshot; October recovered to about 99%, and it is not structural.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Personal Loan run rate and outlook after the sequential flattening?
qa_highlights.answer: Monthly run rate is ₹1,400-1,500 Cr, with interim target of ₹1,700-1,800 Cr; onboarding a new partner now takes 3-4 months versus 2 months earlier, and one large partner remains to migrate.

qa_highlights.question: Is there gold loan stress such as GS2 formation or bullet-loan delinquency?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said collections are business as usual; about 15 months in, no loss episode; auctions recovered over 140% of dues. Early delinquency seen only in recent bullet-loan cohorts, per RBI LTV norms effective 1 April.

533520|2026-03.headline: Indiabulls FY26 PAT of INR346 crores; Q4 FY26 PAT INR195 crores (INR194.26 crores per correction) led by first real estate revenue recognition.

Management said Q4 was the first quarter of real estate revenue recognition in the books and that the group has exited digital lending and e-commerce after merging 17 group entities. The company now runs two verticals, real estate and financial services, with real estate expected to deliver about 80% of group profit. Management guided real estate profits to at least double in FY27 and triple in FY28, though it declined quarterly guidance. segments.commentary: Treated as an investment, not a P&L business; stake acquired about 6 months earlier at a $30 million valuation, with about $100 million of disbursals reported by the company.

Q4 consolidated gross contribution margin fell about 3 points below the 33-34% historical average because of a one-off Turkey contract penalty after components shipped from India were delayed about 1.5 months. 533758|2026-03.headline: APL Apollo Q4 FY26: EBITDA per ton above INR5,500 on lower volumes, while management holds FY27 guidance of 15-20% volume and 20-25% EBITDA growth.
533758|2026-03.overview: Management said Q4 FY26 volume rose 9% YoY and EBITDA per ton ran above INR5,500, with FY26 ROCE at 37% and free cash flow of INR13 billion. Volumes softened from late February after the Middle East crisis, due to steel and gas shortages, labour shortages and channel destocking, and April was slow at about 2.5 lakh tons. Management prioritised margin over volume and said full-year absolute EBITDA targets are unchanged. Net cash rose to about INR1,510 crore by end-March, aided by inventory reduction and better creditor terms.

financial_highlights.value: Above INR5,500/ton (Q4); Devarshi Jani cited INR5,525/ton
financial_highlights.change: Above the INR5,300-5,500 guided in Q3 call

Absolute FY26 EBITDA target to be protected; management is not reducing guidance.

Market share gains expected from disruption hurting smaller players; management says strong players benefit more if disruption exceeds four months.

qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Gupta said it is too early to separate destocking from demand slowdown; yearly volume and profitability targets are intact, with focus on margin over volume.

qa_highlights.question: Can EBITDA per ton of INR5,500 be sustained given Patra pressure and Dubai weakness?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited market leadership, product innovation and steel shortage; INR5,000-5,500 is a two-year track record, INR6,000+ is uncertain.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 capex and capital allocation plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex around INR500-600 crore per year; INR1,400-1,500 crore pending for 8 million tons, completed in 2-2.5 years. After about INR500 crore of liabilities are cleared, cash may go to dividend or buyback.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the EBITDA per ton gap versus value-added mix falling to 25% in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Anubhav Gupta said the general-segment spread rose to INR3,500+/ton from about INR2,000 on the brand premium and the January 2025 price hike, plus cost rationalisation.

qa_highlights.question: Has the company gained share in the disruption and how will it use its balance sheet?
qa_highlights.answer: Market share rose to 65% in FY26 from 55%; capex is self-funded, with two East India plants, Malur 2 and more SKU and branding spend.

533758|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 volume fell ~20% QoQ to 745,000 tons, but EBITDA per ton held near INR5,500 and management reiterates 20% FY27 absolute EBITDA growth.
533758|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 volume of 745,000 tons was below expectations, down roughly 20% QoQ, driven by the UAE disruption (about 25,000 tons lost QoQ), weak SG Premium volumes against secondary steel, an energy crisis hitting rust-proof pipes and roofing (25,000-30,000 tons), and destocking after steel prices rose. Gross profit per ton rose INR1,000 QoQ as management held prices, and EBITDA per ton was flat at above INR5,500. Management says July volumes were up about 20% MoM at over 300,000 tons, and it reiterated 15-20% volume growth and above 20% absolute EBITDA growth for FY27. Working capital days remain below zero and cash was about INR14 billion at June end versus INR15 billion in March 2026.

segments.name: Apollo branded products
segments.commentary: Management targets EBITDA of INR6,000-7,000/ton for Apollo and roofing products combined; the company is at that range currently. Primary and secondary volumes were hit by high prices and channel destocking.

segments.name: SG Premium
segments.commentary: Priced about 6-7% below APL Apollo brand at around INR58,000/ton; EBITDA spread INR0-1,000/ton depending on micro-market. Volumes fell due to the primary-secondary price gap (INR10-12/kg currently).

segments.name: UAE operations
segments.commentary: Dubai volumes fell to 5,000-6,000 tons/month during the disruption; July output was 10,000-12,000 tons, with a target of 16,000-17,000 tons in August and 24,000-25,000 tons in September. About 70,000 tons of inventory is in transit, but raw material for 70,000 tons is not yet lined up. Management expects UAE EBITDA to reach INR5,000-6,000/ton if ramp-up succeeds.

segments.name: Roofing products
segments.commentary: Hit by the energy crisis in India (25,000-30,000 tons lost). Management says roofing EBITDA is currently INR6,000-7,000/ton, with a roofing line starting in APL adding about 20,000 tons of ramped-up volume.

capex_capacity: Total capex plan of 7 million tons. Gorakhpur 200,000 tons (start around September 2026), Siliguri 300,000 tons (Q4 FY27), Malur about 1 million tons (July-October 2027), a 0.5 million ton plant in Maharashtra or North Karnataka, plus 1 million tons from debottlenecking.
The Bhuj plant was dropped; the Mumbai plant is being shifted fully to exports. A new 500,000-ton plant near the Pune corridor is planned to cut freight to INR200-300/ton from INR1,100-1,200/ton.
Current capacity is about 5 million tons, with full operation targeted in Q4 FY27.
Solar segment: management expects 4-5% of total volume from solar products within 2-3 years, versus a low current contribution.
demand_pricing: Q1 disruption drivers: UAE loss (~25,000 tons QoQ), SG Premium share loss to secondary steel, energy crisis in India, and destocking by channel partners after steel prices rose INR7,000-8,000/ton in Q4 FY26.
July demand recovered as the price correction ended; dealers returned to normal stock positions and July volume was over 300,000 tons (about 20% MoM).
Pricing: management says it held prices, passing on steel price increases plus INR100-200/ton. Price cuts of INR100-200/ton were applied to about 15-20% of the portfolio to gain volume.

Primary steel capacity additions (Lloyd, AM/NS, JSW, Tata, JSPL) are expected to narrow the primary-secondary gap over 1-3 quarters.
PEB segment: about 20% of PEB structure weight is steel pipe; APL holds a 65-70% share with large PEB players.

qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated 15-20% volume growth and 20%+ EBITDA growth; 15% is considered confident, and 20% needs tailwinds.

qa_highlights.question: What is the UAE outlook and how will the company participate in reconstruction demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Dubai volume recovered to 10,000-12,000 tons in July, with a target of 24,000-25,000 tons in September. About 70,000 tons of inventory is in transit, but raw material for 70,000 tons is not yet lined up.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBITDA per ton path beyond FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Spreads expected to be INR5,000-5,500/ton in FY27, improving INR100-200/ton a year, with a target of INR6,000/ton at 8 million tons in 2-3 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA per ton rise YoY despite lower volume?
qa_highlights.answer: The January 2025 repositioning of APL Apollo brand raised prices by about INR500/ton, which lifted spreads from Q4 FY25 through FY26 and into Q1 FY27.

533758|2026-09.headline: APL Apollo Q2 FY27 volume hit 960,000 tons with EBITDA near Rs 6,000/ton; management guides FY27 EBITDA up 20%, with the 15% volume target conditional on Dubai and steel supply.
533758|2026-09.overview: Management called Q2 FY27 its best quarter on volume, EBITDA and net profit, with volume of 960,000 tons despite UAE operations being disrupted, steel shortages in the domestic market and container disruption affecting exports. Growth came from the APL Apollo brand and roofing sheets, where pricing and EBITDA spreads improved, while low-margin SG Premium and export volumes were deliberately not pursued. Management guided FY27 EBITDA growth of about 20% on an absolute basis and said Q2 EBITDA per ton of about Rs 6,000 is sustainable. Working capital days were stated as zero, and cash rose 15% QoQ to Rs 16 billion. Several answers on Dubai, SG Premium and volume guidance were non-committal.

segments.name: APL Apollo brand
segments.commentary: Management says brand products get better pricing and EBITDA spreads; APL Apollo and roofing volume grew about 20% YoY in H1, with double-digit growth expected in H2. Analysts were told the brand targets 15-20% YoY growth.

segments.name: Roofing sheets
segments.commentary: Capacity cited at 7 lakh tons per year (about 175,000 tons per quarter); Q1 volume was about 135,000 tons and the target for the current quarter is 175,000 tons. Mix is 50% housing, 25% commercial/industrial and 25% other industrial; thickness 0.4-3.5 mm; no commission paid to third parties.

segments.name: SG Premium
segments.commentary: Low-margin product; management declined to give volume guidance due to steel shortage and low margin. Management said it can sell about 200,000 tons if steel prices fall and that absolute EBITDA would rise as volume increases.

segments.name: UAE (Dubai) operations
segments.commentary: Volume at about 40% of past levels; current run rate about 100,000 tons per year against about 300,000 tons capacity. Brownfield expansion to about 500,000 tons by March 2027, with EBITDA of Rs 8,000-10,000/ton expected on new mills. Management says no losses there.

segments.name: Defence, aerospace and specialised tubes
segments.commentary: New specialised tube mill can produce up to 250x250 mm with 16 mm thickness; samples sent to agencies, with results expected in 2-3 months. Development items for ISRO and DRDO are in progress.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA growth of about 20% on an absolute basis by March 2027; management says it may beat this if UAE operations recover in H2. Management said absolute EBITDA should cross Rs 2,200 crore this year (one analyst cited Rs 2,200-2,300 crore; Shaleen Kumar's Rs 2,400 crore reference was given by management as possible if Dubai performed).

Apollo brand and roofing volume growth of about 15% for FY27 (about double-digit in H2); management also cited 15-20% YoY growth for these two segments. Company-wide volume guidance not committed due to Dubai and SG Premium uncertainty.
Q3 FY27 EBITDA per ton expected to be above Rs 6,000; October described as good and above guidance.

Management said FY28 EBITDA could reach about Rs 2,500 crore; in response to an analyst's Rs 3,000 crore scenario, management agreed it is achievable if Dubai, domestic steel supply and container freight stabilise. Management said that if it targets Rs 6,000-6,500/ton, it will update guidance after another quarter of evidence.
Capex target of 7 million tons greenfield plus brownfield capacity and 1 million tons de-bottlenecking within two years. Capex outflow in H2 expected to be about Rs 200 crore.
Net cash of about Rs 1,600 crore expected to rise to about Rs 2,300 crore; Rs 200-300 crore of this is earmarked for capex, and management will decide the use of the remainder later.
capex_capacity: Target of 7 million tons greenfield plus brownfield capacity and 1 million tons de-bottlenecking within the next two years (per management).
Current run-rate of 960,000 tons per quarter; utilisation about 70-75%.
Dubai capacity about 300,000 tons, rising to about 500,000 tons by March 2027 with two new mills; run-rate about 100,000 tons per year.
H1 FY27 capex Rs 400 crore; H2 capex expected to be low (about Rs 200 crore).
Greenfield additions described as small, limiting fixed-cost impact; brownfield expansion said not to hurt existing fixed costs materially.
demand_pricing: Management said demand for APL Apollo and roofing remains strong, with no decline seen, and that order books are full despite higher steel prices causing customers to delay quotations.
Pricing: black pipe price cited at about Rs 70,000/ton vs competitors at Rs 68,000-70,000; HR coil about Rs 60,000/ton; conversion cost about Rs 10/kg; worst item margin about Rs 6,000/ton.
Discounts: July required higher discounts; August and September needed less. A demand-driven discount swing can move results by Rs 10-15 crore per quarter.
Management said steel plant shutdowns are causing shortages, with November also weak and volumes expected to recover to about 400,000 tons per month from December.

Management said Q2 margin expansion came from three sources: exiting non-profitable volumes, roofing capacity additions and cost/innovation. It declined to give product-level EBITDA; the disclosure has been discontinued.
Exports affected by very high container freight; UAE exports blocked.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revised FY27 volume guidance given H1 growth of about 4% vs an earlier 15%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 15% guidance holds for the Apollo brand and roofing, but company-wide volume guidance is not committed because of Dubai and steel shortage; low-margin volumes are being deliberately dropped.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other income fall QoQ, and why did the FD balance drop?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the other-income decline to FX gains and losses; the FD drop of about Rs 225 crore is due to reclassification of over-one-year FDs to within one year, and management said it would check the FX figure.

qa_highlights.question: How sustainable is Rs 6,000/ton EBITDA, and what if steel prices normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Rs 6,000/ton is sustainable, citing the exit from non-profitable business, roofing additions, cost savings and utilisation of 70-75%. Management said SG Premium growth would dilute per-ton margin but lift absolute EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: What explains the drop in GP per ton when mix has improved?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said light structures carry lower realisation and GP; GP per ton fell about Rs 500/ton QoQ, and light-structure mix was about 25% in Q2 per management (analyst noted 35%).

qa_highlights.question: What drove the large volume jump from Q1 to Q2 beyond roofing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to the APL Apollo brand, where the company shifted focus from SG Premium to Apollo branding and got better pricing, with Q3 seen as strong so far.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY28 EBITDA outlook, including Dubai recovery?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Rs 2,400 crore is achievable this year if Dubai performs, and agreed Rs 3,000 crore for FY28 is possible if Dubai, domestic steel supply and container freight stabilise.

qa_highlights.question: Will falling rainfall affect housing demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said housing demand remains intact; any impact would be 2-4% at most, and order books and enquiries are strong.

risks_watch: Dubai/UAE operations remain largely shut: run-rate about 100,000 tons vs about 500,000 tons capacity after expansion, and management cannot commit on timing.
Steel shortage and plant shutdowns; November expected to be weak, with recovery from December.

Freight and container disruption affecting exports; power cost at Rs 6.2-6.3/unit vs Rs 5 target.

533761|2026-03.headline: GPT Infra FY26 consolidated revenue rose 8.6% to INR1,290 crores, below guidance, while consolidated EBITDA grew 28.5% to INR174.2 crores; FY27 revenue growth guided at 27-30%.
533761|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 standalone revenue grew 1.3% YoY to INR373.9 crores, while consolidated revenue grew 8.9% to INR414.7 crores; management attributed the March shortfall to West Bengal elections and labour migration. Margins improved, with standalone Q4 EBITDA up 27% to INR53 crores at 14% margin and consolidated Q4 EBITDA up 53% to INR59.2 crores, helped by the Ghana factory. The Alcon signalling EPC acquisition (INR151.83 crores cash) closed in the quarter and is being merged into GPT Infra with an appointed date of April 1, 2026. Management guided FY27 revenue growth of 27-30%, order inflow of about INR3,000 crores and consolidated EBITDA margin of around 14%.

segments.name: Infrastructure
segments.commentary: Contributed more than 90% of FY26 revenue; key executing projects include Prayagraj Ganga Bridge, Kona Expressway and Raniganj. Alcon signalling will be reported within the infra line item.

segments.name: Concrete sleepers
segments.commentary: Management said the segment was profitable in FY26 on domestic demand and African operations. Q4 was loss-making in South Africa, Namibia and Ghana, which management attributed mainly to currency mark-to-market effects; Ghana production has started.

segments.name: Signalling (Alcon, acquired)
segments.commentary: Margin of about 20% vs 13-14% for traditional infra; FY27 revenue expected at INR120-130 crores. Order book is about INR90-100 crores; FY27 order inflow expected at INR150-200 crores against about INR500 crores of bids.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at 27-30%, subject to Middle East war-related economic headwinds; long-term revenue growth target above 20%.
FY27 order inflow guidance of about INR3,000 crores across infra, signalling and sleepers.
Consolidated EBITDA margin guided at about 14% for FY27, with long-term standalone and consolidated margin above 13%.
West Bengal catch-up expected: April subdued again due to elections, Q1 not fully caught up, but first half expected to recover the shortfall.
Average capex of about INR70-75 crores a year for the next couple of years including the HAM equity share of INR55-60 crores; equipment purchases of INR40-50 crores a year.
Alcon and GPT merger (appointed date April 1, 2026) expected to complete in FY27, subject to regulatory approvals.
capex_capacity: Acquired Alcon Builders and Engineers (New Delhi EPC signalling) for INR151.83 crores cash; wholly owned subsidiary from January 1, 2026.
First HAM contract (elevated bypass, Jodhpur, NHAI), contract value about INR669 crores; GPT holds 51% in the SPV, which is already incorporated.
Steel girder fabrication factory at Singur, West Bengal, started during the year with about 10,000 tonnes per annum capacity; further expansion under review.
Ghana facility commercially operational, with first supply and invoice raised in March 2026.
demand_pricing: Order inflow of INR2,422 crores in FY26, and about INR500 crores of Alcon signalling bids in the last two months; Alcon contracts of INR70-80 crores individually.

Major wins: Northern Railway rail-cum-road bridge over Ganga at Varanasi, INR1,201 crores total (GPT share 40%, about INR481 crores); MCGM LBS Marg flyover, INR1,805 crores total (JV share 26%, about INR470 crores).
Price escalation formulas in all contracts, linked to SAIL/RINL steel, WPI for cement and fuel; NHAI and MoRTH moved to monthly escalation payments and allowed a 4-month force majeure extension.
Management said about 40% of revenue comes from West Bengal, and migrant labour returning from there was disrupted in March and April.

qa_highlights.question: Why did contract assets rise from INR336 crores to about INR514 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about INR60-65 crores is from Alcon (retention, unbilled revenue, escalation), with the rest from EPC milestone-based billing; contract assets are typically 6-8 months old and are targeted to fall to 3-4 months of revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Where did the QIP proceeds go, given limited debt reduction?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said debt was cut by about INR125-130 crores from March 2024 to March 2025; FY26 debt rose on EPC working-capital drawdowns and internal accruals used for the Alcon purchase, with debt expected to return to the earlier level.

qa_highlights.question: Did West Bengal elections cause the revenue guidance miss, and does Alcon's INR140 crores contribute?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed March execution was hit by elections and labour migration; the Alcon contribution in FY26 was only Q4 numbers of about INR30 crores, since it was consolidated from January 1.

qa_highlights.question: Is labour back and is there execution risk to FY27 growth?
qa_highlights.answer: April was again subdued by elections, but May execution is strong and labour is back on site; new contracts won in December and January are expected to contribute heavily in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: How will raw material inflation from the war affect margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Contracts carry escalation formulas; NHAI now pays escalation monthly, so a lag is possible, but management expects full-year margins to be maintained.

qa_highlights.question: What are the capex plans and is Alcon consolidated separately?
qa_highlights.answer: Average capex about INR70-75 crores a year including the HAM share; Alcon is consolidated and, after the merger, will report within the infra segment rather than as a separate line.

risks_watch: Revenue growth of 27-30% in FY27 depends on recovering the March and April shortfall in the first half; April was subdued again by elections.
Middle East war effects on metal and fuel prices, currency and government payment timing; escalation may lag by a month.

Contract assets at about INR514 crores (consolidated) and debt increase in FY26 against the QIP deconsolidation narrative; working-capital conversion of 75-80% of contract assets in H1 FY27 is targeted.
Concrete sleeper segment losses in South Africa, Namibia and Ghana, driven by currency volatility.
Signalling order inflow of INR150-200 crores in FY27 against the INR500 crores of bids; execution of the Alcon merger subject to regulatory approvals.
Q4 revenue was 40% H2-weighted seasonality; management said it cannot be removed from the business.

The signaling business has a margin profile of almost 20% compared to the 13% / 14% for the traditional infra business that we were doing.

533761|2026-06.headline: GPT Infra Q1 FY27 standalone revenue fell 9% to INR282 crores on West Bengal labour disruption, while consolidated EBITDA margin rose to 15.7% on Alcon signalling.
533761|2026-06.overview: Standalone revenue declined 9% YoY to INR282 crores due to labour unavailability in West Bengal during April-May elections, which management says has since normalised. Consolidated revenue fell 3.4% to INR302 crores, but consolidated EBITDA rose 28.4% to INR47.5 crores (15.7% margin), helped by the Alcon signalling business and African operations. Management reiterated FY27 revenue growth of about 30% and raised its FY27 EBITDA margin expectation to 14-15%, with 13-14% as the long-term range. Order book stood at INR4,303 crores and Q1 order inflow was only about INR130 crores against a INR3,000 crore annual target.

segments.name: Infrastructure
segments.commentary: Largest contributor at INR283 crores in Q1, driven by railway bridges and road projects (NHAI Ganga Bridge Prayagraj, Rupnarayan Bridge Kolaghat, Kona Expressway).

segments.name: Sleeper
segments.commentary: INR19 crores revenue in Q1, supported by domestic demand, export orders from India to Bangladesh and international operations; management cites 14-15% sleeper margin.

segments.name: Alcon (signalling)
segments.commentary: Acquired Q4 FY26; contributed about INR20 crores in Q1 and management guides INR100-120 crores for FY27, implying roughly INR70-80 crores incremental YoY per management.

segments.name: Power EPC (new)
segments.commentary: Entered with a ~INR53 crore contract from Power Grid Corporation of India for a Kurnool, Andhra Pradesh project; targets INR150-200 crores annual revenue in the next couple of years.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth of approximately 30%, implying about INR1,700 crores total and roughly INR1,400 crores over Q2-Q4 (about INR150 crores per month).
FY27 EBITDA margin of 14-15%, 100-150 bps above the 13-14% long-term range, attributed to Alcon integration and better African operations.
FY27 order inflow target of INR3,000 crores; management said it expects to exceed this, as in FY26 (target INR2,000 crores, achieved INR2,400 crores).
Debt expected to reduce over FY27 with no net addition; debt-to-equity to move toward about 0.5x, partly funded by Alcon cash after merger.
Alcon to be merged into GPT Infra in ensuing quarters; African business expected to deliver strong inflows and a sizable South African order this quarter.

Alcon merger into GPT Infra expected in ensuing quarters, enabling bids for larger value contracts (INR1,500-2,000 crore EPC, 3-4 year execution).
Monsoon season in Q2 expected to affect execution pace.

Signalling bids of over INR500 crores submitted; under technical evaluation, none converted to orders yet. Company is not L1 in any contract currently.
Addressable market: Indian Railways outlay of about INR1 trillion over six years for signalling (Kavach, electronic interlocking, DDEI); ~USD1.5 billion market cited.
West Bengal: INR895 crores railway investments approved centrally and INR2,100 crores state connectivity projects announced, including Bhagirathi Bridge and Chingrighata-New Town Corridor.
Africa: concrete sleeper business in South Africa, Namibia and Ghana; new South African order expected in the current quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the 30% FY27 growth given Q1 was flat, and can 9M growth reach 40%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 was planned as flattish; the INR4,300 crore order book and some late-FY26 orders, with revenue from H2, support about INR1,400 crores over the balance nine months.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 margins stay at the long-term 13-14% after 15.7% in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided FY27 EBITDA margin at 14-15%, with long-term range unchanged at 13-14%; standalone Q1 margin was about 13.7%.

qa_highlights.question: Contract assets and cash conversion?
qa_highlights.answer: Contract assets were about INR430 crores at March end, up about 5%; around INR200 crores has since been billed and received. Q1 operating cash flow not disclosed; to be given in the September quarter or half-year.

qa_highlights.question: Debt position and plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt has not risen materially versus March; management expects to reduce debt over FY27 and targets debt-to-equity near 0.5x from about 0.65x.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the Q1 standalone execution slip and when does it recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Labour availability was affected for about half the quarter (April-May); workforce normalised from May, and management expects a monthly run rate of about INR150 crores.

qa_highlights.question: Alcon revenue contribution and signalling bid status?
qa_highlights.answer: Alcon contributed about INR20 crores in Q1 and is guided at INR100-120 crores for FY27; signalling bids worth over INR500 crores are under technical evaluation.

risks_watch: Execution ramp: FY27 30% growth needs about INR1,400 crores over Q2-Q4 versus INR282 crores standalone in Q1; monsoon season in Q2 adds risk.
Order inflow: Q1 inflow of about INR130 crores against INR3,000 crore annual target; order book fell from INR4,480 crores to INR4,300 crores.
Working capital: contract assets elevated, cash flow from operations weak in recent years; Q1 CFO not disclosed.
Alcon merger timing and integration, and conversion of over INR500 crores of signalling bids.
Power EPC: prior execution challenges in this segment; the new entry is small (INR53 crores) and margin target of 13-14% is unproven.
Subcontracting cost ratio moved from about 30% highs to about 20%; management says it depends on project cycle.

534091|2026-03.headline: MCX FY26 consolidated revenue more than doubled to INR2,302 crore and PAT crossed INR1,300 crore, with ADT up ~2.5x.

Average daily turnover across futures and options rose about 2.5 times, with bullion growing more than 4 times and energy growing strongly off a high base. Management said growth was both structural and cyclical, but declined to comment on April and May participation and said not every quarter will be a big jump over the prior quarter. Cost lines (product licence fees, other expenses, SGF contribution, software support) rose faster than revenue in Q4, and management said the focus is on efficiency rather than spending less.

534091|2026-06.headline: MCX Q1 FY27 total income rose 85% YoY to INR752 crores and PAT reached INR413 crores, though revenue fell sequentially from an exceptional Q4 FY26.
534091|2026-06.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 total income of INR752 crores (+85% YoY), revenue from operations of INR702 crores (+88% YoY), EBITDA of INR544 crores (about 72% margin) and PAT of INR413 crores. Management described Q1 as a consolidation after an exceptionally strong Q4 FY26, with ADT at INR10.5 lakh crores and futures ADT up 47% YoY. Bullion options premium ratio fell sharply as volatility normalised, while notional volumes rose, and management said bullion volumes were softer in the quarter. Management said the RBI bank guarantee rule (in force from July) is not expected to be significantly detrimental, and that it is more a Q2 issue.

534139|2026-03.headline: Schneider Electric Infrastructure Q4 FY26 sales were flat at INR590 crore as customers deferred dispatches; FY26 orders grew 27.4% and backlog rose about 50%.
534139|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 sales were roughly flat YoY at INR590 crore, with management attributing the shortfall to customers, mainly EPC contractors, asking to hold dispatches amid geopolitical disruption. Q4 profit margin fell to about 6%, with management citing roughly 2.5 percentage points of commodity impact from copper and aluminium up over 30% and steel up about 10% in FY26. Full-year FY26 orders grew 27.4%, sales 9.6% and profit before tax 10.1%, with backlog up about 50%. Q4 order intake was deliberately selective because customers resisted variable price clauses. Management gave no quantified guidance and declined to size data centre, BESS or market-share opportunities.

segments.name: Services and modernisation
segments.commentary: Services rose to about 15% of revenue per analyst framing; management said modernisation and retrofit margins are falling under L1-based competition.

Management said the company is exploring exports, including for data centre products; no order details given.
demand_pricing: Q4 order intake was low because the company was selective, booking only orders with variable price clauses that allow commodity pass-through; customers were reluctant to accept these.

Commodity hedging covers 50% to 60% of exposure; forex is hedged via order-by-order PO hedges and a net ARAP hedge.

Management said the company is not cost leader in BESS and competes on quality and advisory software.

534139|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 order intake hit a record INR 915 crore (+0.5% YoY, double-digit QoQ) but EBIT fell to INR 32 crore on gross margin pressure and negative operating leverage.
534139|2026-06.overview: Management reported a record quarterly order booking of INR 915 crore, with sales growing about 5% YoY in a seasonally soft Q1 and an order backlog of about INR 2,100 crore entering Q2, up around 33%. EBIT was INR 32 crore, lower than last year, as commodity inflation (copper, aluminium, steel, transformer wire) and legacy fixed-price contracts compressed gross margin, while employee and other costs rose faster than sales. Management attributed the margin dip largely to Q1 operating leverage and FX-driven import costs, and said pricing actions are underway but will take time to flow through. No numerical guidance was given; management said the balance three quarters should be good.

financial_highlights.change: +0.5% YoY; double-digit QoQ growth; highest-ever quarterly order booking
Dipped YoY due to commodity inflation and legacy fixed-price orders
Flat QoQ; YoY increase due to non-cash fair-value accounting gain in last year's Q1
Management cited ~1.9% figure tied to GM pressure and negative operating leverage

segments.name: Power & Grid
segments.commentary: Management said legacy margin pressure is concentrated in Power & Grid, where orders booked before December 2025 carry firm prices; secondary distribution equipment and transformers are mainly Power & Grid products.

segments.name: Emerging segments (data centres, semiconductors)
segments.commentary: Management said more than one-fifth of the order bank now comes from emerging segments; a semiconductor transformer order was described as the largest front-end fab order received, and a data-centre MV panel order was also won.

segments.name: Metals & Mining
segments.commentary: Management said traction is being seen with a healthy pipeline in the MMM segment, without quantification.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Export revenue is 10-12% of revenue; the new Kolkata plant is expected to cater to exports, which are only starting to ramp.

guidance_outlook: No numerical revenue or margin guidance given; management declined to give forward-looking figures for Q2 or FY27.
Management said Q2 is expected to do better than Q1 historically, and that the forward-looking three quarters are good for the company.
Pricing actions have been initiated across standard price-list products but will take time to fructify.
Capacity expansions across the Baroda medium-voltage plant, Baroda transformer plant and Kolkata plant are on track, with some completing in calendar 2027 and some in 2028, followed by ramp-up.
Management expects the commodity tailwinds to moderate and margin headwinds to iron out over time.
capex_capacity: Roughly INR 500 crore of capex deployed over the last three years across the company's three plants, aimed at capacity additions and cutting imports from other Schneider factories.
Kolkata plant began capitalisation and operations early in FY27; depreciation is rising and is expected to be accelerated by plant growth.
Multiple capex programmes (Baroda MV factory, Baroda transformer factory, Kolkata plant) have staggered completion timelines and ramp-up plans, all tracking to plan per management.
Company said it is aligned with government capex, including RDSS of about INR 3,00,000 crore, to address secondary distribution and transformer demand.
demand_pricing: Order intake of INR 915 crore was a record quarterly figure; management said Q1 order timing included spillover of 15-20% at times, varying quarter to quarter.
Commodity inflation (copper, aluminium, steel, labour) and INR depreciation of about 8% YTD are the key headwinds cited.
Legacy contracts booked before December 2025 are largely fixed-price; the company cannot always revise prices, hitting gross margin, mostly in Power & Grid.

Price variation clauses cover about 20-25% of the backlog, mainly large execution cycle projects over 6 months to 1 year; mandatory PVC is now being put into new contracts, but not in government tenders.
Imports are 10-15% of COGS, roughly matched by export revenue, providing a natural FX hedge.
Management said pipeline for Power & Grid is healthy, including private utility inquiries, and expects both volume growth and price increases.

qa_highlights.question: Is the margin miss driven by lack of operating leverage, and what is the outlook for other expenses growth of ~20% YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Q1 squeeze is a normal Q1 effect of annual salary increments and cost inflation from 1 April, combined with moderate sales growth of ~5%. Other expenses rose on FX and an 8-10% regular cost inflation; management expects it to even out over the year.

qa_highlights.question: Will you quantify FY27 revenue expectations given the backlog growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give numbers; said Q2 historically does better than Q1 and that the remaining three quarters look good, and that pricing actions are underway.

qa_highlights.question: Are legacy orders (pre-December) hurting margins, and how much of the backlog has price variation protection?
qa_highlights.answer: Pre-December orders are largely firm-price; about 20-25% of backlog has price variation clauses; new contracts now carry mandatory PVC except in government tenders where bids are price-fixed with validity.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Q1 order growth is fresh versus spillover from Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said spillover from March into April is normal, sometimes 15-20%, sometimes less; it could not quantify it precisely.

qa_highlights.question: What is the export share and medium-term target?
qa_highlights.answer: Exports are 10-12% of revenue; management declined to give a percentage target but said absolute export value will rise with the Kolkata plant.

qa_highlights.question: What is the addressable distribution (DISCOM) capex TAM and how selective are you?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company is selective, bidding only on strategic accounts with visible sites and lower execution ambiguity; it avoids underground cabling and substation civil work and focuses on equipment and grid modernisation within RDSS.

Rising INR depreciation (about 8% YTD) affects imported components and FX-linked other expenses.
Next quarter to monitor: EBIT recovery vs Rs 32 crore base, transactional vs systems revenue mix (management to provide from next quarter), and new capacity commissioning in Baroda and Kolkata.

534139|2026-09.headline: Schneider Electric Infrastructure H1 FY25 sales rose 20.3% to INR 1,193 crore and PAT 32.1% to INR 103 crore, with orders up 17.5% to INR 1,104 crore.
534139|2026-09.overview: H1 FY25 sales grew 20.3% YoY to INR 1,193 crore, driven by execution against backlog, with Q2 sales up 21% to INR 600 crore. Orders grew 17.5% to INR 1,104 crore in H1 and 16.3% to INR 572 crore in Q2, and closing backlog of INR 1,389 crore was up about 14%. Gross margin widened about 3 points to 39.5% in H1, but other expenses rose 38.8% on CSR, customer support and risk provisions, which held EBITDA growth to 44.2% and PAT growth to 32.1%. Q2 PAT of INR 54.3 crore included a INR 5.8 crore deferred tax reversal tied to the revised long-term capital gains tax rate.

qa_highlights.answer: Yes; RDSS (about INR 3 lakh crore investment) is a mainstay driver, though state-level political factors cause some deferments.

qa_highlights.answer: The factory is on track for start in the last quarter of this year, with furnace installation by Q1 next year; the impact on the 20% run rate could not be quantified.

qa_highlights.answer: Government is about 40% (plus/minus 5%) of business. H2 is historically stronger, as buyers push to receive equipment by March, but Q3 government ordering does not automatically translate into Q4 sales.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the strong cash flow and how is export and services performance?

534309|2026-06.headline: NBCC standalone Q1 FY27 EBITDA rose 62% to INR 160 crore (8.77% margin) on 10% revenue growth to INR 1,823 crore.
534309|2026-06.overview: Standalone revenue from operations grew 10% YoY to INR 1,823 crore, while EBITDA rose 62% to INR 160 crore and PAT rose 32% to INR 151 crore, helped by marketing fees from the Bharat Business Park sale. Consolidated revenue was INR 2,260 crore, with a consolidated order book of INR 1,27,000 crore and INR 1,600 crore of orders secured in the quarter. Management reiterated FY27 revenue guidance of INR 15,000-17,000 crore and expects INR 18,000-20,000 crore of new awards over the next 2-3 quarters, but several large awards (GPRA 5 colonies, J&K, MAHAPREIT, Supertech) have slipped repeatedly. Amrapali: about 8,800 units in total, with roughly 4,000-4,500 sold; management expects to sell about INR 4,000-5,000 crore of inventory.

Pipeline: Supertech tender to be floated this quarter (16 projects in Noida and Greater Noida, about INR 10,000 crore); J&K infrastructure tender of about INR 3,500-4,000 crore to be floated this month after an initial INR 100 crore package drew about 15 bidders; MAHAPREIT (about INR 25,000 crore) expected in Q3; Naveen Nagpur infrastructure tender after DPR approval.

Recent wins: Odisha schools INR 253 crore, J&K campus INR 171 crore, New AP Bhavan INR 106 crore (Q1); Seychelles housing about INR 620 crore, RBI Amravati about INR 780 crore, Rajasthan science labs about INR 431 crore (July-August).
International: Seychelles has awarded a further 1,000 houses after about 2,000 in Maldives; management cites prospects in Australia, Saudi Arabia and Fiji, none included in projections.

qa_highlights.question: Why are the large orders (about INR 50,000 crore GPRA 5 colonies plus other large orders) delayed, and when will they come? Is FY27 and FY28 revenue still on track?
qa_highlights.answer: GPRA 5 colonies (about INR 30,000 crore) has cleared the group of ministers and PIB and is with Cabinet; management says it is a matter of time. At least one or two contracts expected in Q2 and major ones in Q3. Management reiterated FY27 revenue guidance of INR 15,000-17,000 crore and said it is adhering to it.

qa_highlights.question: How will margins move over the next two to three quarters, and by how much?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins will rise because redevelopment and Amrapali contribute more than 60% of revenue. Guided EBITDA minimum 6.5-7% and PAT 6-6.5%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA rise sharply while work and consultancy expenses fell from INR 3,412 crore in Q4 FY26 to INR 1,536 crore in Q1 FY27 (standalone)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the jump to marketing fees from the Bharat Business Park sale, which carry low associated expenses. Further marketing fees are expected from Africa Avenue, Vinayak Mandir, Sarojini Nagar (7 GPRA) and 1% on Amrapali inventory sales of about INR 4,000-5,000 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why did standalone and PMC revenue growth look slow, and what are the FY27-FY29 targets?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited HSCC dropping a low-margin (about 2%) Maharashtra health project, costing about INR 300 crore of top line, and said Q1 is seasonally slow. Standalone FY27 revenue INR 13,000-14,000 crore; FY28 about INR 21,000 crore; FY29 INR 24,000-25,000 crore. PAT guidance INR 1,100-1,200 crore FY27, INR 1,300-1,400 crore FY28, about INR 2,000 crore FY29 (consolidated).

qa_highlights.question: Is the Business Park tower purchase a cash drain, and what are the cash timelines?
qa_highlights.answer: Only the first 10% instalment is paid; the rest is construction-linked over about two years. Management said cash will go out as CapEx and cited an auction price rise from a base of INR 39,100 to about INR 66,000 on the ground floor.

qa_highlights.question: What is the CPSE REIT plan, timeline and investment needed?
qa_highlights.answer: NBCC approved an SPV in principle, subject to ministry and DIPAM approval, to hold three rentable assets totalling about 75,000 sq ft. No timeline was given; management said a national REIT will be launched only after a considerable portfolio (across CPSEs, est. INR 40,000-50,000 crore across five or six REITs) is assembled.

qa_highlights.question: Why have big awards (J&K, MAHAPREIT, Supertech) slipped, and is funding the constraint?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited government clearances, DPR approvals, seed money and about 18-20 statutory approvals. Seed money is being arranged by NBCC on some projects and by clients on others; a HUDCO MoU is in place. Management revised awards guidance to INR 20,000-25,000 crore this year from an earlier INR 30,000-32,000 crore.

534392|2026-03.headline: Vardhman Special Steels posted record FY26 profit of about INR122 crore on 225,000 tons volume; EBITDA/ton guidance raised to INR8,000-11,000.
534392|2026-03.overview: Management described FY26 as a record year, with profit of about INR122 crore and sales volume of 225,000 tons, in line with budget. The Iran-US conflict pushed raw material prices up in Q4 and raised gas costs, but gas supply was not disrupted. Management raised FY27 EBITDA/ton guidance to INR8,000-11,000 from INR7,000-10,000 and set a 2-year target of INR9,000-12,000. The call centred on a reheating furnace commissioned in March, a solar plant, a new 210x210 section, a forging project, and a planned greenfield steel plant with capex of about INR2,000 crore.

segments.name: Automotive special steels (existing plant)
segments.commentary: FY26 volume 225,000 tons; FY27 sales target about 250,000-255,000 tons, with 250,000 tons to be used for modelling. Rolling capacity about 180,000 tons was supplemented by outsourced rolling; rolling capacity rises to 270,000 tons after the reheating furnace.

segments.name: Forging (ring gears, Aichi technology)
segments.commentary: Project budget INR475 crore, now expected to come in below that; about INR80 crore spent so far. First line targeted for Jan-Mar 2028 start, with ramp-up in FY29; plans for at least 3 lines.

segments.name: Greenfield steel plant
segments.commentary: Capacity 500,000-600,000 tons; commissioning targeted July 2029; land acquisition expected to close in May 2026. Ramp-up budgeted at 5-6 years to full utilisation.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA/ton guidance INR8,000-11,000; INR9,000-12,000 targeted in about 2 years, with management saying this could be a more confident range.
FY27 rolled volume target about 250,000-255,000 tons; for modelling, management asked analysts to use 250,000 tons, with a static 270,000-275,000 tons thereafter for the existing plant.

Melt shop currently under 300,000 tons licence; expansion to about 360,000 tons needs environmental clearance (50-50 chance, decision expected before March 2027); if approved, commissioning late CY27.
Price increases sought from Q1 FY27 to pass through higher scrap costs; discussions ongoing.
Government incentives expected at about INR12-13 crore in FY27, as the GST refund scheme ends Aug 2026 and electricity duty exemption runs to Aug 2029.
Equity infusion of about INR1,200 crore (INR385 crore already in, about INR800 crore to come), plus about INR1,200 crore debt; peak debt/equity below 0.75, comfort at 0.5.
capex_capacity: Reheating furnace commissioned March 2026, lifting rolling capacity to 270,000 tons; 9 crore units/year solar plant commissioned in Q4; new 210x210 section added to improve cast productivity and reduce rework.
Heat size raised from 37 tons to 40 tons; new NDT line and new peeling line in progress; Kocks Block commissioned.
Melt shop: plan to raise melting from 300,000 to about 360,000 tons, subject to environmental approval; equipment lead time 1-1.5 years.

Capex FY27 about INR100 crore (mostly land and development for the new plant, plus normal/replacement capex); FY27-28 expansion capex about INR700-800 crore, plus about INR100 crore for the existing plant and INR80-100 crore more if environmental approval comes.

Committed investment about INR2,600 crore through FY30: about INR2,000 crore for the steel plant and INR475 crore for forging; further specialised-alloy investments (ESR, VAR, VIM) still to be planned.
demand_pricing: Pricing works on spreads, not commodity prices; alloy steel prices rise less than commodity steel when scrap rises and fall less when scrap falls. Management said average selling price fell in FY26 versus FY25 despite higher volume.
Exports to be mainly indirect, via components from India to global OEs and EU FTA/CBAM benefits; direct export share to stay low. Luxury OEs such as BMW and Mercedes-Benz may give better prices.
Forging customer validation: Maruti Suzuki wants to see the factory running before validation; Aichi-linked approvals may be faster.
Management sees tool and die steel imports of about INR1,000 crore/year as an opportunity for future ingot-casting products.
Product mix expected to stay similar for the foreseeable future; a dip is likely when the new plant ramps up.

qa_highlights.question: What volume should be modelled for rolled products and is 250,000 tons sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said keep 250,000 tons for FY27 (target 255,000), with 270,000-275,000 tons from the following year and static at that level for existing plant modelling.

qa_highlights.question: Will EBITDA/ton be in the 8,500-11,000 range?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed guidance of INR8,000-11,000 for this year, moving to INR9,000-12,000 in about 2 years; FY26 averaged above INR8,500.

qa_highlights.question: What is the breakup of FY26 capex and how much will the forging project cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Kocks Block, reheating furnace, warehouses and land were the main items. Forging budget INR475 crore, spend so far about INR80 crore; expected to finish below budget, with more precise figures in about 6 months.

qa_highlights.question: What are the expected FY27/FY28 capex and funding plans?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex about INR100 crore; FY27-28 about INR700-800 crore for expansion. Debt/equity to stay below 0.75; about INR1,200 crore equity (INR385 crore in, Vardhman Group INR300-400 crore, Aichi, possible QIP) and about INR1,200 crore debt.

qa_highlights.question: What are government incentives and will the new plant get PLI?
qa_highlights.answer: No PLI for the new plant; it will be under the Punjab scheme. Incentives about INR12-13 crore in FY27 versus INR24 crore in FY26, as the GST refund ends Aug 2026.

qa_highlights.question: What ROCE is expected after the new plants?
qa_highlights.answer: Management hopes EBITDA on capital employed stays above 20% once plants reach full utilisation; below 20% it would not make sense to keep investing.

qa_highlights.question: What components will the forging plant make and what is its capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Ring gears for cars, using an Aichi process; one line initially versus Aichi's 9 lines. Management declined to give asset-level detail.

risks_watch: Environmental approval for the melt shop expansion to 360,000 tons is uncertain (management puts it at 50-50); Ludhiana is in a critically polluted zone.
Forging ramp-up depends on customer validation; Maruti Suzuki will validate only after seeing the factory operating; FY29 is the first year of meaningful forging volume.
Greenfield plant timeline (July 2029) and 5-6 year ramp-up carry execution and cost risk; capex figures are described as rough ballpark estimates.
Raw material and gas cost volatility from the Iran-US conflict; management flagged possible global recession and high oil prices as factors affecting the EBITDA range.
Dilution and funding: about INR800 crore equity still to come, including a possible QIP, and about INR1,200 crore debt to raise.
Expiry of the GST refund incentive in Aug 2026 lowers FY27 subsidy income to about INR12-13 crore.

So we are very clear, we will remain only in the area of special steels and automotive forgings.

534392|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 12% to INR486 crore and EBITDA reached INR68 crore (INR10,760/ton), with PAT at INR41 crore.
534392|2026-06.overview: Sales volume was 59,000 tons, up 6.5% YoY, with revenue up 12% on higher volumes and OEM price revisions tied to input cost increases. EBITDA was INR68 crore (INR10,760/ton, management says excluding treasury income from Aichi surplus funds, the figure is near INR10,700/ton), and PAT was INR41 crore versus INR34 crore in Q4 FY26 and INR20 crore a year ago. Management said demand exceeds what it can supply, the 3 lakh ton licensed capacity is the binding constraint, and it has applied for an increase to 3.6 lakh tons. Forging project with Aichi Steel is tracking on schedule with capex now below the INR475 crore estimate, and the greenfield 5 lakh ton plant scope and cost are being revised upward.

financial_highlights.value: INR10,760/ton (INR10,700 excluding treasury income from Aichi surplus funds)

financial_highlights.change: vs INR34 crore in Q4 FY26 and INR20 crore in Q1 FY26

segments.name: Automotive steel (core)
segments.commentary: Volumes were good and prices were revised upward on cost pass-through; Q1 settlement is complete with some OEMs and pending with others, where the price is expected to rise further. Maruti is about 10% of business.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Direct exports are about 6-7% of sales and indirect exports via the Aichi trading arm about 5%; management guides total exports to 7-8% (max about 10%), with Aichi roughly 40-50% of exports.

segments.name: Non-automotive / die steel (planned)
segments.commentary: Ingot casting is due in Q3 FY27 and to stabilise in Q4; die steel production is expected to be regular in FY28. Die steel imports into India are about INR1,000 crore a year, and die steel sells at about INR2.5 lakh/ton (non-ESR) versus average realisation of about INR85,000/ton.

guidance_outlook: FY27 volume target about 255,000 tons; FY28 target above 270,000 tons, rising to about 290,000 tons if the environmental approval for 3.6 lakh tons comes through, and 330,000-340,000 tons in FY28-29 with new capex.
EBITDA/ton range is INR8,000-11,000 currently; management intends to move to INR8,000-12,000 for next year and to INR9,000-12,000 after the new solar plant and value-added products ramp up (FY28-29).
Q2 FY27 realisations are expected to be higher than Q1 after a 1 July price increase request; Q3 is expected broadly flat to slightly up or down depending on raw material prices.
Rolling mill has reached 3 lakh tons input capacity and is expected to reach 330,000 tons of input, about 10% higher, within the current licence constraint.
Forging project with Aichi Steel: commissioning by Q4 FY28, with 6-12 months to fill; revenue from around end FY29 to FY30; capex below INR475 crore estimate (more than 10% saving).

New greenfield steel plant (about 5 lakh tons, to be enlarged): commissioning on track for FY29-30; land and machinery to be finalised by mid-September 2026; cost likely a little higher than earlier per ton due to metals inflation and rupee depreciation.
capex_capacity: Existing licensed capacity is 3 lakh tons; application for 3.6 lakh tons (360,000 tons melting) is pending with the Environment Ministry, with approval expected in about 3-4 months but not assured.
New reheating furnace has stabilised; new NDT (testing) line and new peeling line to be commissioned September-October 2026 to remove bottlenecks and reduce job work.
Solar: about 50% capacity addition planned in roughly 1-1.5 years; savings will be lower than phase one because local cell manufacturing rules raise panel cost.

Greenfield plant being reconfigured (scrap preheating, extra continuous testing and automatic testing lines), so capacity and cost will rise; a refined project is due at the next Board meeting, with details in next quarter.
Funding: internal cash is in hand; a capital raise is planned in FY28 with commitments from Vardhman Group and Aichi; Punjab government support is assured.
demand_pricing: Demand is strong and the company is turning away orders; there are no long-term orders, all business is repeat, and customer volumes drive supply.
Next volume lift comes from commercial production for import substitution for Maruti, expected from Q4 FY27.
Tie-ups with Aichi and Toyota Kirloskar (TKM) support approvals; TKM's new Aurangabad plant needs green steel, where the company claims to be the only Indian player with the approvals.
Price revisions follow raw material cost changes; OEMs can reverse or move prices, and the company operates within a band.
Non-auto product mix is a planned margin lever; die steel is high-price, low-volume and carries higher heat-treatment cost.

qa_highlights.question: How much of revenue is from exports, and how is business concentrated by customer?
qa_highlights.answer: Direct exports are about 6-7% and indirect exports via Aichi's trading arm about 5%; Maruti is about 10% of sales, and management says there is no concentration risk.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the 3 lakh to 3.6 lakh ton expansion and the 5 lakh ton greenfield plant?
qa_highlights.answer: The EC application is filed and approval is expected in 3-4 months; the greenfield land and machinery are to be finalised by August end to mid-September, and the plant will be larger than 5 lakh tons with cost likely a little higher.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the EBITDA/ton range rising from INR8,000-11,000 to INR8,000-12,000?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cites higher volumes spreading fixed costs, lower operating costs, reduced job work from Q3 FY27, and the new solar plant; the range floor is to move to 9,000 after the solar addition.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 volume target and what drives growth beyond the licence limit?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 target is about 255,000 tons, FY28 above 270,000 tons; growth beyond that needs the EC approval and new capex, and non-auto products (ingot casting, die steel, railway axles, windmill shafts) are the next growth levers.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Aichi forging project cost and timeline on track?
qa_highlights.answer: The project is on schedule for commissioning by Q4 FY28, cost is more than 10% below the INR475 crore estimate, and revenue begins around end FY29 with a 6-12 month fill-up period.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a partner for the advanced metals / aerospace JV?
qa_highlights.answer: No partner is selected; management is talking to several parties, the JV will be a separate company that is not Aichi, and it is expected to take a couple of years, so the numbers are outside the forecast horizon.

qa_highlights.question: What is the order book and realisation outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: The company has no formal order book and says it is fully booked; Q2 realisations are expected to be higher than Q1 after a 1 July price increase, while Q3 is expected broadly flat.

risks_watch: Licence cap at 3 lakh tons constrains volume; the 3.6 lakh ton EC approval is pending and not assured.
Pending OEM price settlements for Q1 and Q2 realisations depend on OEM acceptance and raw material costs.
Greenfield project cost is rising (metals inflation, rupee depreciation, added testing lines), and the refined project and cost are due in the next Board meeting and next quarter.
Solar savings in the next phase will be lower because of local cell rules, which affects the planned EBITDA/ton uplift.
The reported EBITDA of INR68 crore includes treasury income from surplus Aichi funds; management excluded it to get INR10,700/ton, so the operating figure should be tracked separately.
Direct export share was over-estimated earlier; the company will start estimating indirect component exports from next quarter.

534392|2026-09.headline: Vardhman Special Steels Q2 FY27 PAT rose about 50% YoY on sales up 27%, with EBITDA per ton at the top of the INR9,000–12,000 guided range.

Strong automotive demand and tight supply after unscheduled shutdowns at a large competitor drove price increases over the last two quarters, and management said EBITDA per ton is currently at the high end of its range, partly due to inventory gains it called non-sustainable. The greenfield steel plant (INR2,000 crore cost, now expected to be higher), the forging plant and the brownfield expansion from 300,000 to 360,000 tons remain in progress, with the environmental approval still pending. Management also flagged a possible shift to 1:1 debt-equity, a rights issue in 2H CY27, and a possible dividend suspension for 3–4 years, to be decided at the April board meeting.

534425|2026-03.headline: Speciality Restaurants Q4 FY26 revenue up 13.65% YoY and PAT up 44.20%, with SSG of 2.25% for the quarter and 11.57% in April.
534425|2026-03.overview: Management reported Q4 FY26 revenue growth of 13.65% YoY and PAT growth of 44.20%, helped by 2.25% same-store sales growth and gross margin expansion from 69.1% to 70.4%. Full-year SSG was 1.49%, and April SSG reached 11.57%, which management attributed to higher dine-in covers and refurbishments of older restaurants. Management guided to about 15% top-line growth in FY27 and about 15-16% EBITDA growth on revenue, with 32 new outlets planned. On the cost side, the company took a 4% price increase and moved 78% of its kitchens off LPG/PNG to induction, targeting 100% within 20 days.

qa_highlights.question: What is the restaurant-level economics for top brands?
qa_highlights.answer: For a 2,500-3,000 sq ft store, revenue is INR 8-9 crores a year with 22% restaurant EBITDA before rent. Rent is about 20-21% of revenue (revenue-share triggers at 17-18%), leaving about 15% post-rent EBITDA. Breakeven takes 4-6 months.

qa_highlights.question: How is the company managing LPG and fuel supply, and what does induction cost?
qa_highlights.answer: The company started the transition on 4 March and imported wok-based induction sets (around 300). It has 78% of the chain off fuel, targeting 100% in 20 days. Management said induction cost is the same or lower, with a 6% saving in a pilot restaurant from avoiding pilot-flame wastage.

qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed seven focus brands (Mainland China, Asia Kitchen, Haka, Gong, Siciliana, Walters, Sweet Bengal). Other brands are profitable and will not be shut, but no further expansion is planned.

qa_highlights.question: Is a buyback under consideration, given the cash pile and the share price correction?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said the question would be taken up by the Board and it was too early to say.

qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said the 15-16% figure is at restaurant level after rent. Cash-flow EBITDA is after corporate costs, which fell to about 4% of revenue from 6-7% as the company resumed expansion.

534425|2026-09.headline: Speciality Restaurants Q2 FY27 standalone revenue rose 18.24% YoY to INR 129.78 crore, with operational EBITDA up 39.44% to INR 10.24 crore.
534425|2026-09.overview: Standalone revenue from operations grew 18.24% YoY to INR 129.78 crore and PAT rose 45.75% to INR 6.94 crore. Operational EBITDA margin expanded to 8.03% from 6.81%, and same-store sales growth was 8.1% in Q2 (11.32% in Q1; 9.8% in H1). Delivery mix rose to 32% from 27.4% a year earlier, and the network stood at 125 outlets at September 30, 2026. Management flagged a pipeline of 2-3 openings in Q3 and a 200-outlet target by FY2030, with restaurant-level EBITDA of 22-23% post Ind AS as the internal benchmark.

Restaurant-level EBITDA target of 22-23% post Ind AS for new restaurants.
Revenue growth expected at about 20-22% a year from new openings and existing stores.

capex_capacity: H2 FY27 openings planned across Mumbai, Delhi, Pune, Bangalore, Kolkata and Dubai, alongside renovations and brand conversions at select existing sites.
Gong re-entry into Delhi this quarter; expansion focus shifts to Delhi, Hyderabad and Bangalore alongside existing core markets of West Bengal, Mumbai, Bangalore and Pune.
Capex of about INR 50 crore a year; management said per-restaurant spend is INR 4-5 crore.

Conversions of Mainland China to Asia Kitchen reportedly grew sales 25-30%; management targets same-store growth of 10-15% for Oriental brands.
Q3 is seasonally the strongest quarter; seasonal and marketing plans are in place.

qa_highlights.answer: Management is optimistic on Q3 with 2-3 new restaurants launching, including 2 Gong, 3 Walters and 1 Siciliana.

qa_highlights.question: Long-term delivery mix and how the company will grow customer reach?
qa_highlights.answer: Delivery is about 29-30% of business and is expected to reach 30-35%; growth will come through kitchen-within-kitchen formats and aggregator campaigns.

qa_highlights.question: How are raw material inflation and margins managed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has not taken a large price hike and has relied on vendor renegotiation and scale-based buying power.

qa_highlights.question: Plans for the 200-outlet target by FY2030 and per-outlet economics?
qa_highlights.answer: Expansion is mainly physical outlets across the Oriental, Siciliana and QSR brands; target restaurant EBITDA is 22-23% post Ind AS and revenue growth of 20-22%.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of rising delivery mix on margins (QSR lens)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said dine-in growth should offset delivery cost pressure, so net margins should improve; 70% of business is dine-in based.

qa_highlights.answer: Per-restaurant capex is INR 4-5 crore, roughly INR 50 crore a year; management expects the business to turn cash flow positive in future years.

This is a complete trend because we've seen a complete shift of diner habits to more of a hybrid model where dine-in is something that people feel is achievable may be probably once a week or twice in a month.

The best plan that has worked magically for us is kitchen within kitchen concepts, where, for example, if we have an Asian kitchen, we also do deliver our other Asian brands from the very same kitchen without having any extra capex or staff costs or any other costs added to it.

534600|2026-03.headline: JTL Industries Q4 FY26 revenue rose 47.5% YoY to INR693 crore on a record 1,23,262 MT quarterly volume; FY27 guided to about 30% volume growth.
534600|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was INR693 crore (up 47.5% YoY, 47.2% QoQ), with EBITDA of INR58 crore and PAT of INR38 crore, and the company reported record quarterly and annual volumes. Management attributed the volume jump mainly to higher utilisation at the Mangaon facility and DFT structural steel pipes, with no channel-inventory gain. FY26 totals were revenue INR2,136 crore, EBITDA INR166 crore, PAT INR103 crore and volume 3,95,900 MT. Management guided to about 30% FY27 volume growth, while the 2 million tonne capacity target by FY27 was reiterated but the Aryan Bhatia question flagged that the earlier 6 lakh tonne FY27 guidance has effectively been reduced after capex delays.

financial_highlights.change: Management says Q4 EBITDA/ton ~INR4,700 per analyst question; about INR150 higher QoQ

segments.name: DFT structural steel pipes
segments.commentary: Main growth driver in Q4 and exports; being empanelled with customers, and ACRS certification obtained for Australia, with US and Canada being explored.

EBITDA per ton growth of 10-15% in FY27, taking it from INR3,900 to about INR4,500-4,800; longer-term aspiration of INR5,000/ton.

JTL Defence: 10-15% EBITDA margin targeted in coming quarters; defence capacity of 700-800 MT/month by FY29.
capex_capacity: Mangaon cold rolling complex (color-coated pipes, GT pipes) with 7 lakh tonne outlay; nearing completion, full running by end of H1 FY27.

All further capacity addition is at Maharashtra; no other facility additions planned.

Capacity delays attributed to rains and complexity of the color-coated capex; the outlook timeline has slipped as a result.

534618|2026-09.headline: Waaree RTL Q2 FY27 revenue rose 36.53% YoY to INR1,057.84 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 15.12% as solar EPC execution dropped to 456 MWp.
