534748|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 19.45% QoQ to INR 287.70 crore and EBITDA margin to 17.41%, with net profit at INR 12.37 crore.
534748|2026-03.overview: Total income for Q4 FY26 was INR 287.70 crore, up 19.45% QoQ from INR 240.86 crore. EBITDA rose 118.12% QoQ to INR 50.10 crore, with margin up 788 bps to 17.41%. Net profit was INR 12.37 crore versus INR 2.28 crore in Q3, with a 4.30% net margin. For FY26, total income was INR 1,066.42 crore, EBITDA INR 138.03 crore and net profit INR 26.99 crore. Management said it redeemed INR 43.19 crore of NCDs in one tranche and cut debt by nearly INR 68 crore over the last two quarters.

segments.name: TMT rebar / long products (Simhadri brand)
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 rebar volume was 49,760 tonnes, up from about 39,000 t in Q3. Management said the average EBITDA per tonne was about INR 9,000-9,500 in the last quarter versus about INR 6,000 in earlier quarters, and about INR 6,800-7,000 on a yearly average.

segments.name: Power
segments.commentary: Power segment revenue fell in FY26. Management attributed this to kiln refurbishments; it expects data-centre tie-ups and capacity expansion to improve consumption.

segments.name: Logistics (SEIL Logistics and Infra Company)
segments.commentary: A subsidiary formed to run a private freight terminal and logistics at Visakhapatnam, with railway sidings. MoUs with the Andhra Pradesh government cover about 150 acres adjacent to the existing land.

guidance_outlook: Management said Q4 FY26 is 'fine' but later years should be better; it expects steady margins while the market stays buoyant.
Management expects FY27 volumes to roughly double once the reheating furnace and capacity expansion come on stream from Q2 FY27, with capacity mostly doubled.
Sustainable EBITDA guidance given as about INR 7,000 per tonne on average volumes of 40,000-50,000 tonnes per quarter.

Finance cost is expected at about INR 12-13 crore per quarter, not below 10, after the new loan costs and trade finance charges fall away. Refinancing is targeted to bring the cost of debt to about 9%.

Existing capex (reheating furnace, furnace refurbishment, kiln work) is to be completed in FY27. New greenfield capex for the 1 million tonne green steel plant is about one year away, pending groundbreaking and the strategic investor's inputs.
Pledged shares are expected to be released once refinancing is complete and IMR funds are received.
capex_capacity: A reheating furnace is being installed, expected to start from Q2 FY27 and to add about 50,000 tonnes of new bar capacity. Management said it will raise rolling mill efficiency by 30-40%.
Billet and rebar capacities were raised by about 44-45% at the end of FY25. Utilisation is about 46-47% for rebar and 55-56% for billet, with a target of 70-75% in FY27.
Expansions already under way are expected to be operational by end-July 2026.
Land bank: about 400-450 acres existing; another 150 acres targeted for the logistics park and 150 acres for steel manufacturing. MoUs cover a 1 million tonne green steel plant.
Planned capex and debt paydown are to be funded from INR 300 crore of share warrant money from IMR Group and internal accruals.
demand_pricing: Management said the Indian steel outlook is strong, citing infrastructure, housing, railways, defence and import substitution. It also said Andhra Pradesh and Visakhapatnam projects (Google AI hub, ArcelorMittal, Amaravati) are sources of demand, and that the company is an approved vendor for them.
April 2026 sales were described as 'great' and May as slightly weaker due to heatwave and the war situation. Management expects a June recovery.
Management said the company is largely insulated from the ongoing war, except for some diesel cost in transport. Coal, iron ore and scrap are sourced locally.
The company was re-empanelled under MES for TMT bar supplies to the Ministry of Defence.

qa_highlights.question: What does the company plan to fund its capacity growth and reduce its debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company has MoUs with state governments for expansion and a 1 million tonne green steel plant. Project reports are pending, and the plan is to announce them once formalised.

qa_highlights.question: When is the balance payment expected from IMR on the share warrants?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the INR 300 crore warrant subscription is expected within about six months and will fund growth, including green steel.

Term debt has fallen from about INR 350 crore to INR 250 crore, and current debt is about INR 270 crore.

qa_highlights.answer: Q4 FY26 rebar sales were 49,760 tonnes. Management said FY27 capacity is expected to roughly double from Q2 FY27.

qa_highlights.answer: Rebar utilisation is about 46-47% and billet about 55-56%. Management expects 70-75% in FY27 after the reheating furnace is commissioned.

534816|2026-03.headline: Indus Towers Q4 FY26: reported EBITDA INR 44.6bn (+1.6% YoY, 55.1% margin) and FY26 final dividend of INR 14/share distributing full-year FCF of INR 37.6bn.
534816|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 total revenue was INR 81bn (+4.8% YoY) and core rental revenue INR 53.1bn (+5.4% YoY), with co-locations up 5.6% YoY. Reported EBITDA was flat-to-up YoY but down 1% QoQ, held back by a Q4 one-time settlement hit to revenue, a Q3 positive one-off in other expenses, and higher seasonal maintenance spend. Full-year PAT fell 28.1% YoY to INR 71.4bn because FY25 carried a INR 51bn receivables write-back; normalised EBITDA and PAT grew 11.4% and 13%. The Board recommended a final dividend of INR 14/share, distributing the full FY26 free cash flow, with management guiding to a steady and progressive payout going forward.

financial_highlights.value: INR 11.1bn in Q4; INR 37.6bn in FY26

segments.name: Towers and co-locations (India)
segments.commentary: Q4 added 4,892 macro towers and 6,192 co-locations, taking the base to about 264,500 towers and 428,000 co-locations (+6.1% and +5.6% YoY). Tenancy ratio stable at 1.62; leaner-tower co-locations exceed 14,000, portfolio about 442,000 including leaner towers.

segments.name: Energy
segments.commentary: Energy revenue fell QoQ on cost optimisation and seasonal energy cost decline; energy margin -3.6% in Q4 vs -5.2% a year earlier. Solar access added at about 2,500 sites in Q4, taking the total to about 42,400; diesel consumption down about 7% YoY.

segments.name: Africa
segments.commentary: Operating licence secured in Zambia with on-ground execution starting; Uganda and Nigeria in final regulatory stages. Commercial frameworks and initial orders in place with the anchor customer; capex for Africa described as not significant initially.

segments.name: Non-tower / DAS / IBS
segments.commentary: Company says it reached leadership in IBS in Q4; DAS deployments picked up in metros, tunnels and highways. No figures disclosed.

guidance_outlook: Final dividend of INR 14/share recommended; management says the endeavour is steady and progressive distribution, with no minimum payout formula (dividend policy: FCF distributed at year-end, subject to working capital).
Management does not give forward numbers; says order book is healthy for the next few quarters with growth-oriented capex (about 70% of capex is growth, about 25% replacement/maintenance).
Full-year EBITDA margin said to be in line with the 55%-plus expectation.
Africa tower deployment expected to begin soon in Zambia, with ramp-up as approvals come through in Uganda and Nigeria.

Management said a major customer's contract expiries affect only a very small portion of the portfolio; some Jio tenancies have expired but are still operating, with minor churn.

rows.why: FY27 capex is already guided at INR170-180 crore versus FY26 INR159 crore, but this is a budget rather than a new capacity announcement, and utilisation was not disclosed.

rows.why: Management planned a 1-1.5% LFL price increase on similar products and expects ASP gains mainly from mix, after Q4 apparel ASP rose 5% YoY, though it passes on only a controlled share of the 5-7% apparel cost increase.

534976|2026-06.headline: V-Mart Q1 FY27 revenue rose 23% YoY with 9% like-for-like growth, while PAT grew 41% to INR 47 crore.
534976|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 23% YoY with same-store sales up 9% (V-Mart 8%, Unlimited 13%), marking the 11th consecutive quarter of positive LFL growth. Pre-Ind AS EBITDA rose 36% to INR 83 crore (margin 7.6%) and PAT rose 41% to INR 47 crore. Gross margin fell 80 bps to 34.5% on mix change and aged-inventory provisioning, partly offset by 150 bps of operating leverage as expenses rose 15%. Management flagged raw material inflation of around 10%, rising minimum wages, and a weaker Q2 due to Durga Puja shifting into Q3.

financial_highlights.value: Down 39% YoY and 7% QoQ on 18% higher NMV

segments.name: V-Mart (core)
segments.commentary: SSG 8% in the quarter; apparel ASP up 2%; memo count up 18% YoY; footfalls up 39%.

segments.name: Unlimited (South India)
segments.commentary: Revenue up 33%, EBITDA up 40%; sales per sq ft INR 710, up 18% YoY; SSG 13%. Newer stores are outperforming acquired legacy stores on SPSF.

segments.name: LimeRoad (marketplace)
segments.commentary: Losses down 39% YoY and 7% QoQ despite 18% higher NMV; first quarter in eight with NMV growth and falling EBITDA loss.

guidance_outlook: Store expansion guidance for FY27 unchanged at 90+ gross openings; management expects 8-10 closures this year.
Management targets mid-to-high single-digit SSG for the year, per Q&A.
Price increase range of 3-5% ASP targeted; about 2-2.5% overall price increase expected from inflation, with mix change also contributing.
Management expects 0.5-0.75% of margin compromise to absorb raw material inflation; margin loss to stay below 1%.
Q2 FY27 expected to see negative impact on sales and margins from Durga Puja shifting into Q3 (19-day shift); recovery expected in Q3 festive season.
Expects Unlimited and V-Mart store-level EBITDA margins to converge over time; more Southern store openings than last year.
Employee cost to be held flat as a percentage of sales despite minimum wage hikes.
capex_capacity: Q1 capex INR 38 crore, mainly new store additions and selective refurbishments.
Added 15 stores and closed 1 in Q1; network at 591 stores across 335 cities, total 51 lakh sq ft.
FY27 expansion guidance 90+ stores, with more Unlimited openings in South India than last year.
Operating cash flow of INR 76 crore in the quarter; balance sheet debt-free with zero long-term debt and bank limit utilisation near nil.
demand_pricing: Footfalls up 39% and memo count up 18% YoY; conversion fell from mid-40s to 38-39%, attributed to heavier competition and some past counting errors.
Apparel ASP up 2% YoY, driven by product-line mix (sets and combos) rather than inflation.
Days of inventory down 8% YoY to 86 days; inventory per store down 5% to around INR 1.5 crore.
Raw material costs up around 10%, linked to crude, cotton, and yarn; partial pass-through to customers so far, with caution on demand elasticity.
Monsoon rainfall about 30% deficient as of call date, with partial recovery in late July; watchful on rural demand.
Karnataka minimum wage hike on stay; vendor exposure to Karnataka below 5% per management.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 80 bps gross margin decline and how is the split between mix change and provisioning?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the split is not equal and varies over time. Mix change reflects customer preference, not deliberate changes. Provisioning follows a 10-15 year old policy applied every quarter. Benefits should come as aged inventory is liquidated.

qa_highlights.question: Why has conversion dropped from mid-40s to 38-39%?
qa_highlights.answer: Partly past counting errors and partly greater competition, with customers shopping across stores and returning later. Memo count still grew 18%.

qa_highlights.question: How will raw material inflation be passed on?
qa_highlights.answer: Around 10% RM inflation; some passed on, some offset through vendor efficiencies and yarn mix changes. Margin compromise limited to 0.5-0.75%. Price increase target 3-5% ASP including mix.

qa_highlights.question: How much minimum wage impact is in Q1 and what remains?
qa_highlights.answer: Two of three months of the wage hike are already in Q1 wage bill. Further increases are coming. Karnataka is on stay, with no provision made.

qa_highlights.question: What is the SSG expectation for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Mid-to-high single digit SSG, aiming to beat last year's SSG.

qa_highlights.question: What SSG is needed for operating leverage to continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 3-4% SSG offsets inflation, since about 95-98% of costs are fixed except marketing.

qa_highlights.question: Will Unlimited store additions accelerate and will margins converge?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, more Southern openings than last year. Gross margin in Unlimited is structurally higher; EBITDA margin gap narrowing as legacy stores improve, with similar margins expected over time.

risks_watch: Raw material inflation (crude-linked yarn, cotton, dyes) and supply-chain stability for festive season deliveries.
Gross margin pressure from provisioning and mix; management expects benefits only in later quarters.
Conversion trend below mid-40s amid rising competition.
Minimum wage hikes in UP and Karnataka; Karnataka impact not yet provided for.
Monsoon deficiency affecting rural demand; Q2 weaker on Durga Puja timing shift.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Gross margin fell 80 bps to 34.5% and management guides a 0.5-0.75% margin compromise to absorb ~10% raw material inflation, but 150 bps operating leverage and 3-4% SSG covering inflation (95-98% of costs fixed) could lift EBITDA margin from 7.6% once aged-inventory provisioning eases.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: 90+ gross store openings for FY27 guidance held unchanged, with 15 stores added and 1 closed in Q1 (network 591 stores) and Q1 capex of INR 38 crore.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q1 SSG was 9% (V-Mart 8%, Unlimited 13%) with memo count up 18% and footfalls up 39%, and management targets mid-to-high single-digit SSG for FY27, though conversion fell to 38-39% from mid-40s and Q2 is hit by Durga Puja shift.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No utilisation figure disclosed and the company is debt-free with near-nil bank limit use, while capex is already committed to the store roll-out of 90+ stores, so a separate capex announcement is not signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management is cautious on raw material inflation (~10%), monsoon ~30% deficient and a weaker Q2 from the 19-day Durga Puja shift, with store guidance merely held rather than raised.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new product, brand or model launches were discussed; the only product commentary is the sets and combos mix driving ASP up 2%.

rows.label: 3-5% ASP price increase target
rows.why: Management is targeting a 3-5% ASP increase, with 2-2.5% overall price rise expected from inflation, against ~10% raw material inflation and only 2% ASP growth in Q1.

rows.label: More Southern Unlimited openings and margin convergence
rows.why: Management guided more Unlimited openings in South India than last year, with Unlimited revenue +33%, EBITDA +40% and SPSF INR 710 (+18%), and expects Unlimited and V-Mart store EBITDA margins to converge.

rows.label: LimeRoad losses narrowing
rows.why: LimeRoad losses fell 39% YoY and 7% QoQ on 18% higher NMV, the first quarter in eight with both NMV growth and a falling EBITDA loss.

tone.note: Management was confident on top-line growth, Unlimited and LimeRoad losses and the debt-free balance sheet, but cautious on raw material inflation, monsoon deficiency, minimum wages and conversion falling to 38-39%.
